docs.title: Flow (go-flow) Documentation Hub
docs.text:
Slashing ETL Madness with Go, HTMX, and Declarative Pipelines Current Version: 1.1.24 | Runtime: Single-Binary Go (flow.exe / flow) | Visual Studio: flow -builder

Flow (go-flow) is an enterprise-grade, single-binary ETL and workflow orchestration engine written in Go. It combines declarative, Git-friendly XML pipeline definitions with an embedded HTMX visual web builder (-builder), multi-engine relational and Key-Value database connectors, $O(1)$-memory bulk streaming replication, in-process Go scripting (via Yaegi), cross-platform AES-256-GCM encryption, and multi-standard digital signatures.

Flow Ecosystem (FLOW_ECOSYSTEM.md) | Is an overview of how flow core package, CLI, web builder, and API ecosystem components interact with each other.

docs.title: 1. Executive Overview & Why Flow?
docs.text:
Traditional enterprise data orchestration forces teams to choose between heavyweight distributed clusters (Apache Airflow, Dagster, Prefect) that require dedicated Kubernetes/Celery infrastructure, or legacy proprietary GUI monoliths (SSIS, Informatica) that produce opaque, un-diffable binary files.

Flow eliminates both extremes by compiling the entire orchestration runtime, database drivers, scripting interpreter, cryptographic verifier, and visual web studio into a single zero-dependency binary.

Capability Traditional Python / Cluster (Airflow, Prefect) Legacy Enterprise GUI (SSIS, Informatica) Flow (go-flow) Deployment Footprint Multi-container cluster, Redis/Celery, Python venvs Heavy Windows server licenses & proprietary agents Single static binary (~30 MB), zero runtime dependencies Authoring Experience Imperative Python code only Desktop-only drag-and-drop Bidirectional: Embedded Web UI (-builder) + Git-friendly XML High-Volume Bulk ETL Memory-heavy DataFrames (pandas) Fast, but locked to specific vendor ecosystems $O(1)$ constant-memory streaming (<sql_bulk>, <kv_bulk>) In-Process Scripting Native Python (dependency conflicts common) C# / VB (requires compilation/GAC) Embedded Go (Yaegi) + PowerShell, Bash, Cmd, Zsh, CSX Cryptographic Security External vaults / custom plugins OS-bound DPAPI encryption Cross-platform AES-256-GCM + OpenSSL/PKCS#7/OpenPGP signatures Audit & Observability Requires external Postgres + log forwarders Proprietary logging tables Plug-and-play log_db sink, JSONL, & real-time stream events

docs.title: 2. Architecture & Execution Lifecycle
docs.text:
Every pipeline run follows a deterministic, security-first execution pipeline: Verify $\rightarrow$ Decrypt $\rightarrow$ Resolve Configuration Hierarchy $\rightarrow$ Validate Schema/AST $\rightarrow$ Execute Preflight $\rightarrow$ Execute Flow $\rightarrow$ Emit Audit Telemetry.

flowchart TD
    subgraph Sources["1. Uniform Resource Loader"]
        S1["Local Filesystem<br/>(scripts.xml / UTF-8 / UTF-16)"]
        S2["HTTP / HTTPS Endpoints<br/>(https://...)"]
        S3["Database Repositories<br/>(sql:// or db:// DSN Query)"]
    end

    subgraph Security["2. Decoupled Cryptographic Gate"]
        V["Digital Signature Verification<br/>(OpenSSL X.509 / PKCS#7 .p7s / OpenPGP .asc / FLOWSIGNED:v1)"]
        D["AES-256-GCM Decryption<br/>(PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 / FLOWENC:v1)"]
    end

    subgraph Config["3. Configuration & Validation"]
        H["Hierarchy Merge<br/>Base (--file) < Options (--options) < Config (--config) < CLI (--vars)"]
        X["XSD & Semantic AST Validation<br/>(--validate / pipeline.xsd)"]
    end

    subgraph Runtime["4. Execution Engine"]
        PRE["Preflight Quality Gates<br/>(<preflight> / --preflight)"]
        FLOW["Main Workflow Execution<br/>(<flow>: Sequential, <group transaction='true'>, <parallel>, <foreach>, <while>)"]
    end

    subgraph Telemetry["5. Observability & Output"]
        OUT["Console Renderer<br/>(csv, text, json, jsonpretty, markdown, stream)"]
        LOG["Database Audit Sink (log_db)<br/>(pipeline_runs & pipeline_events)"]
        DOC["Auto-Documentation<br/>(Mermaid.js Flowchart + XSLT 3.0)"]
    end

    S1 & S2 & S3 --> V
    V --> D
    D --> H
    H --> X
    X --> PRE
    PRE --> FLOW
    FLOW --> OUT & LOG & DOC

docs.title: 3.2 CLI, Configuration Hierarchy & Remote Sources
docs.text: Document Description Complete CLI Reference (flow, crypto_tool, db_importer) Exhaustive flag reference, secret precedence rules, exit codes, and enterprise recipes across all three binaries. Summary of Available Pipeline XML Options Complete XML element and attribute specification for <pipeline>, <databases>, <variables>, <preflight>, and <flow>. Configuration & Execution Hierarchy How Flow merges --file, --options, --config, and --vars across Dev, Staging, and Production environments. Variables Container (<variables>) Declaring typed variable collections (string, int, float, bool, date, datetime) and recursive {{var}} expansion. Variable Element (<variable>) Detailed reference for individual <variable> definitions, type parsing, and runtime overrides. Remote File, HTTP & SQL DSN Sources Loading pipelines, options, and configs from local paths, HTTP/HTTPS (with Basic Auth), and sql:// or db:// queries. Database-Backed XML Storage Storing and executing PipelineXML, OptionsXML, and ConfigXML inside SQL Server (dbo.flow_*_content) via db_importer. UTF-8 & UTF-16 Encoding Guide Automatic BOM detection and transcoding for Windows PowerShell UTF-16LE files and SQL Server NVARCHAR(MAX) columns. Using Pipeline & Node Descriptions Best practices for self-documenting pipelines using description attributes rendered in logs and Mermaid flowcharts.

docs.title: 3.3 Security: Encryption & Digital Signatures
docs.text: Document Description Security Order of Operations & Options Deep dive into Encrypt-then-Sign vs. Sign-then-Encrypt vs. Detached Signatures, key precedence, and security flags. Single-File Cryptography (Combined Encryption & Signatures) End-to-end Windows (PowerShell/Cert Store) and Linux/macOS (OpenSSL/Bash) walkthroughs for unified .sec packages (-wrap). Cross-Platform Encryption Guide (FLOWENC:v1:) AES-256-GCM architecture, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 key derivation, memory zeroization, and at-rest database encryption. Cross-Platform Digital Signatures Guide (FLOWSIG:v1:) Pure-Go verification and signing with OpenSSL (RSA/ECDSA/Ed25519), PKCS#7/CMS (.p7s), and OpenPGP/GPG (.asc).

docs.title: 3.4 Databases, Bulk ETL, Key-Value & Transactions
docs.text: Document Description Database Connections & Pooling (<database>) Configuring relational and KV drivers, connection pool tuning (max_open_conns, max_idle_conns, workload), and dialect rules. Database Connection Strings Reference Copy-paste connection string templates for SQL Server (including Azure Entra ID fedauth), PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, SQLite, and KV stores. SQL Execution (<sql>) Executing DDL, DML, and SELECT queries with intelligent statement classification (isDMLQuery), parameter binding, and output_var. High-Speed Bulk ETL (<sql_bulk>) $O(1)$ constant-memory cross-database streaming replication, native SQL Server TDS CopyIn (tablock), and batch tuning. Comparing <sql> and <sql_bulk> Architectural comparison and decision guide for choosing between standard <sql> execution and <sql_bulk> streaming. Database Transactions & Savepoints Atomic <group transaction="true"> blocks, dialect-aware nested savepoints, parallel transaction isolation, and bulk copy caveats. Key-Value Store Operations (<kv> & <kv_bulk>) Unified NoSQL interface for bbolt, BadgerDB, Redis/Valkey, and etcd, plus SQL-to-KV bulk streaming (<kv_bulk>). DB Select, Template & Stdio Pattern End-to-end guide for querying relational data, formatting rows via <template>, and streaming to standard output.

docs.title: 3.5 Control Flow, Loops, Concurrency & Quality Gates
docs.text: Document Description Preflight Validation Gates (<preflight>) Pre-execution environment checks, connectivity verification, and schema readiness assertions before <flow> begins. Sequential & Transactional Grouping (<group>) Organizing steps into logical units with optional conditional execution (if_var/if_equals) and atomic transactions. Conditional Branching (<if>, <then>, <else>) Dynamic branching using variable equality (var/equals) or expression evaluation (condition). Dataset Iteration (<foreach> / <loop>) Row-by-row SQL cursor iteration in $O(1)$ streaming mode (stream="true") or in-memory buffered mode with automatic column binding. Conditional Loops (<while>) State-driven polling and pagination loops with WHILE_INDEX tracking and max_iterations safety guards. Concurrent Worker Pools (<parallel>) Multi-threaded execution (max_threads) with isolated variable cloning, cooperative cancellation, and collision namespacing. Declarative Assertions (<assert>) Data quality gates with halt vs. warn policies, failure flag variables (fail_var), and nested <on_failure> recovery blocks.

docs.title: 3.6 Scripting, Templates, HTTP & Data Formats
docs.text: Document Description Polyglot Scripting (<script>) In-process pure-Go Yaegi interpreter (host/vars, host/db) plus external shells (pwsh, powershell, bash, sh, cmd, zsh, csx). Text Templates (<template>) Dynamic SQL, JSON, and report generation using Go's text/template engine and helper functions. HTML Templates (<template_html>) Context-aware XSS-safe HTML email and dashboard rendering using Go's html/template engine. Comparing <template> and <template_html> Side-by-side comparison of raw text interpolation vs. automatic HTML contextual escaping. HTTP / REST Client (<http_client>) Full-featured REST integration with custom headers, TLS/mTLS tuning, proxies, cookie jars, redirects, and status capture. JSONPath Extraction (<json_path>) Extracting scalars, objects, and arrays from API responses or files using JSONPath expressions. JSONPath Syntax & Examples Guide Comprehensive tutorial on JSONPath operators, recursive descent, array slicing, and filter expressions in Flow. XPath Extraction (<xml_xpath>) Querying XML documents and SOAP payloads with XPath expressions in text, xml, or json_array output modes. YAML Path Extraction (<yaml_path>) Extracting configuration values and structured nodes from YAML files or variables. Excel Workbook Reader (<excel_read>) Reading .xlsx worksheets into structured JSON arrays for downstream iteration and transformation. Excel Workbook Writer (<excel_write>) Exporting SQL query results directly into multi-tab .xlsx spreadsheets with automatic header generation. File Reader (<file_read>) Loading local text, JSON, XML, or SQL files into pipeline variables. File Writer (<file_save>) Writing or appending pipeline variables and inline templates to disk with automatic directory creation.

docs.title: 3.7 Observability, Telemetry, Failure Handling & Debugging
docs.text: Document Description Database Logging Configuration (log_db) DDL schemas for PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle, and SQLite (pipeline_runs & pipeline_events), session auditing (spid, db_user_name), and -node-output. Failure Response & Error Propagation Fail-fast semantics, cooperative <parallel> cancellation, cursor cleanup, transaction rollbacks, and <assert> recovery paths. Comprehensive Pipeline Debugging Guide 5 production debugging patterns (variable dumps, interactive operator prompts, loop tracing, <while> state mutation, and <assert> post-mortems) in Go and C# CSX. Observability & Event Sinks Usage Guide Programmatic guide to ExecuteRun, JSONLineSink, multi-sink fanout (SetEventSinks), row count metrics, and custom OpenTelemetry bridges.

docs.title: 3.8 Developer & Extension Guides
docs.text: Document Description Executing Flow Pipelines (Execute vs ExecuteRun) Go SDK guide comparing flat []ScriptResult execution with structured RunResult observability trees. Builder Modal Tooltips & Documentation Popups Step-by-step developer guide for adding interactive markdown documentation modals and ⚡ Use Example autofill buttons to the Builder UI. Builder Theme Customization Guide Architecture of the 15 built-in UI themes (slate, vscode-dark-plus, visual-studio-light, soft-white, etc.) and how to add new themes.

docs.title: 1. Build or Run Flow
docs.text:
# Build the core engine
go build -o flow.exe .

# Build the companion cryptographic utility (optional)
go build -o crypto_tool.exe ./crypto_tool

docs.title: 2. Author a Declarative Pipeline (pipeline.xml)
docs.text:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<pipeline description="Customer Analytics Sync & Executive Report"
          xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/go-flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">

    <variables>
        <variable name="MinSpend" type="float" value="5000.00" description="Minimum customer spend filter" />
        <variable name="ReportPath" type="string" value="./reports/vip_customers.xlsx" />
    </variables>

    <databases>
        <database name="source_pg" driver="postgres"
                  connection_string="postgres://app:{{PG_PASS}}@localhost:5432/commerce?sslmode=disable" />
        <database name="warehouse_mssql" driver="sqlserver"
                  connection_string="sqlserver://sa:{{MSSQL_PASS}}@localhost:1433?database=AnalyticsDW&trustServerCertificate=true" />
        <database name="log_db" driver="sqlite"
                  connection_string="file:./telemetry_audit.db?_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)" />
    </databases>

    <preflight>
        <sql id="ping_source" db="source_pg" output_var="SourceReady">SELECT 'OK';</sql>
        <assert id="verify_source" var="SourceReady" equals="OK" message="Source PostgreSQL database is unreachable!" />
    </preflight>

    <flow>
        <!-- O(1) Memory Bulk Streaming Replication from PostgreSQL to SQL Server -->
        <sql_bulk id="stream_vip_orders"
                  db="source_pg"
                  target_db="warehouse_mssql"
                  target_table="dbo.StagingVIPOrders"
                  batch_size="10000"
                  tablock="true"
                  output_var="RowsCopied">
            SELECT order_id, customer_id, order_date, total_amount
            FROM orders
            WHERE total_amount >= {{MinSpend}};
        </sql_bulk>

        <!-- Atomic Transaction Group in Warehouse -->
        <group id="merge_warehouse_txn" transaction="true" db="warehouse_mssql">
            <sql id="upsert_vip_summary" db="warehouse_mssql">
                MERGE INTO dbo.FactVIPOrders AS target
                USING dbo.StagingVIPOrders AS src ON target.order_id = src.order_id
                WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET total_amount = src.total_amount
                WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (order_id, customer_id, order_date, total_amount)
                VALUES (src.order_id, src.customer_id, src.order_date, src.total_amount);
            </sql>
            <sql id="truncate_staging" db="warehouse_mssql">
                TRUNCATE TABLE dbo.StagingVIPOrders;
            </sql>
        </group>

        <!-- Export Summary directly to Excel Workbook -->
        <excel_write id="export_vip_excel" file="{{ReportPath}}" sheet="VIP Orders" db="warehouse_mssql">
            SELECT customer_id, COUNT(order_id) AS order_count, SUM(total_amount) AS total_spent
            FROM dbo.FactVIPOrders
            GROUP BY customer_id
            ORDER BY total_spent DESC;
        </excel_write>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: 3. Validate, Preflight, and Execute
docs.text:
# 1. Validate XML Schema and Semantic AST without executing
./flow -file pipeline.xml -xsd ./xsd/pipeline.xsd -validate

# 2. Run Preflight Checks only
./flow -file pipeline.xml -preflight

# 3. Execute Pipeline with Runtime Variable Overrides and Live Stream Output
./flow -file pipeline.xml -vars "MinSpend=10000.00" -format stream

docs.title: Core Engine Flags (flow.exe / flow)
docs.text: Flag Default Description -file <path\|uri> scripts.xml Pipeline XML path, HTTP(S) URL, or sql:// / db:// database query URI. -options <path\|uri> "" XML options profile defining default CLI flags (<flow_cli_options>). -config <path\|uri> "" Environment override XML (CONFIG.xml) for variables and databases. -vars "K=V,..." "" Runtime variable overrides (highest precedence; recursive expansion up to 3 levels). -format <fmt> csv Output renderer: csv, text, json, jsonpretty, markdown, or stream. -validate false Validates XML schema (-xsd) and AST semantics without executing nodes. -preflight false Executes <preflight> nodes only and exits. -builder false Launches the interactive HTMX visual pipeline studio web server. -builder-port <int> 0 Port for the visual builder web server (0 selects an ephemeral port). -encrypted false Decrypts AES-256-GCM input resources (auto-detected for FLOWENC:v1: payloads). -key-file <path> "" Path to symmetric key/passphrase file (recommended over -secure-key). -verify-signature false Enforces digital signature verification before decryption or execution. -public-key / -cert "" Public key (.pem) or X.509 certificate (.pem/.cer) for signature verification. -node-output false Persists redacted node outputs into pipeline_events.node_output when log_db is active. -xslt <path> / -out "" Transforms pipeline XML via XSLT 3.0 with an injected Mermaid.js diagram. -debug false Enables verbose diagnostic logging.

docs.title: Flow Builder: Visual Pipeline Designer & Runtime Orchestration
Modern, Zero-Dependency ETL & Workflow Engine in Go
docs.text:
"Slashing ETL Madness with Go, HTMX, and Declarative Pipelines"

  • Single-Binary Engine: No Python runtimes, Celery workers, or JVM footprint.
  • Embedded HTMX Visual Builder: Interactive web studio served directly from the Go binary (flow -builder).
  • Live Bidirectional XML Sync: Visual drag-and-drop synchronized in real time with Git-friendly declarative XML.
  • Built-in Quality Gates & Telemetry: Full preflight validation, row-level telemetry, and compliance logging out of the box.

docs.title: An Embedded Visual Studio for Declarative Data Pipelines

docs.title: Core Capabilities at a Glance:
docs.text:
1. Interactive Component Toolbox: Instant drag-and-drop or click-to-add for variables, database connections, loops, scripts, and SQL tasks.
  2. Visual Hierarchy Canvas: Organizes pipelines into 4 distinct phases: Setup, Connections, Preflight Quality Gates, and Execution Flow.
  3. Real-time Live XML Preview: Instant validation, bidirectional feedback, copy, and export.
  4. Execution Dashboard: Run entire pipelines or preflight checks in isolation with live stream logs and row-count metrics.

docs.title: Default Slate Theme with Live Synchronization
What It's Doing:
docs.text:
• Left Panel (Component Palette): Provides organized categories of pipeline primitives:
  • Pipeline Setup: <variable>, <database>, <preflight>
  • Control Flow: <script>, <group>, <if>, <foreach>, <while>, <parallel>
  • Database & SQL: <sql>, <sql_bulk>
  • Key-Value & Cache: <kv>, <kv_bulk>
  • Templates & Storage: <template>, <excel_write>
  • Center Panel (Interactive Canvas): Displays the active pipeline split into clear execution stages:
  • <variables>: Configuration variables like TargetTable and connection strings (log_db_cs).
  • <databases>: Configured connection pools (local_sqlite, log_db).
  • <preflight>: Pre-execution diagnostic checks (pre_select_from_db_1, PRE_TABLE_RUN_CHECK).
  • <flow>: Main execution tasks (GET_LOGS).
  • Right Panel (Live XML Preview): Renders the exact schema-compliant declarative XML in real time with copy and export controls.
  • Top Bar Controls: Fast pipeline switching, tab navigation (scripts.xml, Config Overrides, CLI Options, Pipeline Runner), and database management (Purge DB).

docs.title: What It's Doing:
docs.text:
• Instant Dynamic Theme Switching: Powered by HTMX and CSS variables without page reloads.
  • Clean Daytime Ergonomics: Crisp borders, high-contrast typography, and accessible syntax coloring in the Live XML pane.
  • Identical Functional Parity: Full access to component insertion, drag reordering, and runner telemetry across all visual themes.

docs.title: What It's Doing:
docs.text:
• Developer-Centric Dark Mode: Modern dark charcoal surfaces with vibrant neon status indicators (blue, cyan, emerald, amber).
  • Code Editor Aesthetics: Matches standard VS Code dark styling for data engineers spending extended sessions designing complex ETL pipelines.
  • Syntax-Highlighted Live Code: Right pane provides clear, syntax-highlighted XML markup reflecting every card modification instantly.

docs.title: What It's Doing:
docs.text:
• Instant Palette Search: Typing "sql" into the component search bar dynamically filters available components down in real time.
  • Pipeline Selector: Active pipeline if_testing loaded from SQLite storage (flow_builder.db).
  • Visualizing Complex Control Flow:
  • Shows a conditional branch card (<if> PRE_IF_TABLE_COUNT_GT_0).
  • Condition expression: var: PRE_TABLE_AVAIL == '1'.
  • Distinct colored sub-branches:
    • Green Branch: <then> containing PRE_SUCCESS_STEP
    • Red Branch: <else> containing PRE_FAIL_STEP with template fallback {{.PRE_TABLE_AVAIL}} Failed.
  • Reordering & Editing: Every card features drag handles, up/down arrows (▲ ▼), in-line Edit dialog, and ✕ removal.

docs.title: Inserting Primitives Inside Conditional & Loop Blocks
What It's Doing:
docs.text:
• Scoped Component Insertion: The Add Step to <then> modal allows targeted insertion of any task directly inside nested branch containers.
  • Searchable Step Catalog: Instant filter bar (Filter components (e.g. assert, sql, http, template)...).
  • Supported Nested Primitives:
  • <script>: Execute embedded Go, Shell, PowerShell, Bash, Cmd, or C# (.NET CSX) code.
  • <group>: Nest tasks with independent retry policies, transaction rollback boundaries, and error policies.
  • <if>: Multi-level nested conditional logic.
  • <foreach> / <while>: Iterative streaming data loops over SQL result sets.
  • <parallel>: Concurrent multi-goroutine execution with synchronized joins.
  • <sql> / <sql_bulk>: High-throughput query execution and direct table-to-table stream copying.
  • <kv> / <kv_bulk>: Key-value operations on embedded BBolt/Badger or external Redis/etcd.
  • <template> / <template_html>: Contextual template rendering with automatic escaping.

docs.title: Native Multi-Engine Dialect Pooling & Secret Interpolation
What It's Doing:
docs.text:
• Named Connection Definition: Configures connection pool log_db assigned to the <databases> section.
  • Cross-Dialect Drivers: Built-in support for sqlserver, postgres, mysql, sqlite, oracle, and kv.
  • Dynamic Secret Interpolation:
  • Supports variable expansion syntax {{log_db_cs}}.
  • Resolves secrets up to 3 levels deep across base XML, environment overrides (-config), and CLI arguments (-vars).
  • Protects sensitive production credentials from hardcoded Git commits.
  • Workload Tuning Profiles: Optimizes connection pooling for oltp, bulk, analytics, or batch.
  • Connection Lifecycle Limits:
  • Max Open Connections (25)
  • Max Idle Connections (10)
  • Max Lifetime Duration (300 seconds)
  • Custom Dynamic Attributes: Expandable key-value pairs (e.g. description: Logging Database).

docs.title: Embedded SQLite Storage for Drafts and Production Scripts
What It's Doing:

• Centralized Pipeline Catalog: The Manage Loaded Pipelines modal lists all pipelines stored in the builder's local SQLite database (flow_builder.db).
  • Multi-Pipeline Switching:

docs.title: Everything You Need to Run Flow and the Visual Builder
Key Capabilities Summary:
docs.text:
• Visual HTMX Studio: Launch with flow -builder on an ephemeral or designated port.
  • Declarative XML Schema: Full pipeline reproducibility, version control, and CI/CD friendly.
  • Multi-Engine Dialects: Native translation for SQL Server, Postgres, MySQL, Oracle, and SQLite.

docs.title: Quick Start Commands:
docs.text:
# 1. Launch the Visual Builder web interface
flow -builder -builder-port 8080

# 2. Run Preflight quality validation only (non-destructive)
flow -file pipeline.xml -preflight

# 3. Execute full pipeline with pre-baked options profile
flow -file pipeline.xml -options options.xml

# 4. Run pipeline with runtime variable overrides
flow -file pipeline.xml -vars "TargetTable=prod_orders,BatchSize=10000"

docs.title: Executive Overview
docs.text:
Flow is an enterprise data integration and pipeline orchestration engine designed to automate, validate, and monitor complex ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) workflows. Built as a lightweight, low-overhead Go application, Flow enables organizations to define data processing jobs in structured XML or via an embedded web builder, execute parallel and conditional logic, automatically log operational telemetry to centralized databases, and auto-generate workflow documentation.

By combining traditional relational database support with high-performance Key-Value (K/V) stores and a visual web interface, Flow reduces operational overhead, accelerates job design, and enforces standardized auditing across heterogeneous enterprise data environments.

docs.title: 1. Interactive Web Builder & Low-Code Orchestration
docs.text:
• Embedded HTMX Web Builder: Features a standalone visual management web interface (-builder) running on a dynamically assigned ephemeral port (or user-configured via -builder-port) backed by an embedded metadata storage engine (flow_builder.db). Data engineers and analysts can visually design, inspect, and configure data pipelines without hand-crafting XML.

  • Declarative XML Workflows: Pipelines, scripts, connection strings, and variables are stored in structured XML definitions, enabling seamless version control and automated deployment pipelines.

  • Advanced Flow Control: Supports conditional evaluation (if), iterative looping (foreach, while), and concurrent execution branches (parallel) to maximize throughput for large-scale data processing.

  • Preflight & AST Validation: Performs pre-execution semantic schema (XSD) and AST validation passes to catch configuration errors before running production workloads.

docs.title: 2. Multi-Engine Storage: Relational & Key-Value (K/V) Databases
docs.text:
• Hybrid Storage Support: Integrates seamlessly across standard relational platforms (PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, SQLite, and Oracle) as well as Key-Value (K/V) database stores.

  • High-Speed Lookups & State Caching: Utilizes Key-Value data stores for rapid key-based state persistence, intermediate row caching, reference lookups, and fast deduplication during active pipeline execution.

  • Dialect & Syntax Abstraction: Dynamically handles connection pooling, dialect detection, and database-specific query and parameter placeholders across diverse database platforms.

docs.title: 3. Enterprise Auditability & Operational Telemetry
docs.text:
• Centralized Audit Logging: Automatically logs pipeline runs and individual step events to standardized audit tables (pipeline_runs and pipeline_events).

  • Granular Telemetry: Tracks real-time status, run durations, timestamps, error classifications, and exact row counts read, written, and affected.

  • Multi-Sink Fanout: Supports concurrent event streaming to console streams and database sinks simultaneously for real-time observability.

docs.title: 4. Dynamic Configuration & Environment Portability
docs.text:
• Multi-Tiered Parameter Management: Merges base XML configurations with environment-specific override files (-config) and command-line overrides (-vars).

  • Environment Promotion: Promotes data pipelines across Development, Staging, and Production environments without modifying core source logic.

  • XML CLI Load Profiles: Pre-loads flag options from reusable configuration files (-options) to simplify scheduled job runs.

docs.title: 5. Automated Documentation & Visual Management
docs.text:
• Auto-Generated Flowcharts: Dynamically renders XML pipeline structures into visual Mermaid.js diagrams (flowchart TD) for documentation and monitoring.

  • XSLT Stylesheet Processing: Includes an integrated XSLT 3.0 transformation engine to convert XML configurations into custom enterprise reports or formatted documentation packages.

docs.title: 6. Flexible Output Formatting
docs.text: • Multi-Format Output Engine: Generates output in raw JSON, formatted JSON, Markdown tables, CSV, plain text, or live-streamed console events.

docs.title: Feature Matrix
docs.text: Functional Area Business Capability Operational Benefit Pipeline Builder Embedded HTMX web UI (-builder) backed by flow_builder.db Speeds up pipeline construction and lowers technical barriers for non-developer teams. Multi-Engine Storage Native support for Relational DBs (Postgres, SQL Server, Oracle, etc.) and Key-Value stores Combines structured SQL processing with high-speed key-value state lookups. Pipeline Execution Parallel processing, conditional branching, loops (parallel, if, foreach) Minimizes batch execution windows and streamlines complex dependency handling. Audit & Logging Real-time event tracking (pipeline_events) with row-level metrics Ensures enterprise compliance readiness and provides instant root-cause failure diagnostics. Configuration Variable inheritance and runtime parameter overrides (-vars) Simplifies CI/CD integration and multi-environment deployment. Governance Auto-generated Mermaid.js visual diagrams & XSLT transformation engine Keeps pipeline architecture self-documenting and auditable.

docs.title: Strategic Value & ROI Impact
docs.text: Flow delivers a versatile, enterprise-ready data execution framework that eliminates the complexity of managing custom, brittle ETL scripts. By uniting an intuitive visual Web Builder with dual-mode storage support (relational and key-value) and automated compliance tracking, Flow enables organizations to scale their data operations efficiently while maintaining strict audit controls.

docs.title: The Flow Ecosystem (flow, go-flow, go-flowAPI, flowUI)
docs.text: The Flow Ecosystem is a complete, lightweight, and high-performance data integration, ETL (Extract, Transform, Load), and workflow orchestration platform. Designed as a modern, zero-bloat alternative to legacy tools like SSIS and heavy code-based orchestrators like Apache Airflow, the ecosystem spans four modular projects across Go and .NET 10.

docs.title: 1. High-Level Architecture & Component Relationships
docs.text:
The four projects form a layered architecture—from the embeddable core execution library up to the standalone CLI/runner, the central REST API & governance tier, and the enterprise Blazor Studio UI:
