docs.title: Summary of Projects
docs.text: Project Path Language / Stack Primary Role flow flow/ Go (1.26.5) Library Core embeddable pipeline AST parser, XSD/semantic validator, thread-isolated state Registry, polyglot script & control-flow Executor, and cross-database streaming ETL engine. go-flow go-flow/ Go (1.26.5) CLI & Packages Standalone single-binary CLI engine (flow.exe / go-flow.exe), cryptographic security package (pkg/flowcrypto), embedded local HTMX builder (builder/), Mermaid diagram generator, XSLT 3.0 processor, and helper tools (crypto_tool, db_importer). go-flowAPI go-flowAPI/ Go (1.26.5) HTTP Server Unified REST & Server-Sent Events (SSE) API wrapping flow and go-flow. Provides multi-dialect database artifact CRUD (pipelines, options, configs), synchronous and live-streamed execution, cryptographic endpoints, RBAC authentication (BasicAuth & Windows/AD), OpenAPI/Swagger UI, and full API/pipeline audit telemetry. flowUI flowUI/ .NET 10 / Blazor Server (C#) Rich web-based visual IDE ("Flow Builder Studio") built with Radzen Blazor. Communicates strictly via go-flowAPI (zero direct DB dependencies) to design pipelines, manage configs/options, sign/encrypt payloads, run & stream jobs, and inspect telemetry logs.

docs.title: 2.1 flow — Core Orchestration & Stream ETL Library
docs.text:
Location: flow/ | Module: github.com/etl-madness/flow

flow is the foundational Go package that defines the declarative XML pipeline language and executes the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST).

  • Zero Global State (registry.go): All variable values (string, int, bool, float, datetime, date) and database connection pools are encapsulated inside a thread-safe Registry instance. Multiple pipelines can run concurrently in the same OS process without interference.
  • Parsing & Multi-Stage Validation (config.go, validator.go, schema.go):
  • ParseXMLConfig decodes UTF-8 and UTF-16 XML configurations into <variables>, <databases>, <preflight>, and <flow> AST nodes.
  • ValidateXSD validates XML structure against the embedded xsd/pipeline.xsd schema.
  • ValidateAST performs semantic validation (ID uniqueness, database handle reference integrity, loop bounds).
  • Multi-Dialect Relational & Key-Value Support (etl.go, executor.go):
  • Relational Engines: Microsoft SQL Server (sqlserver/mssql), PostgreSQL (postgres), MySQL/MariaDB (mysql), Oracle (oracle), and SQLite (sqlite). Automatically translates parameter placeholders ($1, @p1, :1, ?) across dialects.
  • High-Speed MSSQL Bulk Copy: <sql_bulk> uses native TDS mssql.CopyIn streaming when targeting SQL Server (supporting tablock, check_constraints, fire_triggers, keep_nulls), and automatically throttles multi-row batched inserts for other engines to respect the 2,100-parameter limit.
  • Key-Value Engines (<kv>, <kv_bulk>): Native support for bbolt, badger, redis/valkey, and etcd for rapid state lookups, caching, and SQL-to-KV bulk streaming.
  • Control Flow & Task Primitives (executor.go):
  • Control Flow: <preflight>, <flow>, <parallel> (semaphore-throttled via max_threads, cloned worker registries, dirty-variable tracking, and WORKER_<id>_<var> collision namespacing), <if>/<then>/<else>, <foreach> (SQL-driven row iteration), <while> (bounded condition loops), <group> (optional database transaction wrapping with automatic commit/rollback), and <assert> (with <on_failure> fallback nodes).
  • Polyglot <script> Execution:
    • Embedded Go (language="go"): Powered by Yaegi with injected host/vars and host/db bridges.
    • Embedded Lua (language="lua"): Powered by Gopher-Lua with a global vars table (vars.Get, vars.Set, etc.) and stdout capture.
    • C# Scripts (language="csx" / dotnet-script): Inline or file-sourced C# execution with NuGet package support.
    • OS Shells: shell, cmd, powershell/pwsh, bash, git-bash, zsh, ksh, csh, tcsh, dash, fish, sh.
  • Data & File Nodes: <http_client> (full TLS, proxy, redirect, cookie jar, and header/status capture), <file_read>, <file_save>, <excel_read>, <excel_write> (via excelize), <template> (text/template), <template_html> (html/template), <json_path> (ajson), <yaml_path> (yaml.v3), and <xml_xpath> (xmlquery).
  • Observability & Event Sinks (observability.go): Emits structured ExecutionEvent and RunResult telemetry (tracking sequence numbers, durations, rows_read, rows_written, rows_affected, and node_output) to pluggable EventSink implementations.

docs.title: 2.2 go-flow — Standalone CLI Runner, Security Engine & Local Builder
docs.text:
Location: go-flow/ | Module: github.com/etl-madness/go-flow

go-flow wraps the flow library into a production-ready single-binary CLI executable (flow.exe / go-flow.exe) and provides reusable sub-packages consumed by go-flowAPI.

  • Hierarchical Configuration & Resource Loading (main.go, cli_loader.go, resource_loader.go):
  • Loads pipelines (-file), environment overrides (-config), and pre-baked CLI option profiles (-options, validated via xsd/options.xsd) from either local disk or database URIs (sql://... / db:...).
  • Applies a strict override hierarchy: Base Pipeline XML -> -options XML -> -config XML -> CLI -vars.
  • Expands nested variables in database connection strings up to 3 levels deep.
  • Cryptographic Security & Digital Signatures (pkg/flowcrypto/):
  • Encryption (FLOWENC:v1:): Pure-Go AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 key derivation. Supports key resolution via -key-file, -secure-key, or FLOW_SECURE_KEY.
  • Multi-Standard Digital Signatures (FLOWSIGNED:v1: & FLOWSIG:v1:): Pure-Go signature creation and verification across:
    1. OpenSSL / PEM: RSA (PKCS#1v1.5 & PSS), ECDSA (P-256, P-384), and Ed25519 keys and X.509 certificates.
    2. PKCS#7 / CMS (.p7s): Detached signatures with X.509 certificate and Root CA chain validation.
    3. OpenPGP / GPG (.asc, .sig): Armored detached signatures and keyrings via gopenpgp/v2.
  • Enforces a strict Verify -> Decrypt -> Parse -> Execute lifecycle.
  • Self-Documenting Pipelines (mermaid.go, xslt_processing.go, autodoc/):
  • Automatically converts pipeline ASTs into Mermaid.js flowchart TD diagrams.
  • Integrates an XSLT 3.0 processor (lestrrat-go/helium/xslt3) and built-in stylesheets (autodoc_html.xslt, autodoc_md.xslt, pipeline-to-csv.xslt) for automated HTML/Markdown/CSV documentation generation.
  • Multi-Format Output (formating.go): Supports csv, json, jsonpretty, markdown, text, and live stream output formats.
  • Embedded HTMX Web Builder (builder/): Invoking flow -builder starts a self-contained local web UI backed by SQLite (flow_builder.db) for standalone visual pipeline editing without external servers.
  • Companion Utilities:
  • crypto_tool/: Standalone CLI for key generation, file encryption/decryption, and digital signing/verification.
  • db_importer/: Utility for importing/exporting pipelines, options, and configs into database tables.

docs.title: 2.3 go-flowAPI — Unified REST, Execution, Security & Audit API
docs.text:
Location: go-flowAPI/ | Module: github.com/etl-madness/go-flowAPI

go-flowAPI exposes the full capabilities of flow and go-flow as a centralized, multi-tenant HTTP service and acts as the sole backend for flowUI.

  • 5 Supported Metadata & Audit Database Dialects (db.go, store.go, tables.go):
  • Connects at startup (-dsn / FLOW_API_DSN) to SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite, or Oracle.
  • Automatically adapts SQL dialect syntax and schema prefixes (DefaultSchema = "dbo." on SQL Server/Postgres, stripped automatically on SQLite/MySQL/Oracle).
  • Artifact Management & Upload (handlers.go, store.go):
  • Full CRUD, file upload (POST /api/v1/upload/{type}), and raw XML export across three artifact repositories:
    1. pipelines -> flow_pipeline_content
    2. options -> flow_options_content
    3. configs -> flow_config_content
  • Supports addressing artifacts by either unique Name or database ID, with on-the-fly decryption (?decrypt=true).
  • Synchronous & Live SSE Pipeline Execution (executor.go):
  • Full parity with go-flow CLI flags: supports inline XML or db:<name> / artifact ID references, -config and -options merging, runtime vars, XSD/AST validation (/api/v1/validate), preflight-only execution, XSLT transformations, signature verification, and decryption.
  • Synchronous Execution: POST /api/v1/execute and POST /api/v1/execute/{type}/{id}.
  • Real-Time Server-Sent Events (SSE): POST /api/v1/execute/stream and POST|GET /api/v1/execute/stream/{type}/{id} stream live node_event updates as each AST node starts and completes, followed by a final done event.
  • Cryptographic REST Endpoints (handlers_crypto.go):
  • /api/v1/crypto/keygen: Generates AES-256 keys, RSA-2048/4096, ECDSA-P256/P384, Ed25519 keypairs (with optional self-signed X.509 certificates), and OpenPGP keypairs.
  • /api/v1/crypto/encrypt & /api/v1/crypto/decrypt: Wraps/unwraps FLOWENC:v1: payloads.
  • /api/v1/crypto/sign & /api/v1/crypto/verify: Supports OPENSSL, PKCS7, and PGP schemes with none, sign-then-encrypt, and encrypt-then-sign envelope modes.
  • Authentication & Role-Based Access Control (auth.go, win_groups_windows.go):
  • Database-Backed BasicAuth: Validates users against flow_api_users (supporting bcrypt hashes, sha256: digests, or constant-time plaintext matching).
  • Windows / Active Directory Integrated Auth: Supports DOMAIN\user and DOMAIN\group resolution via X-Flow-Windows-User / X-Flow-Windows-Groups headers and native Windows group lookup so AD groups can be granted permissions directly in flow_api_users.
  • Granular Roles: read-only, execution-only, write / upload, and all (combinable via comma-separated lists).
  • Comprehensive Telemetry & OpenAPI (telemetry.go, swagger.go):
  • Every API request is audited to flow_api_events (/api/v1/audit).
  • Every pipeline run logs summaries to pipeline_runs (/api/v1/runs) and step-level metrics + 64 KB UTF-8 truncated & secret-redacted node_output to pipeline_events (/api/v1/events).
  • Built-in interactive Swagger UI at /swagger/ (and /docs) backed by an OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec (/api/v1/openapi.json).

docs.title: 2.4 flowUI — Enterprise Blazor Visual Studio
docs.text:
Location: flowUI/ | Solution: FlowUI.sln (.NET 10 / Blazor Interactive Server)

flowUI is a modern, stateless web IDE ("Flow Builder Studio") built with ASP.NET Core 10 Razor Components and Radzen Blazor.

[!IMPORTANT] Strict API-Driven Architecture: flowUI has no direct database connection and no internal database. All artifact persistence, validation, execution, cryptography, authentication, and log queries flow exclusively through FlowApiClient to go-flowAPI.

  • Workspace Tabs (Components/Tabs/):
  • Pipeline Designer (PipelineDesignerTab.razor): Visual drag-and-drop/card-based AST builder for Variables, Databases, Preflight steps, and Flow nodes (including nested <parallel>, <if>, <foreach>, <while>, <group>, and <assert> blocks), paired with bidirectional XML generation (XmlGeneratorService.cs), XML import (XmlImporterService.cs), and live Mermaid.js diagram rendering.
  • Config (ConfigTab.razor): Visual and XML editor for environment override <Configuration> artifacts (flow_config_content).
  • Options (OptionsTab.razor): Editor for reusable <cli_options> execution profiles (flow_options_content).
  • Runner (RunnerTab.razor): Interactive execution console supporting artifact selection, runtime variable overrides, validation/preflight toggles, cryptographic key/certificate inputs, and live SSE event streaming from go-flowAPI.
  • Logs (LogsTab.razor): Unified telemetry explorer for pipeline_runs, step-level pipeline_events (with detailed node_output inspection via EventDetailModal.razor), and flow_api_events API audit trails.
  • Settings (SettingsTab.razor): API connectivity diagnostics, database connection testing (/api/v1/db/test), and flow_api_users RBAC user management.
  • Handbook (Handbook.razor & DocsService.cs): Embedded searchable component reference guide rendered from FlowUI/Docs/*.md via Markdig.
  • Integrated Cryptographic Studio (CryptoSignVerifyModal.razor & FlowCryptoService.cs): Interactive UI for generating keys/certificates, encrypting/decrypting artifacts (FLOWENC:v1:), and signing/verifying payloads (FLOWSIGNED:v1:).
  • Pluggable UI Authentication (Services/Auth/):
  • FlowApiPassthroughAuthProvider (ApiBasic): Authenticates directly against go-flowAPI using HTTP Basic Auth credentials entered at login.
  • WindowsIntegratedUiAuthProvider (Windows) & WindowsCredentialsUiAuthProvider (WindowsCredentials): Resolves OS/Active Directory identity (DOMAIN\user) and group memberships (DOMAIN\group) via Windows advapi32.dll LogonUser / WindowsIdentity and maps permissions against flow_api_users in go-flowAPI.

docs.title: 3. Shared Database Schema & Storage Model
docs.text:
Across go-flow, go-flowAPI, and flowUI, a unified 7-table schema (defaulting to schema dbo. on SQL Server and PostgreSQL) powers artifact storage, security, and observability:

Table Name Used By Purpose flow_pipeline_content go-flow, go-flowAPI, flowUI Stores named <pipeline> XML definitions (plaintext, FLOWENC:v1: encrypted, or FLOWSIGNED:v1: signed). flow_options_content go-flow, go-flowAPI, flowUI Stores reusable <cli_options> execution profiles. flow_config_content go-flow, go-flowAPI, flowUI Stores environment-specific <Configuration> override profiles (variables & database connections). pipeline_runs flow, go-flow, go-flowAPI, flowUI Run-level execution summary (run_id, status, started_at, finished_at, duration_ms, task_count, user_name, hostname, error_class, error_message). pipeline_events flow, go-flow, go-flowAPI, flowUI Granular step-level audit trail (sequence_num, node_kind, node_id, status, rows_read, rows_written, rows_affected, node_output). flow_api_events go-flowAPI, flowUI HTTP API audit trail recording every REST operation, authenticated user, status code, duration, and JSON details. flow_api_users go-flowAPI, flowUI Users, Active Directory groups, password hashes (bcrypt/SHA-256), and role permissions (read-only, execution-only, write, upload, all).

docs.title: 4. End-to-End Execution & Security Lifecycle
docs.text:
Whether a pipeline is triggered from the CLI (go-flow), via REST/SSE (go-flowAPI), or interactively from Flow Builder Studio (flowUI), the ecosystem executes a deterministic 6-stage pipeline lifecycle:

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as User / Scheduler
    participant UI as flowUI (Blazor Studio)
    participant API as go-flowAPI (REST / SSE)
    participant Crypto as go-flow/pkg/flowcrypto
    participant Engine as flow (Registry & Executor)
    participant DB as Metadata & Target DBs

    User->>UI: Click "Run Pipeline" (or invoke CLI / API)
    UI->>API: POST /api/v1/execute/stream (Basic / Windows Auth)
    API->>DB: Authenticate User/Group (flow_api_users) & Log API Event
    API->>DB: Load Pipeline, Options & Config XML (flow_*_content)
    API->>Crypto: 1. Verify Signature (FLOWSIGNED:v1: / .sig / .p7s / .asc)
    API->>Crypto: 2. Decrypt Payload (FLOWENC:v1: AES-256-GCM)
    API->>Engine: 3. ParseXMLConfig + Apply Overrides (Options -> Config -> Vars)
    API->>Engine: 4. ValidateXSD & ValidateAST
    API->>Engine: 5. InitVariables & InitDatabases (3-level conn string expansion)
    loop For each AST Node in <preflight> and <flow>
        Engine->>DB: Execute SQL / Bulk Stream / KV / Script / HTTP
        Engine-->>API: Emit ExecutionEvent (rows read/written, node_output)
        API-->>DB: Insert into pipeline_events
        API-->>UI: Stream SSE event: node_event
    end
    Engine-->>API: Return RunResult
    API->>DB: Insert summary into pipeline_runs & flow_api_events
    API-->>UI: Stream SSE event: done (Final Run Summary)

docs.title: 5. Deployment Topologies
docs.text:
The ecosystem supports flexible deployment models ranging from zero-dependency single-binary CLI execution to full containerized microservices (detailed in go-flowAPI/DOCKER.md and flowUI/DOCKER.md):

  1. Standalone CLI / Batch Agent (go-flow only):
  2. Deploy the single flow.exe / go-flow binary on any Windows, Linux, macOS, or FreeBSD host (e.g., via Cron, Autosys JIL, or Windows Task Scheduler) using local XML files or sql:// database URIs.
  3. Local Developer Mode (go-flow -builder):
  4. Run flow -builder -builder-port 8080 to use the embedded HTMX visual builder backed by a local flow_builder.db SQLite file.
  5. Headless API Server (go-flowAPI + Database):
  6. Run go-flowAPI via binary or Docker Compose (docker-compose.sqlserver.yml, docker-compose.postgres.yml, docker-compose.sqlite.yml) for CI/CD artifact publishing, remote job triggering, and centralized auditing.
  7. Full Enterprise Studio Stack (flowUI + go-flowAPI + Database):
  8. Orchestrated via flowUI/docker-compose.full.yml (self-contained with SQL Server 2022 and automatic schema initialization), flowUI/docker-compose.api.yml (UI + API containers against an external DB), or Windows Containers (Dockerfile.windows) for native Active Directory / Windows Integrated Authentication.

docs.title: Pipeline Assertions in Flow 🚨
docs.text: Flow pipelines support native <assert> tags to perform data quality checks, environment checks, and business rule validations. With assertions, you can gracefully halt execution on critical issues or run fallback pipelines to recover or log warnings.

docs.title: 🛠️ Configuration Syntax
docs.text:
The <assert> tag supports the following attributes:

  • var: The name of the variable inside the pipeline registry to evaluate. (Required)
  • equals / value: The expected value to compare against (case-insensitive string comparison).
  • message: A custom error/warning message to log when the assertion fails.
  • on_failure: Behavior on assertion failure. Options:
    • halt (default): Immediately stops pipeline execution and returns a non-zero exit code.
    • warn / continue: Logs a warning to the execution results but allows the pipeline to continue.
  • fail_var: (Optional) Pipeline variable name to set when the assertion fails.
  • fail_val: (Optional) The value to set in fail_var (defaults to "true" if omitted).
  • <on_failure>: (Optional) A nested child element containing sequence nodes (e.g., <script>, <sql>, <http_client>) to execute only if the assertion fails.

docs.title: Example 1: Basic Environment Check (Fail-Fast)
docs.text:
Ensure the active pipeline environment variable matches the production expectation. If not, halt the pipeline immediately.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="ENV" type="string" value="staging" />
    </variables>
    <flow>
        <!-- This will halt execution since ENV is staging instead of production -->
        <assert id="check_production" 
                var="ENV" 
                equals="production" 
                message="Pipeline must be run in production environment!" 
                on_failure="halt" />

        <!-- Subsequent nodes will not run -->
        <script id="prod_deploy" language="powershell">
            Write-Host "Deploying to production..."
        </script>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 2: API Status Verification with Warnings
docs.text:
Run a warning-only assertion that checks an HTTP client's status code, logging a warning and setting a failure flag, but allowing execution to continue.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <flow>
        <http_client id="fetch_health" 
                     url="https://api.example.com/health" 
                     status_code_var="STATUS_CODE" />

        <!-- Log a warning and set PIPELINE_DIRTY to true if status is not 200 -->
        <assert id="assert_api_health" 
                var="STATUS_CODE" 
                equals="200" 
                message="Health check returned non-200 code!" 
                on_failure="warn"
                fail_var="PIPELINE_DIRTY" 
                fail_val="true" />

        <script id="log_results" language="go">
            package main
            import (
                "fmt"
                "host/vars"
            )
            func main() {
                isDirty := vars.GetString("PIPELINE_DIRTY")
                if isDirty == "true" {
                    fmt.Println("Warning: Pipeline marked as dirty.")
                } else {
                    fmt.Println("Health checks passed successfully!")
                }
            }
        </script>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 3: Fallback and Cleanup on Failure (<on_failure>)
docs.text:
Use the nested <on_failure> block to run fallback scripts or cleanup actions when an assertion fails.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="temp_db" driver="sqlite" connection_string="./temp.db" />
    </databases>
    <variables>
        <variable name="RECORD_COUNT" type="int" value="0" />
    </variables>
    <flow>
        <!-- Check if we ingested any records. If not, trigger the <on_failure> block -->
        <assert id="verify_ingested_records" 
                var="RECORD_COUNT" 
                equals="1000" 
                on_failure="halt" 
                message="Ingested record count does not match expected threshold!">
            <on_failure>
                <!-- Run a SQL cleanup script before halting -->
                <sql id="rollback_staging" db="temp_db">
                    DELETE FROM staging_records;
                </sql>
                <script id="notify_slack" language="go">
                    package main
                    import "fmt"
                    func main() {
                        fmt.Println("Sending Slack alert: Ingestion failed, staging table rolled back.")
                    }
                </script>
            </on_failure>
        </assert>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Database Operations in Flow Pipelines 🗄️
docs.text: Flow features native, high-performance integration with both relational SQL databases and modern Key-Value (KV) stores—enabling direct query execution, transactional grouping, rapid bulk data replication, key-value lookups/streaming, and styled multi-tab spreadsheet generation.

docs.title: Supported Databases & Storage Engines
docs.text:
Engine / Store Driver Identifier(s) Type Connection String Example Primary Workload & Capabilities PostgreSQL postgres, postgresql, pq Relational SQL postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/dbname?sslmode=disable OLTP, high-throughput bulk ETL, JSON analytics SQLite sqlite, sqlite3 Embedded SQL file::memory:?cache=shared or ./app.db Local development, testing, caching, zero-config persistence MySQL mysql Relational SQL user:pass@tcp(localhost:3306)/dbname?parseTime=true Web OLTP, read replicas, batch ingestion SQL Server sqlserver, mssql Relational SQL sqlserver://sa:pass@localhost:1433?database=dbname Enterprise OLTP, analytics, fast bulk copies (tablock) Oracle oracle, godror Relational SQL oracle://user:pass@localhost:1521/service_name Mission-critical enterprise OLTP, data warehouses bbolt bbolt, bolt Embedded KV ./data/cache.db ACID transactions, zero-dependency embedded KV caching BadgerDB badger, badgerdb Embedded KV ./data/badger_dir LSM-tree architecture, high-write-throughput embedded KV Redis / Valkey redis, valkey Server KV redis://:password@localhost:6379/0 or 127.0.0.1:6379 In-memory caching, pub/sub, pipelined bulk replication etcd etcd, etcdv3 Distributed KV http://127.0.0.1:2379,http://127.0.0.1:22379 Distributed configuration, metadata consensus, prefix scans

[!TIP] For an exhaustive reference of all driver options, SSL/TLS certificates, query pragmas, network packet sizing, and multi-scenario connection string examples across all supported engines, see the dedicated Database Connection Strings & Driver Reference Guide.

docs.title: Database Connection Tuning <database>
docs.text:
Defined under <databases> as child <database> elements. Connection parameters live on the <database> definition itself, not on each SQL or KV step.

  • name: unique logical database identifier used by SQL and KV nodes.
  • driver: database driver (e.g., sqlite, postgres, mysql, sqlserver, oracle, bbolt, badger, redis, etcd).
  • connection_string: driver-specific DSN, file path, or endpoint list. Supports variable interpolation (e.g. {{DB_URL}}).
  • max_open_conns: max number of simultaneous open connections in the pool (SQL engines).
  • max_idle_conns: number of idle connections retained ready for reuse (SQL engines).
  • conn_max_lifetime_seconds: maximum age of a pooled connection before it is recycled (SQL engines).
  • workload: optional tuning profile label such as oltp, bulk, or analytics (SQL engines).

A workload is the operational pattern of a database connection. It describes how a connection is expected to be used at runtime so the pool can be tuned for the right trade-off between concurrency, latency, and throughput. In practice, Flow uses the workload label as a hint to choose sane defaults for connection count, idle retention, and lifetime without hardcoding one-size-fits-all values.

Common workload types: - oltp: short, latency-sensitive reads and writes; keep a moderate number of open connections and shorter idle time to reduce cold-start latency. - bulk: large ETL or ingestion jobs; favor larger pools and more throughput, with a shorter connection lifetime to handle high churn. - analytics: read-heavy reporting workloads; balance concurrency and reuse to support many query workers without oversubscribing the server. - batch: scheduled, non-interactive jobs that may run bursts; a tuned pool can temporarily scale higher but still recycle stale connections.

These labels are metadata, not required switches: they are optional and can be omitted. When omitted, the runtime falls back to the safe defaults already used by the registry.

Supported database engines and typical workload fit: - SQLite: best for local dev, embedded apps, testing, and lightweight single-user workflows; commonly used with oltp or batch. - PostgreSQL: strong fit for oltp, analytics, and bulk patterns; widely used for transactional apps, staging pipelines, and reporting. - MySQL: commonly used for oltp and batch workloads; also suitable for bulk ingestion when configured with a larger pool. - SQL Server / MSSQL: strong fit for oltp, analytics, and bulk, including large ETL copy operations with tablock and other MSSQL-specific bulk options. - Oracle: commonly used for mission-critical oltp and analytics workloads with tuned connection reuse and larger query fan-out.

These workload labels are not limited to a single database engine; they describe the application behavior of the connection, so all supported drivers can use the same tuning model.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
<databases>
    <database name="analytics_db"
              driver="postgres"
              connection_string="host=localhost port=5432 user=app password=secret dbname=analytics sslmode=disable"
              max_open_conns="25"
              max_idle_conns="10"
              conn_max_lifetime_seconds="300"
              workload="oltp" />
</databases>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example: Pool tuning for bulk ETL
docs.text:
Use a larger pool for high-throughput bulk workloads and a shorter idle lifetime for transient jobs.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
<databases>
    <database name="warehouse_db"
              driver="postgres"
              connection_string="host=warehouse.internal port=5432 user=loader password=secret dbname=warehouse sslmode=disable"
              max_open_conns="80"
              max_idle_conns="20"
              conn_max_lifetime_seconds="180"
              workload="bulk" />
</databases>

<flow>
    <sql_bulk id="bulk_copy_orders"
              db="orders_db"
              target_db="warehouse_db"
              target_table="orders_fact"
              batch_size="5000">
        SELECT order_id, customer_id, amount, created_at FROM orders WHERE created_at >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 days';
    </sql_bulk>
</flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: 1. <sql>
docs.text: Used for executing standard SQL scripts (DDL, DML, multi-statement batches, and analytical queries). - db / database: Name of the configured database connection to execute against. - id: Unique identifier for this step. - output_var / var / variable: (Optional) Pipeline variable where query results (with column headers) or affected row counts will be stored as a string. - Intelligent Query vs. DML Classification: Flow employs a token-aware query classifier (isDMLQuery) that strips SQL line comments (--), block comments (/* ... */), and XML <![CDATA[...]]> tags. - Query Mode: Statements starting with SELECT, WITH, SHOW, PRAGMA, DESCRIBE, or containing row-returning clauses like RETURNING or OUTPUT are executed as queries. Results are formatted as a tabular text block into output_var. Columns named deleted_at, is_deleted, insert_ts, or update_count are recognized as regular projected columns without false DML classification. - DML / DDL Mode: Pure mutating statements (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, DROP, CREATE, ALTER, TRUNCATE) are executed as updates, and the affected row count is recorded.

docs.title: 2. <sql_bulk>
docs.text:
Optimized for streaming massive datasets directly from a source database query into a target table across heterogeneous database engines (e.g., PostgreSQL to SQL Server, MySQL to SQLite), bypassing CPU and memory bottlenecks with constant $O(1)$ RAM usage. - db / database: The source database connection name. - target_db / target_database: The destination database connection name (defaults to the source database if omitted). - target_table: The destination table to bulk insert records into. - batch_size: The row batch size (defaults to 10000). - tablock: Acquire a table lock for minimal logging on SQL Server (true / false, defaults to true). - check_constraints: Evaluate table constraints during bulk insert (true / false). - fire_triggers: Execute target table triggers during insert (true / false). - keep_nulls: Preserve explicit NULL values (true / false).

[!TIP] For in-depth guidance on choosing between <sql>, <sql_bulk>, and <foreach>, refer to the dedicated SQL & SQL Bulk Guide.

docs.title: 3. <kv>
docs.text: Executes individual atomic operations (get, put/set, delete/del, scan/list) against Key-Value stores (bbolt, badger, redis, etcd). - db / database: Name of the configured KV database connection handle. - id: Unique identifier for this step. - bucket: Target bucket name (bbolt, badger) or namespace key prefix (redis, etcd). Defaults to "default". - op: Operation type: get, put / set, delete / del, or scan / list. - key: Target key name. - value: Value payload to store (for put / set). - output_var / var / variable: (Optional) Pipeline variable receiving the operation result or returned values. - Inline DSL: Operations, keys, and values may also be written inside the node body (e.g. set mykey myval or get mykey).

docs.title: 4. <kv_bulk>
docs.text: Streams records directly from a SQL query source into a target Key-Value store bucket or namespace in high-throughput batches. - db / database: Name of the source SQL database connection executing the query. - target_db: Target Key-Value database connection handle. - target_bucket: Target bucket or key namespace prefix in the destination KV store. - batch_size: Number of records committed per chunk (defaults to 10000). Automatically flushes Badger write batches and submits transactional commits in Etcd. - output_var / var: (Optional) Pipeline variable receiving the total count of transferred records. - Query Body: The enclosed SQL query must project at least two columns: key (col 1) and value (col 2).

docs.title: Example 1: Schema Setup and Data Ingestion (<sql>)
docs.text:
Initialize a database table structure and load initial seed data.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="analytics_db"
                  driver="sqlite"
                  connection_string="file::memory:?cache=shared"
                  max_open_conns="25"
                  max_idle_conns="10"
                  conn_max_lifetime_seconds="300"
                  workload="oltp" />
    </databases>
    <flow>
        <sql id="setup_analytics_schema" db="analytics_db">
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS page_views (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                url TEXT NOT NULL,
                visitor_ip TEXT,
                viewed_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
            );

            INSERT INTO page_views (url, visitor_ip) VALUES 
            ('/home', '192.168.1.1'),
            ('/products', '192.168.1.100'),
            ('/checkout', '192.168.1.100');
        </sql>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 2: Dynamic Querying with Parameter Interpolation (<sql>)
docs.text:
Filter database records dynamically utilizing pipeline environment variables.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="production_db" driver="postgres" connection_string="postgresql://app:secret@localhost:5432/prod" />
    </databases>
    <variables>
        <variable name="MIN_RATING" type="float" value="4.5" />
        <variable name="LIMIT_COUNT" type="int" value="10" />
    </variables>
    <flow>
        <sql id="fetch_top_products" db="production_db" output_var="RECOMMENDED_PRODUCTS">
            SELECT product_id, title, rating 
            FROM store.products 
            WHERE rating >= {{MIN_RATING}} 
            ORDER BY rating DESC 
            LIMIT {{LIMIT_COUNT}};
        </sql>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 3: High-Performance Data Archival (<sql_bulk>)
docs.text:
Bulk replicate records from a production database directly into a separate analytics cold storage target.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="prod_db" driver="mysql" connection_string="root:secret@tcp(localhost:3306)/prod" />
        <database name="archive_db" driver="sqlite" connection_string="./archive.db" />
    </databases>
    <flow>
        <!-- Stream rows in batches of 5000 directly from source to target -->
        <sql_bulk id="archive_historical_logs" 
                  db="prod_db" 
                  target_db="archive_db" 
                  target_table="historical_logs" 
                  batch_size="5000">
            SELECT log_id, event, severity, created_at 
            FROM system.logs 
            WHERE created_at < DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 90 DAY);
        </sql_bulk>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 4: Exporting Queries to Multiple Excel Tabs (<excel_write>)
docs.text:
Consolidate multiple database reports into separate tabs inside a single .xlsx workbook using consecutive <excel_write> nodes.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="retail_db" driver="postgres" connection_string="postgresql://app:secret@localhost:5432/retail" />
    </databases>
    <flow>
        <!-- Tab 1: Store Sales Overview -->
        <excel_write id="write_sales_overview" 
                     file="./reports/Retail_Dashboard.xlsx" 
                     sheet="Sales Summary" 
                     db="retail_db">
            SELECT date_trunc('month', sale_date) AS sale_month, SUM(revenue) AS total_revenue
            FROM sales.daily_ledger
            GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 DESC;
        </excel_write>

        <!-- Tab 2: Best Performing Products -->
        <excel_write id="write_top_inventory" 
                     file="./reports/Retail_Dashboard.xlsx" 
                     sheet="Top Products" 
                     db="retail_db">
            SELECT sku, product_name, units_sold, stock_on_hand
            FROM sales.product_performance
            WHERE units_sold > 500
            ORDER BY units_sold DESC;
        </excel_write>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 5: Combined Ingestion, Bulk Replication, and Multi-Tab Reporting
docs.text:
Build a complete end-to-end data staging, bulk copy, and multi-tab Excel dashboard export workflow.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="crm_db" driver="postgres" connection_string="postgresql://app:secret@localhost:5432/crm" />
        <database name="reporting_warehouse" driver="sqlite" connection_string="./warehouse.db" />
    </databases>
    <flow>
        <!-- 1. Staging tables creation -->
        <sql id="create_staging_structures" db="reporting_warehouse">
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS stg_leads (
                lead_id INTEGER, 
                company TEXT, 
                deal_size REAL, 
                stage TEXT
            );
        </sql>

        <!-- 2. Bulk stream dynamic leads data directly to staging database -->
        <sql_bulk id="stage_crm_leads" 
                  db="crm_db" 
                  target_db="reporting_warehouse" 
                  target_table="stg_leads" 
                  batch_size="1000">
            SELECT id AS lead_id, company, deal_size, status AS stage 
            FROM public.leads 
            WHERE status IN ('Qualified', 'Proposal Sent');
        </sql_bulk>

        <!-- 3. Export Summary to Sheet 1 -->
        <excel_write id="report_summary" 
                     file="./reports/CRM_Leads_Report.xlsx" 
                     sheet="Summary Overview" 
                     db="reporting_warehouse">
            SELECT stage, COUNT(lead_id) AS total_leads, SUM(deal_size) AS pipeline_value
            FROM stg_leads
            GROUP BY stage;
        </excel_write>

        <!-- 4. Export Raw Details to Sheet 2 -->
        <excel_write id="report_raw_details" 
                     file="./reports/CRM_Leads_Report.xlsx" 
                     sheet="Lead Details" 
                     db="reporting_warehouse">
            SELECT lead_id, company, deal_size, stage
            FROM stg_leads
            ORDER BY deal_size DESC;
        </excel_write>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 6: Reading Excel Data and Writing to a Database
docs.text:
Extract data from a spreadsheet using <excel_read> and write it to a database using a Go interpreter script.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="inventory_db" driver="postgres" connection_string="postgresql://app:secret@localhost:5432/inventory" />
    </databases>
    <flow>
        <!-- 1. Extract spreadsheet data into a pipeline variable containing JSON string -->
        <excel_read file="./uploads/inventory_updates.xlsx" sheet="New_Arrivals" header="true" output_var="EXCEL_JSON" />

        <!-- 2. Loop over extracted data programmatically and insert/update in database -->
        <script lang="go">
            package main
            import (
                "encoding/json"
                "fmt"
                "host/vars"
                "host/db"
            )

            type Item struct {
                SKU   string  `json:"sku"`
                Name  string  `json:"name"`
                Price float64 `json:"price"`
                Stock int     `json:"stock"`
            }

            func main() {
                jsonData := vars.GetString("EXCEL_JSON")
                var items []Item
                if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(jsonData), &items); err != nil {
                    panic(err)
                }

                // Retrieve the database connection
                conn, err := db.Get("inventory_db")
                if err != nil {
                    panic(err)
                }

                for _, item := range items {
                    _, err := conn.Exec(`
                        INSERT INTO products (sku, name, price, stock) 
                        VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4) 
                        ON CONFLICT (sku) 
                        DO UPDATE SET price = EXCLUDED.price, stock = EXCLUDED.stock`,
                        item.SKU, item.Name, item.Price, item.Stock,
                    )
                    if err != nil {
                        panic(err)
                    }
                }
                fmt.Printf("Successfully imported %d items from Excel to DB\n", len(items))
            }
        </script>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 7: Wrapping SQL Script Blocks inside Transactions
docs.text:
Use <group> with transaction="true" to wrap multiple SQL operations inside an atomic transaction, ensuring automatic rollback on any failure.

Flow implements a thread-safe transaction stack (activeTxs): - Nested Transactions: If an inner <group transaction="true"> executes against the same database as an outer transaction, Flow automatically provisions a dialect-aware savepoint: ANSI SAVEPOINT / ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT / RELEASE SAVEPOINT for PostgreSQL, SQLite, and MySQL; T-SQL SAVE TRANSACTION / ROLLBACK TRANSACTION (with automatic release omission) for Microsoft SQL Server; and SAVEPOINT for Oracle. If the inner group completes successfully, its savepoint is committed/released; if it fails, it rolls back to the savepoint without corrupting the outer transaction. - Fail-Safe Defer Rollback: Any unhandled error, pipeline cancellation, or runtime panic triggers an immediate rollback, popping the transaction stack cleanly and preventing hanging database locks. - Transaction Timeout: You can specify timeout="30s" on the <group> node to ensure a stuck transaction does not block connection pools indefinitely.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="finance_db" driver="postgres" connection_string="postgresql://app:secret@localhost:5432/finance" />
    </databases>
    <flow>
        <!-- Outer transaction boundary with a 30s deadline -->
        <group id="transfer_funds_txn" transaction="true" db="finance_db" timeout="30s" description="Transfers balance safely between accounts">

            <!-- Step 1: Withdraw from Account A -->
            <sql id="withdraw_acc_a" db="finance_db">
                UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 250.00 WHERE account_id = 'ACC-001' AND balance >= 250.00;
            </sql>

            <!-- Step 2: Nested transaction block using ANSI SAVEPOINT -->
            <group id="nested_audit_log" transaction="true" db="finance_db">
                <sql id="log_txn_event" db="finance_db">
                    INSERT INTO transactions_ledger (from_account, to_account, amount) VALUES ('ACC-001', 'ACC-002', 250.00);
                </sql>
            </group>

            <!-- Step 3: Deposit into Account B -->
            <sql id="deposit_acc_b" db="finance_db">
                UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 250.00 WHERE account_id = 'ACC-002';
            </sql>

        </group>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 8: Inserting excel_read JSON Output directly using SQL JSON Parsing
docs.text: If your database engine supports native JSON processing functions, you can pass the JSON output variable from <excel_read> directly into your <sql> node for inline database insertion.

docs.title: Method A: PostgreSQL (Using json_populate_recordset)
docs.text:
<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="store_db" driver="postgres" connection_string="postgresql://app:secret@localhost:5432/store" />
    </databases>
    <flow>
        <!-- 1. Extract spreadsheet rows to a variable containing a JSON array string -->
        <excel_read file="./uploads/catalog.xlsx" sheet="Products" header="true" output_var="CATALOG_JSON" />

        <!-- 2. Deserialize and insert directly inside SQL using postgres JSON engine functions -->
        <sql id="import_catalog" db="store_db">
            INSERT INTO store.inventory (sku, name, price)
            SELECT sku, name, price 
            FROM json_populate_recordset(NULL::store.inventory, '{{CATALOG_JSON}}');
        </sql>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Method B: SQLite (Using json_each)
docs.text:
<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="local_db" driver="sqlite" connection_string="./local.db" />
    </databases>
    <flow>
        <!-- 1. Extract worksheet data into a variable containing a JSON array string -->
        <excel_read file="./uploads/users.xlsx" sheet="Sheet1" header="true" output_var="USER_JSON" />

        <!-- 2. Parse and insert using SQLite's built-in json_each function -->
        <sql id="import_users" db="local_db">
            INSERT INTO users (username, role)
            SELECT 
                json_extract(value, '$.username') AS username,
                json_extract(value, '$.role') AS role
            FROM json_each('{{USER_JSON}}');
        </sql>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Method C: Microsoft SQL Server / MSSQL (Using OPENJSON)
docs.text:
<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="mssql_db" driver="sqlserver" connection_string="sqlserver://sa:secret@localhost:1433?database=store" />
    </databases>
    <flow>
        <!-- 1. Extract spreadsheet rows into a JSON array variable string -->
        <excel_read file="./uploads/catalog.xlsx" sheet="Products" header="true" output_var="CATALOG_JSON" />

        <!-- 2. Parse and insert using SQL Server's native OPENJSON function -->
        <sql id="import_catalog_mssql" db="mssql_db">
            INSERT INTO dbo.inventory (sku, name, price)
            SELECT sku, name, price
            FROM OPENJSON('{{CATALOG_JSON}}')
            WITH (
                sku VARCHAR(50) '$.sku',
                name VARCHAR(100) '$.name',
                price DECIMAL(10, 2) '$.price'
            );
        </sql>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 9: Key-Value Single Operations (<kv>)
docs.text:
Demonstrates interacting with embedded stores (bbolt, badger) and server instances (redis, etcd) using both XML attributes and inline DSL syntax.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="local_cache" driver="bbolt" connection_string="./data/cache.db" />
        <database name="redis_pub" driver="redis" connection_string="redis://localhost:6379/0" />
    </databases>
    <flow>
        <!-- Attribute syntax: write and read from bbolt -->
        <kv id="set_cfg" db="local_cache" bucket="settings" op="put" key="max_workers" value="64" />
        <kv id="get_cfg" db="local_cache" bucket="settings" op="get" key="max_workers" output_var="WORKER_COUNT" />

        <!-- Inline DSL syntax: Redis commands -->
        <kv id="redis_cache_session" db="redis_pub" bucket="sessions">
            set sess:12345 user_session_payload
        </kv>
        <kv id="redis_get_session" db="redis_pub" bucket="sessions" output_var="SESSION_DATA">
            get sess:12345
        </kv>

        <!-- Prefix Scan -->
        <kv id="scan_sessions" db="redis_pub" bucket="sessions" op="scan" key="sess:" output_var="ACTIVE_SESSIONS" />

        <!-- Key Deletion -->
        <kv id="delete_session" db="redis_pub" bucket="sessions" op="del" key="sess:12345" />
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 10: SQL to Key-Value High-Throughput Bulk ETL (<kv_bulk>)
docs.text:
Streams key-value projections from a relational SQL database straight into a Key-Value target bucket in high-speed batches.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="sql_catalog" driver="postgres" connection_string="postgresql://app:secret@localhost:5432/store" />
        <database name="fast_redis" driver="redis" connection_string="redis://localhost:6379/0" />
        <database name="embedded_badger" driver="badger" connection_string="./data/product_cache" />
    </databases>
    <flow>
        <!-- Replicate product prices directly into Redis cache in chunks of 5000 -->
        <kv_bulk id="bulk_cache_prices"
                 db="sql_catalog"
                 target_db="fast_redis"
                 target_bucket="product_prices"
                 batch_size="5000"
                 output_var="RECORDS_CACHED">
            SELECT sku, CAST(price AS TEXT) FROM store.products WHERE active = true
        </kv_bulk>

        <!-- Stream lookup values into an embedded BadgerDB LSM storage -->
        <kv_bulk id="bulk_seed_badger"
                 db="sql_catalog"
                 target_db="embedded_badger"
                 target_bucket="sku_inventory"
                 batch_size="10000">
            SELECT sku, CAST(quantity AS TEXT) FROM store.inventory
        </kv_bulk>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

For dedicated details, driver characteristics, and DSL syntax, refer to the Key-Value Documentation.

docs.title: Database-Backed Resource Storage & Encryption 🔒
docs.text:
Flow supports loading pipelines, options, and configuration overrides directly from database tables using standard SQL URIs:

sql://<driver>@<dsn>#SELECT ...

docs.title: Encrypted Storage at Rest
docs.text:
Sensitive database rows containing pipeline logic, connection strings, or variables can be encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM. Because Flow uses a text-safe armored envelope (FLOWENC:v1:<base64(...)>), encrypted payloads can be stored directly into standard database string columns without schema modifications:

  • dbo.flow_pipeline_content ([PipelineXML] NVARCHAR(MAX))
  • dbo.flow_options_content ([OptionsXML] NVARCHAR(MAX))
  • dbo.flow_config_content ([ConfigXML] NVARCHAR(MAX))

docs.title: Executing Encrypted Database Pipelines
docs.text:
At runtime, specify the -encrypted flag and provide the decryption key via -secure-key or the FLOW_SECURE_KEY environment variable:

flow.exe -encrypted -secure-key "MySecretPassphrase123!" \
         -file "sql://sqlserver@localhost:1433?database=master#SELECT PipelineXML FROM dbo.flow_pipeline_content WHERE Name = 'production_daily_etl'"

If the stored record begins with FLOWENC:v1:, Flow will automatically detect and decrypt the payload before parsing and execution.

For detailed table schemas, SQL Server merge queries, and tooling, refer to: * Database-backed Resource Storage Guide * Cross-Platform Encryption Guide * Database Importer Documentation

docs.title: Database Connection Strings & Driver Reference Guide 🔌
docs.text: This guide provides a comprehensive reference of all supported database drivers in go-flow, detailing every available connection string format, query parameter, security setting, and performance tuning option. It includes practical examples for local development, enterprise production, cloud-managed instances, mutual TLS, and high-throughput ETL pipelines.

docs.title: 1. Driver Overview & Comparison Matrix
docs.text:
The table below outlines each database and storage engine supported by go-flow, the registered driver aliases, default network ports, URI schemes, and supported operational capabilities.

Database / Engine Driver Aliases Underlying Go Library Default Port Primary DSN Schemes Key Capabilities Safe Default Example PostgreSQL postgrespostgresqlpq github.com/lib/pq 5432 postgresql://postgres://host=... (Key-Value) Full SSL/TLS (mTLS), schema search_path, session timeouts, binary parameters, connection keepalives postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/mydb?sslmode=disable MySQL & MariaDB mysql github.com/go-sql-driver/mysql 3306 user:pass@tcp(host:port)/dbuser:pass@unix(socket)/db Datetime parsing (parseTime), TLS/SSL, bulk parameter interpolation (interpolateParams), multi-statements, packet sizing user:pass@tcp(localhost:3306)/mydb?parseTime=true&loc=UTC Microsoft SQL Server & Azure SQL sqlservermssqlazuresql github.com/microsoft/go-mssqldb(incl. /azuread) 1433 sqlserver://server=...; (ADO.NET) TLS encryption, self-signed cert trust, named instances, Kerberos/AD auth, Microsoft Entra (fedauth), MultiSubnetFailover (Always On AG), packet sizing (packet size), MARS sqlserver://sa:pass@localhost:1433?database=mydb&encrypt=disable SQLite sqlitesqlite3 modernc.org/sqlite N/A file:...:memory:/path/to/file.db Pure Go (zero CGO), WAL journal mode, busy timeouts, RAM caches, shared in-memory caches, read-only immutable mounts file:app.db?cache=shared&mode=rwc&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL) Oracle Database oraclegodror github.com/sijms/go-ora/v2 1521 oracle://user/pass@host:port/svc Pure Go (zero Oracle Client/OCI), Service Names & SIDs, Oracle Cloud Wallets (mTLS), bulk prefetch tuning oracle://user:pass@localhost:1521/XEPDB1 Redis & Valkey redisvalkey github.com/redis/go-redis/v9 6379 redis://rediss:// (TLS)host:port In-memory key-value, pipelines, TLS verification, connection pooling, DB indexes redis://:password@localhost:6379/0?dial_timeout=5s bbolt bboltbolt go.etcd.io/bbolt N/A /path/to/cache.db./store.db Embedded ACID transactions, lock timeouts, POSIX file permissions ./data/cache.db?timeout=1s BadgerDB badgerbadgerdb github.com/dgraph-io/badger/v4 N/A /path/to/dirbadger://:memory: Pure Go LSM-tree KV, fast sequential writes, in-memory mode, Snappy compression ./data/badger_data?sync_writes=false etcd (v3) etcdetcdv3 go.etcd.io/etcd/client/v3 2379 http://host:port,...https://host:port (TLS) Distributed consensus KV, multi-endpoint failover, client certificate authentication http://127.0.0.1:2379,http://127.0.0.1:22379

[!IMPORTANT] XML Entity Escaping: When defining connection strings inside XML pipeline files (<database connection_string="..." />) or options files (<options><dsn>...</dsn></options>), all literal ampersands (&) separating URL query parameters must be escaped as &. * Example: postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/db?sslmode=disable&connect_timeout=10

docs.title: 2. Common Parameter Comparison Matrix
docs.text:
The following table summarizes common operational categories and how they are configured across the relational SQL drivers:

docs.title: 3. PostgreSQL
docs.text: The PostgreSQL driver (github.com/lib/pq) supports two distinct connection string formats: URI format (postgresql://...) and Key-Value format (host=... port=...).

docs.title: Available Options Reference
docs.text: Parameter Type Allowed Values / Format Description sslmode string disable, require, verify-ca, verify-full Determines TLS verification rigor. disable skips encryption; require encrypts without CA validation; verify-full validates server certificate hostname against CA. sslrootcert path Absolute or relative path to CA certificate Root CA certificate file (PEM format) used to verify server identity. sslcert path Absolute or relative path to client cert Client certificate file (PEM format) for mutual authentication (mTLS). sslkey path Absolute or relative path to client private key Client private key file (PEM format, must have restricted POSIX permissions 0600). connect_timeout integer Number of seconds (e.g. 10) Maximum wait time for connection establishment before failing. 0 disables timeout. statement_timeout integer Milliseconds (e.g. 30000) Aborts any SQL statement that takes longer than the specified number of milliseconds. application_name string Text identifier (e.g. flow_etl_worker) Sets the application name displayed in pg_stat_activity for auditing and DBA monitoring. fallback_application_name string Text identifier Fallback application name if application_name is not specified. search_path string Comma-separated schemas (e.g. analytics,public) Configures the schema search order for unqualified table and view references. timezone string Time zone identifier (e.g. UTC, America/New_York) Sets the session TimeZone configuration variable. client_encoding string Character encoding (e.g. UTF8) Configures the character encoding of SQL statements and returned results. binary_parameters string yes, no When set to yes, sends parameters in binary format for improved transmission speed. keepalives integer 1 (enable) or 0 (disable) Controls whether client-side TCP keepalives are enabled. keepalives_idle integer Seconds Number of seconds of inactivity before sending a keepalive probe. keepalives_interval integer Seconds Interval in seconds between keepalive retransmissions. keepalives_count integer Integer count Number of unacknowledged keepalive probes before dropping connection. sslsni integer 1 (default) or 0 Enables or disables Server Name Indication (SNI) during TLS handshake.

docs.title: Example 1: Local Development (Plaintext / No SSL)
docs.text:
postgresql://postgres:localDevPass123@localhost:5432/app_db?sslmode=disable
Equivalent Key-Value format: 
host=localhost port=5432 user=postgres password=localDevPass123 dbname=app_db sslmode=disable

docs.title: Example 2: Production Cloud Database (AWS RDS / GCP Cloud SQL / Neon / Supabase)
docs.text:
Requires TLS encryption with connection timeout and UTC session timezone: 

postgresql://app_user:StrongProdPass2026!@db.internal.company.com:5432/analytics_prod?sslmode=require&connect_timeout=10&timezone=UTC&application_name=flow_pipeline
XML pipeline syntax (note the escaped &): 
<database name="analytics_db"
          driver="postgres"
          connection_string="postgresql://app_user:StrongProdPass2026!@db.internal.company.com:5432/analytics_prod?sslmode=require&connect_timeout=10&timezone=UTC&application_name=flow_pipeline" />

docs.title: Example 3: High-Security Mutual TLS (mTLS) with Root CA Verification
docs.text:
Validates the server certificate against a custom root certificate authority and authenticates the client using client certificates: 

host=secure-db.internal port=5432 user=etl_service dbname=finance sslmode=verify-full sslrootcert=/etc/ssl/certs/internal_ca.pem sslcert=/etc/ssl/certs/etl_client.pem sslkey=/etc/ssl/certs/etl_client_key.pem connect_timeout=15

docs.title: Example 4: Schema Isolation with Search Path & Statement Guardrails
docs.text:
Directs queries to the staging schema first and aborts long-running statements after 60 seconds: 

postgresql://loader:SecretPass@db.internal:5432/warehouse?sslmode=require&search_path=staging,shared,public&statement_timeout=60000&application_name=batch_loader

docs.title: Example 5: High-Speed Local Unix Domain Socket
docs.text:
Avoids loopback TCP stack overhead on Linux / macOS servers: 

host=/var/run/postgresql user=postgres dbname=app_db sslmode=disable

docs.title: 4. MySQL & MariaDB
docs.text:
The MySQL driver (github.com/go-sql-driver/mysql) uses Data Source Names (DSNs) structured as: 

[username[:password]@][protocol[(address)]]/dbname[?param1=value1&param2=value2]

docs.title: Available Options Reference
docs.text: Parameter Type Allowed Values / Format Description parseTime boolean true, false (default false) Automatically parses DATE and DATETIME columns into Go time.Time values instead of raw []byte. Essential for ETL pipelines. loc string Local, UTC, or URL-encoded IANA location (e.g. America%2FNew_York) Sets the timezone location used when parsing datetime values. tls string false, true, skip-verify, preferred, or custom profile name false disables TLS; true requires valid server cert; skip-verify enables TLS but skips certificate chain verification (useful for self-signed certificates). timeout duration Duration string (e.g. 5s, 10s) Timeout for establishing the network connection (dial timeout). readTimeout duration Duration string (e.g. 30s, 1m) I/O read timeout on established connections. writeTimeout duration Duration string (e.g. 30s, 1m) I/O write timeout on established connections. interpolateParams boolean true, false (default false) Interpolates placeholders client-side into a single query string instead of preparing separate statements. Significantly accelerates bulk inserts and batch updates. multiStatements boolean true, false (default false) Allows executing multiple semicolon-delimited SQL statements in a single query call (e.g. DDL scripts, multi-table transactions). collation string MySQL Collation name (e.g. utf8mb4_unicode_ci, utf8mb4_general_ci) Sets the character set collation for client communication. charset string Charset name (e.g. utf8mb4, utf8) Sets the connection character set. maxAllowedPacket integer Size in bytes (e.g. 67108864 for 64MB) Sets maximum packet size accepted from the MySQL server. clientFoundRows boolean true, false (default false) Returns matching rows instead of changed rows for UPDATE statements. allowNativePasswords boolean true, false (default true) Allows the mysql_native_password authentication method. checkConnLiveness boolean true, false (default true) Performs connection health check before executing queries. autocommit boolean true, false (default true) Controls automatic transaction commitment.

docs.title: Example 1: Standard Local Development (TCP with Datetime Parsing)
docs.text: root:localPassword123@tcp(localhost:3306)/flow_data?parseTime=true&loc=Local

docs.title: Example 2: High-Performance Bulk ETL Pipeline
docs.text:
Enables parameter interpolation for rapid bulk insertions, 64MB packet buffers, and explicit I/O timeouts: 

etl_writer:ETLSecretPass2026!@tcp(db-cluster.internal:3306)/sales_warehouse?parseTime=true&loc=UTC&interpolateParams=true&maxAllowedPacket=67108864&timeout=10s&readTimeout=60s&writeTimeout=60s
XML pipeline syntax (with escaped &): 
<database name="sales_warehouse"
          driver="mysql"
          connection_string="etl_writer:ETLSecretPass2026!@tcp(db-cluster.internal:3306)/sales_warehouse?parseTime=true&loc=UTC&interpolateParams=true&maxAllowedPacket=67108864&timeout=10s&readTimeout=60s&writeTimeout=60s" />

docs.title: Example 3: Cloud Database with Managed SSL / Self-Signed Skip-Verify
docs.text:
Suitable for Amazon RDS, Google Cloud SQL, or DigitalOcean Managed MySQL when intermediate CA certs are not locally configured: 

app_service:ProdPassword99@tcp(mysql-master.c7xyz.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com:3306)/production?parseTime=true&loc=UTC&tls=skip-verify&timeout=15s

docs.title: Example 4: Local High-Speed Unix Domain Socket
docs.text:
Directly connects to local daemon via Unix socket without TCP networking: 

flow_user:Pass123!@unix(/var/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock)/production_db?parseTime=true&loc=UTC

docs.title: Example 5: Migration Runner (Multi-Statement Support)
docs.text:
Enables running multi-statement schema migration files containing semicolons: 

admin_user:AdminPass123@tcp(127.0.0.1:3306)/app_schema?multiStatements=true&parseTime=true

docs.title: Example 6: IPv6 Loopback Connection
docs.text: flow_app:MyPassword@tcp([::1]:3306)/ipv6_test?parseTime=true

docs.title: 5. Microsoft SQL Server & Azure SQL
docs.text: The Microsoft SQL Server driver (github.com/microsoft/go-mssqldb) supports both URL format (sqlserver://...) and ADO.NET / ODBC semi-colon key-value format (server=...;database=...;).

docs.title: Available Options Reference
docs.text: Parameter (URL / ADO.NET) Type Allowed Values / Format Description database string Database name Target database / catalog name to switch to upon connecting. encrypt string / bool true, false, disable true enforces TLS/SSL encryption; disable or false allows unencrypted connections. TrustServerCertificatetrustservercertificate boolean true, false (default false) When set to true, trusts self-signed server certificates without CA validation. Essential for local Docker or test instances. connection timeout integer Seconds (e.g. 15) Connection establishment timeout. app nameapplication name string String identifier (e.g. Flow_ETL_Service) Surfaces client application name in SQL Server dynamic management views (sys.dm_exec_sessions). workstation id string Hostname (e.g. ETL-NODE-01) Workstation identifier logged in SQL Server connection telemetry. packet size integer Bytes (512 to 32767, default 4096) Network Packet Size (TDS buffer). Setting to 32767 significantly accelerates high-volume ETL bulk copies. multisubnetfailoverMultiSubnetFailover boolean true, false, Enabled, Disabled When true, connects in parallel to all IP addresses resolved for an Always On Availability Group listener across multi-subnet clusters. applicationintentApplicationIntent string ReadOnly, ReadWrite Directs read-only queries to secondary replicas in Always On Availability Group configurations (requires database parameter). MultipleActiveResultSetsmars boolean true, false Enables Multiple Active Result Sets (MARS) on a single connection. failoverpartner string Hostname or IP of mirror server Specifies the database mirroring or Always On Availability Group failover partner. keepAlive integer Seconds (default 30) Frequency of TCP keep-alive packets sent to detect dead connections. log integer Integer bitmask (e.g. 63) Enables internal driver logging to standard error for troubleshooting connection negotiation. fedauth string ActiveDirectoryIntegratedActiveDirectoryDefaultActiveDirectoryMSIActiveDirectoryServicePrincipalActiveDirectoryInteractiveActiveDirectoryPassword Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) authentication workflow. applicationclientid string UUID (Client / Application ID) Azure Client ID required for ActiveDirectoryPassword and ActiveDirectoryInteractive. clientcertpath path File path to .pem certificate Certificate path for certificate-based Service Principal authentication. resource id string Azure Resource ID Azure resource ID when using User-Assigned Managed Identity (ActiveDirectoryMSI). additionallyallowedtenants string Comma-separated tenant IDs Allowed additional tenant IDs for multi-tenant Microsoft Entra authentication. integrated security string / bool true, sspi Uses Windows Integrated Authentication (SSPI / Kerberos) under on-premises Windows Active Directory.

docs.title: Example 1: Local Development / Docker (Plaintext Encryption Disabled)
docs.text:
sqlserver://sa:YourStrongPassword123!@localhost:1433?database=master&encrypt=disable
Equivalent ADO.NET key-value format: 
server=localhost;port=1433;user id=sa;password=YourStrongPassword123!;database=master;encrypt=disable;

docs.title: Example 2: Local Staging with Self-Signed Certificate
docs.text:
Enables TLS encryption while instructing the client to trust the self-signed certificate: 

sqlserver://sa:YourStrongPassword123!@localhost:1433?database=telemetry&encrypt=true&TrustServerCertificate=true
XML pipeline syntax (note the escaped &): 
<database name="telemetry_db"
          driver="sqlserver"
          connection_string="sqlserver://sa:YourStrongPassword123!@localhost:1433?database=telemetry&encrypt=true&TrustServerCertificate=true" />

docs.title: Example 3: Azure SQL Database (SQL Authentication)
docs.text:
Azure SQL requires encryption enabled and authenticates using username and server suffix: 

sqlserver://appadmin@my-sql-srv:ComplexAzurePass999!@my-sql-srv.database.windows.net:1433?database=enterprise_db&encrypt=true&connection+timeout=30&app+name=Flow_Pipeline

docs.title: Example 4: Named Instance Connection
docs.text:
Connects to a specific named instance (e.g. SQLEXPRESS or REPORTING): 

sqlserver://sa:StrongPass123!@db-host\SQLEXPRESS?database=orders&encrypt=disable
ADO.NET format: 
server=db-host\SQLEXPRESS;user id=sa;password=StrongPass123!;database=orders;encrypt=disable;

docs.title: Example 5: High-Throughput Bulk ETL (Max TDS Packet Size)
docs.text:
Tunes network TDS buffers from the 4KB default to 32KB (32767 bytes) to maximize network throughput during large data warehouse bulk copies, and logs workstation identity:

URL format (spaces encoded as + or %20): 

sqlserver://etl_operator:SecretPass2026!@sql-cluster.internal:1433?database=staging_area&encrypt=true&TrustServerCertificate=true&packet+size=32767&app+name=Flow_Bulk_Loader&workstation+id=ETL-HOST-01

Equivalent ADO.NET semi-colon format: 

server=sql-cluster.internal;port=1433;user id=etl_operator;password=SecretPass2026!;database=staging_area;encrypt=true;TrustServerCertificate=true;packet size=32767;app name=Flow_Bulk_Loader;workstation id=ETL-HOST-01;

XML pipeline definition (note the escaped &): 

<database name="bulk_staging_db"
          driver="sqlserver"
          connection_string="sqlserver://etl_operator:SecretPass2026!@sql-cluster.internal:1433?database=staging_area&encrypt=true&TrustServerCertificate=true&packet+size=32767&app+name=Flow_Bulk_Loader&workstation+id=ETL-HOST-01"
          max_open_conns="50"
          max_idle_conns="10" />

docs.title: Example 6: On-Premises Windows Integrated Authentication (Kerberos / NTLM)
docs.text:
Uses current on-premises Windows domain logon credentials without storing passwords in configuration files: 

server=localhost;database=finance;integrated security=true;

docs.title: Example 7: Multi-Subnet Failover (Always On Availability Groups)
docs.text:
In SQL Server Always On Availability Group (AG) architectures spanning multiple subnets or disaster recovery data centers, an AG listener registers multiple IP addresses in DNS. Setting MultiSubnetFailover=true instructs the driver to attempt parallel TCP connections to all resolved IP addresses simultaneously. Whichever replica answers first (the currently active primary or secondary node) wins the connection immediately—slashing failover discovery time from standard 20–30 second TCP timeout delays to milliseconds.

Combine with ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly to offload analytical or reporting queries directly to secondary read-only replicas:

URL format: 

sqlserver://app_etl:SecurePassword2026!@ag-listener.corp.internal:1433?database=enterprise_reporting&multisubnetfailover=true&applicationintent=ReadOnly&encrypt=true&TrustServerCertificate=true

Equivalent ADO.NET semi-colon format: 

server=ag-listener.corp.internal;database=enterprise_reporting;user id=app_etl;password=SecurePassword2026!;MultiSubnetFailover=True;ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly;encrypt=true;TrustServerCertificate=true;

XML pipeline definition: 

<database name="ag_reporting_db"
          driver="sqlserver"
          connection_string="sqlserver://app_etl:SecurePassword2026!@ag-listener.corp.internal:1433?database=enterprise_reporting&multisubnetfailover=true&applicationintent=ReadOnly&encrypt=true&TrustServerCertificate=true"
          max_open_conns="20"
          max_idle_conns="5"
          workload="analytics" />

docs.title: Example 8: Multiple Active Result Sets (MARS)
docs.text:
Multiple Active Result Sets (MARS) allows executing multiple batches or interleaving queries across a single physical database connection without buffering the entire result set in client memory before issuing another command on that connection.

URL format: 

sqlserver://flow_app:OrderPass2026!@sql-srv.internal:1433?database=order_processing&MultipleActiveResultSets=true&encrypt=true&TrustServerCertificate=true

Equivalent ADO.NET semi-colon format: 

server=sql-srv.internal;database=order_processing;user id=flow_app;password=OrderPass2026!;MultipleActiveResultSets=True;encrypt=true;TrustServerCertificate=true;

XML pipeline definition: 

<database name="orders_mars_db"
          driver="sqlserver"
          connection_string="sqlserver://flow_app:OrderPass2026!@sql-srv.internal:1433?database=order_processing&MultipleActiveResultSets=true&encrypt=true&TrustServerCertificate=true" />

[!NOTE] Go Concurrency vs. MARS: In Go's database/sql, concurrent queries dispatched across goroutines automatically receive separate physical connections managed by the connection pool (max_open_conns). For single queries or stored procedures returning multiple result sets (e.g. SELECT * FROM headers; SELECT * FROM lines;), Go processes each result set sequentially using rows.NextResultSet() natively. Specifying MultipleActiveResultSets=True is primarily utilized when porting legacy .NET connection strings, connecting through proxies that require the MARS prelogin flag, or when integrating with frameworks expecting MARS-enabled endpoints.

docs.title: Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) Connection Examples
docs.text: go-flow provides native support for Microsoft Entra ID authentication (via github.com/microsoft/go-mssqldb/azuread). You can specify the driver as either azuresql or sqlserver (Flow automatically routes connection strings containing fedauth= to the Entra ID token provider).

docs.title: Example 9: Microsoft Entra Integrated Authentication (Single Sign-On / SSO)
docs.text:
Microsoft Entra Integrated (fedauth=ActiveDirectoryIntegrated) is designed for machines that are domain-joined to on-premises Active Directory federated with Microsoft Entra ID, or joined directly via Microsoft Entra Hybrid Join. It uses the active Windows session ticket via Kerberos/WS-Trust to seamlessly negotiate an Entra access token without requiring passwords or secrets in configuration files.

URL format: 

sqlserver://my-sql-srv.database.windows.net?database=sales_analytics&fedauth=ActiveDirectoryIntegrated&encrypt=true

ADO.NET semi-colon format: 

server=my-sql-srv.database.windows.net;database=sales_analytics;fedauth=ActiveDirectoryIntegrated;encrypt=true;

Standard ODBC / ADO.NET alias syntax: 

server=my-sql-srv.database.windows.net;database=sales_analytics;Authentication=Active Directory Integrated;encrypt=true;

XML pipeline definition (using either driver="azuresql" or driver="sqlserver"): 

<database name="sales_dw"
          driver="azuresql"
          connection_string="sqlserver://my-sql-srv.database.windows.net?database=sales_analytics&fedauth=ActiveDirectoryIntegrated&encrypt=true"
          max_open_conns="25"
          max_idle_conns="5"
          workload="analytics" />

CLI execution: 

.\flow.exe -dsn "sqlserver://my-sql-srv.database.windows.net?database=sales_analytics&fedauth=ActiveDirectoryIntegrated&encrypt=true"

docs.title: Example 10: Microsoft Entra Default (DefaultAzureCredential)
docs.text:
Uses the Azure SDK DefaultAzureCredential provider. It dynamically resolves credentials from: 1. Environment variables (AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET) 2. Workload Identity (AKS / Kubernetes pod service accounts) 3. Managed Identity (Azure VMs, Azure Container Apps, Azure App Services) 4. Azure Developer CLI (az login or azd login) 5. Visual Studio Code credentials

URL format: 

sqlserver://my-sql-srv.database.windows.net?database=enterprise_dw&fedauth=ActiveDirectoryDefault&encrypt=true

XML pipeline definition: 

<database name="azure_dw"
          driver="azuresql"
          connection_string="sqlserver://my-sql-srv.database.windows.net?database=enterprise_dw&fedauth=ActiveDirectoryDefault&encrypt=true" />

docs.title: Example 11: Microsoft Entra Managed Identity (System-Assigned & User-Assigned MSI)
docs.text:
Ideal for automated workloads running on Azure Virtual Machines, Azure Functions, Azure Container Instances (ACI), or Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS).

System-Assigned Managed Identity: 

sqlserver://my-sql-srv.database.windows.net?database=finance&fedauth=ActiveDirectoryMSI&encrypt=true

User-Assigned Managed Identity (specifying Client ID): 

sqlserver://my-sql-srv.database.windows.net?database=finance&fedauth=ActiveDirectoryMSI&user+id=11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555&encrypt=true

User-Assigned Managed Identity (specifying Resource ID): 

server=my-sql-srv.database.windows.net;database=finance;fedauth=ActiveDirectoryMSI;resource id=/subscriptions/sub-id/resourceGroups/rg-name/providers/Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities/my-identity;encrypt=true;

docs.title: Example 12: Microsoft Entra Service Principal (Headless CI/CD & Automated ETL)
docs.text:
Used when ETL pipelines run unattended outside Azure (e.g. on-premises data centers, AWS, GCP, or automated Jenkins/GitHub Actions runners).

With Client Secret: 

server=my-sql-srv.database.windows.net;database=warehouse;fedauth=ActiveDirectoryServicePrincipal;user id=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000@tenant-uuid-1234;password=YourClientSecretKey!;encrypt=true;
URL equivalent: 
sqlserver://00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000@tenant-uuid-1234:YourClientSecretKey!@my-sql-srv.database.windows.net?database=warehouse&fedauth=ActiveDirectoryServicePrincipal&encrypt=true

With Client Certificate (mTLS with Microsoft Entra): 

server=my-sql-srv.database.windows.net;database=warehouse;fedauth=ActiveDirectoryServicePrincipal;user id=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000@tenant-uuid-1234;clientcertpath=/etc/ssl/certs/service_principal.pem;encrypt=true;

docs.title: Example 13: Microsoft Entra Interactive (Browser MFA Prompt)
docs.text:
Prompts the operator with an interactive browser or MFA authenticator prompt. Recommended for local developer workstations using Builder UI: 

sqlserver://admin@company.com@my-sql-srv.database.windows.net?database=dev_db&fedauth=ActiveDirectoryInteractive&applicationclientid=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000&encrypt=true

docs.title: Example 14: Microsoft Entra Password (ROPC Flow)
docs.text:
Authenticates with an Entra username and password directly (non-MFA accounts only): 

sqlserver://user@company.com:MyEntraPass2026!@my-sql-srv.database.windows.net?database=staging&fedauth=ActiveDirectoryPassword&applicationclientid=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000&encrypt=true

docs.title: 6. SQLite
docs.text: go-flow utilizes modernc.org/sqlite, a 100% pure Go SQLite engine that requires no CGO and no external C compiler. Connections are specified using standard filesystem paths or URI syntax.

docs.title: Available Options & Pragmas Reference
docs.text: Parameter / Pragma Type Allowed Values / Format Description mode string ro (read-only)rw (read-write)rwc (read-write-create)memory (in-memory) Access mode for opening database files. rwc creates the file if it does not already exist. cache string shared, private Controls shared-cache mode among multiple connections within the same process. immutable integer 1, 0 Informs SQLite that the underlying file is on read-only media and will never be modified.
