Skips all locking and shared memory. _pragma=journal_mode(...) pragma WAL, DELETE, TRUNCATE, MEMORY, OFF WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) provides maximum concurrency, allowing readers and writers to operate simultaneously without locking. _pragma=synchronous(...) pragma NORMAL, FULL, OFF In WAL mode, NORMAL ensures database durability across application crashes while dramatically speeding up write transactions. _pragma=busy_timeout(...) pragma Milliseconds (e.g. 5000) Sleep time before returning SQLITE_BUSY when waiting for another write lock to release. _pragma=foreign_keys(...) pragma 1 (on), 0 (off) Enforces relational foreign key constraints. (SQLite defaults to off). _pragma=temp_store(...) pragma MEMORY, FILE, DEFAULT Stores temporary tables and scratch query sorting indexes in RAM instead of disk files. _pragma=cache_size(...) pragma Negative integer (e.g. -64000 = 64MB) Sets the memory page cache allocated to the connection handle. _pragma=locking_mode(...) pragma NORMAL, EXCLUSIVE EXCLUSIVE retains database file locks for the lifetime of the connection to maximize write throughput in single-process ETL. _pragma=mmap_size(...) pragma Bytes (e.g. 268435456 = 256MB) Enables memory-mapped I/O up to the specified size for ultra-fast reading.

docs.title: Example 1: High-Performance Production File (WAL Mode)
docs.text:
Configures Write-Ahead Logging, 5-second lock timeout, RAM temp storage, and 64MB memory page cache: 

file:./data/production.db?cache=shared&mode=rwc&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)&_pragma=synchronous(NORMAL)&_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)&_pragma=temp_store(MEMORY)&_pragma=cache_size(-64000)&_pragma=foreign_keys(1)
XML pipeline syntax (note the escaped &): 
<database name="local_warehouse"
          driver="sqlite"
          connection_string="file:./data/production.db?cache=shared&mode=rwc&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)&_pragma=synchronous(NORMAL)&_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)&_pragma=temp_store(MEMORY)&_pragma=cache_size(-64000)&_pragma=foreign_keys(1)" />

docs.title: Example 2: Simple Local File Path
docs.text:
Creates or connects to a local database file using default SQLite settings: 

./data/application.db
On Windows: 
C:\etl\databases\application.db

docs.title: Example 3: Shared In-Memory Database (Ephemeral)
docs.text:
Lives entirely in memory, persists across pipeline steps for the lifetime of the process, and is shared among all connection pool threads: 

file::memory:?cache=shared

docs.title: Example 4: Isolated In-Memory Database
docs.text: :memory:

docs.title: Example 5: Read-Only Immutable Database
docs.text:
Opens an existing reference database in strict read-only mode, bypassing all file lock overhead (ideal for Docker containers, read-only NFS volumes, or distribution bundles): 

file:/opt/data/geo_reference.db?mode=ro&immutable=1

docs.title: 7. Oracle Database
docs.text: The Oracle driver (github.com/sijms/go-ora/v2) is a pure Go Oracle client implementation. It connects directly to Oracle Database instances over TCP/IP without requiring Oracle Instant Client, CGO, or libclntsh.so.

docs.title: Available Options Reference
docs.text: Parameter Type Allowed Values / Format Description CONNECTION TIMEOUT / timeout integer Seconds (e.g. 10) TCP dial timeout before aborting connection attempts. SSL string ENABLE, TRUE, FALSE Enables SSL/TLS transport encryption (TCPS protocol). SSL VERIFY string TRUE, FALSE Validates server SSL certificate validity. Set to FALSE for self-signed certificates. WALLET path Path to Oracle Cloud Wallet (cwallet.sso or .zip) Points to client credentials wallet for Oracle Cloud Autonomous Databases (ATP / ADW). SERVER string DEDICATED, SHARED Instructs the Oracle TNS listener to assign a dedicated server process. AUTH TYPE string DEFAULT, SYSDBA, SYSOPER Privileged administrative logon mode. PREFETCH_ROWS integer Number of rows (e.g. 1000) Number of rows prefetched per network round-trip. Essential for large ETL SELECT queries. CLIENT IDENTIFIER string Text identifier (e.g. flow_etl) Client identity stored in V$SESSION for enterprise database auditing. TRACE FILE path File path (e.g. ./oracle_trace.log) Dumps internal TDS protocol packet traces for low-level debugging.

docs.title: Example 1: Standard Service Name Connection
docs.text:
Connects to an Oracle Pluggable Database (PDB) via Service Name: 

oracle://app_user:SecretPassword123@localhost:1521/XEPDB1

docs.title: Example 2: Legacy SID (System Identifier) Connection
docs.text:
Connects using an Oracle SID (e.g. ORCL): 

oracle://system:ManagerPassword@db-host.internal:1521/ORCL

docs.title: Example 3: High-Performance Bulk ETL with Prefetching
docs.text:
Configures dedicated server processes, 10-second timeout, and 2,500 row network prefetch buffers: 

oracle://etl_reader:ComplexPass999!@oracle-cluster.internal:1521/PROD_SVC?SERVER=DEDICATED&CONNECTION+TIMEOUT=10&PREFETCH_ROWS=2500&CLIENT+IDENTIFIER=Flow_ETL_Runner
XML pipeline syntax (note the escaped &): 
<database name="oracle_dw"
          driver="oracle"
          connection_string="oracle://etl_reader:ComplexPass999!@oracle-cluster.internal:1521/PROD_SVC?SERVER=DEDICATED&CONNECTION+TIMEOUT=10&PREFETCH_ROWS=2500&CLIENT+IDENTIFIER=Flow_ETL_Runner" />

docs.title: Example 4: Oracle Autonomous Cloud Database (ATP / ADW via Wallet)
docs.text:
Connects securely to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) using mutual TLS and the client wallet bundle: 

oracle://admin:MyCloudPassword123@adb.us-ashburn-1.oraclecloud.com:1522/myatp_high?SSL=ENABLE&WALLET=/etc/oracle/wallets/Wallet_myatp.zip

docs.title: Example 5: EZCONNECT Format
docs.text: scott/tiger@localhost:1521/XEPDB1

docs.title: 8. Key-Value Storage Engines
docs.text: In addition to relational SQL databases, go-flow includes first-class support for embedded and distributed Key-Value (KV) storage engines.

docs.title: Redis & Valkey
docs.text: Supports single-node instances, managed Redis caches (e.g. AWS ElastiCache, Azure Redis, Google Memorystore), and TLS-encrypted clusters.

docs.title: Format:
docs.text:
redis://[:password@]host[:port][/db_index][?param1=val1&param2=val2]
For TLS / SSL connections: 
rediss://[:password@]host[:port][/db_index][?param1=val1&param2=val2]

docs.title: Examples:
docs.text:
# Local unauthenticated Redis instance (Database 0)
redis://localhost:6379/0

# Authenticated Redis with password, custom database, and timeouts
redis://:SecretRedisPass2026!@redis.internal:6379/2?dial_timeout=5s&read_timeout=3s&write_timeout=3s

# Encrypted Redis over TLS (rediss://)
rediss://:SecurePass@redis-cache.us-east-1.cache.amazonaws.com:6379/0?dial_timeout=10s

docs.title: bbolt (Embedded KV)
docs.text: bbolt is an embedded, transactional key-value store stored in a single binary file.

docs.title: Format:
docs.text: /path/to/database.db[?timeout=duration&mode=octal]

docs.title: Examples:
docs.text:
# Standard local cache database file
./data/kv_cache.db

# With explicit lock acquisition timeout
./data/kv_cache.db?timeout=2s

docs.title: BadgerDB (Embedded LSM-Tree KV)
docs.text: BadgerDB is an embedded Key-Value engine optimized for solid-state storage (SSDs) using Log-Structured Merge (LSM) trees.

docs.title: Format:
docs.text:
/path/to/storage_directory[?sync_writes=bool]
For in-memory ephemeral KV store: 
badger://:memory:

docs.title: Examples:
docs.text:
# Local directory on SSD with asynchronous write-flushing for maximum ingestion throughput
./data/badger_store?sync_writes=false

# In-memory ephemeral KV store
badger://:memory:

docs.title: etcd (Distributed KV v3)
docs.text: Supports distributed configuration and consensus lookups across multi-node clusters.

docs.title: Format:
docs.text:
http://endpoint1:port,http://endpoint2:port
With client TLS certificates: 
https://etcd1.internal:2379,https://etcd2.internal:2379?ca_cert=/path/to/ca.pem&cert=/path/to/cert.pem&key=/path/to/key.pem

docs.title: Defining Databases in <pipeline> XML
docs.text:
Databases are registered in the <databases> block of a pipeline definition. Connection strings support variable interpolation (e.g. {{DB_PASSWORD}} or {{DB_HOST}}), enabling credentials to be injected securely at runtime without hardcoding.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">

    <databases>
        <!-- 1. PostgreSQL Data Warehouse -->
        <database name="dw_postgres"
                  driver="postgres"
                  connection_string="postgresql://etl_app:{{PG_PASSWORD}}@postgres.internal:5432/warehouse?sslmode=require&connect_timeout=10"
                  max_open_conns="50"
                  max_idle_conns="10"
                  conn_max_lifetime_seconds="300"
                  workload="bulk" />

        <!-- 2. SQL Server Source -->
        <database name="source_mssql"
                  driver="sqlserver"
                  connection_string="sqlserver://sa:{{MSSQL_PASSWORD}}@sql-srv.internal:1433?database=Orders&encrypt=true&TrustServerCertificate=true&packet+size=32767"
                  max_open_conns="25"
                  max_idle_conns="5"
                  workload="oltp" />

        <!-- 3. Local High-Throughput SQLite Staging -->
        <database name="staging_sqlite"
                  driver="sqlite"
                  connection_string="file:./scratch/staging.db?cache=shared&mode=rwc&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)&_pragma=synchronous(NORMAL)&_pragma=busy_timeout(10000)"
                  max_open_conns="1"
                  workload="batch" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <!-- Steps referencing registered databases by name -->
        <sql id="extract_orders" db="source_mssql">
            SELECT order_id, customer_id, total_amount FROM orders WHERE status = 'PENDING';
        </sql>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Telemetry & Execution Logging Database (log_db)
docs.text:
When a database element is named log_db, go-flow automatically directs all pipeline execution telemetry, step events, row counts, and database SPID tracking to that database:

<database name="log_db"
          driver="sqlserver"
          connection_string="sqlserver://telemetry_user:{{LOG_PASSWORD}}@telemetry.internal:1433?database=pipeline_telemetry&encrypt=true&TrustServerCertificate=true" />

docs.title: Loading Pipelines Directly from Databases (sql:// / db://)
docs.text:
go-flow can fetch pipeline XML definitions dynamically from a database repository using the sql:// source prefix:

sql://<driver>@<connection_string>#<SQL_SELECT_QUERY>

docs.title: Examples:
docs.text:
# From PostgreSQL
.\flow.exe -source "sql://postgres@postgresql://app:SecretPass@localhost:5432/pipelines?sslmode=disable#SELECT xml_content FROM pipeline_catalog WHERE pipeline_name = 'daily_sales'"

# From SQL Server
.\flow.exe -source "sql://sqlserver@sqlserver://sa:SecretPass!@localhost:1433?database=master&encrypt=disable#SELECT definition_xml FROM dbo.etl_scripts WHERE id = 42"

# From SQLite
.\flow.exe -source "sql://sqlite@file:./repos/scripts.db?mode=ro#SELECT xml_body FROM registry WHERE name = 'extract_orders'"

docs.title: 10. Security Best Practices for Connection Strings
docs.text:
1. Never Hardcode Plaintext Passwords in Version Control:
  2. Use variable substitution: connection_string="postgresql://app:{{SECRET_DB_PASS}}@host:5432/db".
  3. Pass runtime values using -var SECRET_DB_PASS=MyPassword or environment variables FLOW_VAR_SECRET_DB_PASS=MyPassword.
  4. Encrypt Options and Pipeline Files:
  5. Use crypto_tool to encrypt options and pipeline files with AES-256-GCM.
  6. Supply decryption keys via -key-file to prevent credentials from being exposed in system process listings (ps or Process Hacker).
  7. Always Escape Ampersands in XML:
  8. Remember that XML parsers reject bare & characters in attribute values. Always write & when joining query parameters inside <database connection_string="..." />.
  9. Enforce TLS Verification in Production:
  10. For PostgreSQL: Use sslmode=verify-full or sslmode=verify-ca.
  11. For MySQL: Use tls=true or registered CA bundles.
  12. For SQL Server: Use encrypt=true and avoid TrustServerCertificate=true in untrusted networks.
  13. Tune Connection Pool Sizes for ETL:
  14. Avoid setting max_open_conns excessively high when executing parallel pipelines against shared databases.
  15. For SQLite, set max_open_conns="1" or use WAL mode (_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)) to avoid database lock contention.

docs.title: Database Query to Template and Standard I/O (os.stdio) Output
docs.text: This guide explains how to query a database, format result rows using the <template> engine, and stream the rendered output directly to standard output (os.stdio / os.Stdout) in Flow.

docs.title: Pattern Overview
docs.text:
The Query $\rightarrow$ Template $\rightarrow$ Stdio pattern decouples data extraction, presentation formatting, and stream writing:

flowchart LR
    DB[(Database)] -->|Streaming Cursor| Foreach["<foreach><br/>Row Iteration"]
    Foreach -->|Exposes Row Columns as Variables| Template["<template><br/>Go text/template Engine"]
    Template -->|Writes to output_var| Script["<script language='go'><br/>host/vars & os.Stdout"]
    Script -->|Direct Stream| Stdio["Standard Output<br/>(os.stdio / Console)"]
  1. Database Cursor (<foreach>): Executes the SQL query and processes rows iteratively with constant $O(1)$ RAM usage.
  2. Variable Binding: In each loop iteration, all columns in the row (e.g. id, name, salary) are automatically exposed as in-scope pipeline variables.
  3. Template Formatting (<template>): The row variables are interpolated into custom text formats using Go's text/template engine and saved to a target variable (output_var).
  4. Standard I/O Writing (<script>): An embedded Go script imports "host/vars" and "os" to write the formatted string directly to os.Stdout.

docs.title: Complete Pipeline Example
docs.text:
The pipeline below is available in the repository at examples/db_select_template_stdio.xml.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">

    <!-- 1. Pipeline Variables -->
    <variables>
        <variable name="DBPath" type="string" value="./demo_employees.db" />
        <variable name="MinSalary" type="float" value="100000.00" />
    </variables>

    <!-- 2. Database Connection Definition
         Uses SQLite for an immediately runnable, zero-dependency local example.
         For other engines, see the connection string section below.
    -->
    <databases>
        <database name="sample_db" driver="sqlite" connection_string="{{DBPath}}" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <!-- 3. Setup Sample Table and Data (Self-contained demonstration) -->
        <sql id="InitSampleData" db="sample_db">
            <![CDATA[
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS employees (
                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
                    name TEXT NOT NULL,
                    department TEXT NOT NULL,
                    salary REAL NOT NULL
                );
                DELETE FROM employees;
                INSERT INTO employees (id, name, department, salary) VALUES
                    (101, 'Alice Smith', 'Engineering', 125000.50),
                    (102, 'Bob Jones', 'Data Science', 118000.00),
                    (103, 'Carol White', 'DevOps', 132500.75);
            ]]>
        </sql>

        <!-- 4. Query Database and Iterate Over Rows in a Streaming Foreach Loop -->
        <foreach id="SelectEmployees" db="sample_db">
            <![CDATA[
                SELECT id, name, department, salary
                FROM employees
                WHERE salary >= {{MinSalary}}
                ORDER BY id;
            ]]>

            <!-- 5. Render Row Data into a Variable Using Go text/template -->
            <template id="FormatEmployeeRow" output_var="FormattedRow">
==================================================
Employee ID: {{.id}}
Name:        {{.name}}
Department:  {{.department}}
Salary:      ${{.salary}}
==================================================
            </template>

            <!-- 6. Print Formatted Output Directly to Standard Output (os.stdio / os.Stdout) -->
            <script id="PrintToStdio" language="go">
                <![CDATA[
                package main

                import (
                    "fmt"
                    "os"
                    "host/vars"
                )

                func main() {
                    // Fetch the rendered template text from pipeline variables
                    rowText := vars.GetString("FormattedRow")

                    // Output directly to os.Stdout (os.stdio)
                    fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, rowText)
                }
                ]]>
            </script>
        </foreach>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: 1. Database Configuration (<databases>)
docs.text:
The example uses SQLite for immediate, zero-dependency execution. You can target any supported database engine by updating the driver and connection_string attributes:

<!-- SQL Server -->
<database name="sample_db" driver="sqlserver" 
          connection_string="sqlserver://dbhost:1433?database=Production&integrated+security=true&trustServerCertificate=true" />

<!-- PostgreSQL -->
<database name="sample_db" driver="postgres" 
          connection_string="postgres://app_user:secret@localhost:5432/production?sslmode=disable" />

<!-- MySQL -->
<database name="sample_db" driver="mysql" 
          connection_string="app_user:secret@tcp(localhost:3306)/production" />

<!-- Oracle -->
<database name="sample_db" driver="oracle" 
          connection_string="oracle://app_user:secret@localhost:1521/ORCLPDB1" />

docs.title: 2. Streaming Query (<foreach>)
docs.text:
The <foreach> container executes the SQL query in streaming mode:

  • Query results are streamed row-by-row rather than loading the entire result set into memory.
  • Columns returned by the SELECT clause are automatically registered as current-row variables accessible inside the loop body.
  • Variable interpolation ({{MinSalary}}) allows parameterized filtering directly within the query.

docs.title: 3. Template Engine (<template>)
docs.text:
The <template> node leverages Go's standard text/template library:

  • Variable Access: Row columns are accessed using dot notation ({{.id}}, {{.name}}, {{.department}}, {{.salary}}).
  • Conditionals & Logic: Native Go template directives such as {{if .department}}...{{else}}...{{end}} can be used.
  • output_var: Defines the pipeline variable where the rendered text string is stored.

docs.title: 4. Printing to os.stdio (<script language="go">)
docs.text:
The embedded Go script provides direct access to operating system file descriptors and standard streams:

  • "host/vars": Built-in host integration package that exposes pipeline variables to the script runtime. Use vars.GetString("FormattedRow") to retrieve the template output.
  • "os" & "fmt": Standard Go packages. fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, rowText) or os.Stdout.WriteString(rowText + "\n") flushes the rendered text to standard output (os.stdio).

docs.title: Alternative Script Languages
docs.text: While Go is fast and portable with zero external interpreter dependencies, the print step can also be written in other supported scripting languages:

docs.title: PowerShell
docs.text:
<script id="PrintStdio" language="powershell">
    Write-Host "{{FormattedRow}}"
</script>

docs.title: Bash / Linux Shell
docs.text:
<script id="PrintStdio" language="bash">
    echo "$FormattedRow"
</script>

docs.title: Windows Command Prompt (cmd)
docs.text:
<script id="PrintStdio" language="cmd">
    echo {{FormattedRow}}
</script>

docs.title: Running from the Command Line
docs.text:
Run the example using flow.exe:

.\flow.exe -file .\examples\db_select_template_stdio.xml

docs.title: Overriding Parameters at Runtime
docs.text:
Override variables on the command line without modifying the XML file:

.\flow.exe -file .\examples\db_select_template_stdio.xml -vars "MinSalary=125000.00"

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
[!TIP] Use CDATA Blocks for SQL & Scripts: Wrapping queries and script code inside <![CDATA[ ... ]]> avoids XML entity escaping issues with characters like <, >, &, or &&.

[!NOTE] Memory Efficiency: The <foreach> node uses a streaming cursor by default. Even when iterating over millions of rows, memory consumption remains constant ($O(1)$).

[!IMPORTANT] Case Sensitivity: Database column names exposed as variables within Go templates match the case returned by the database driver. For consistency across database engines (e.g. Oracle returning uppercase identifiers), use explicit SQL column aliases (e.g. SELECT id AS id, name AS name ...).

docs.title: Overview of the <excel_read> in Flow
docs.text: The <excel_read> node in flow enables direct integration with .xlsx workbooks. You can extract data from Excel into JSON for APIs for downstream processing.

docs.title: <excel_read>
docs.text:
• file: Target path of the .xlsx file to read. Supports {{VarName}} interpolation.
  • sheet: (Optional) The name of the worksheet to read. Defaults to the first sheet if omitted.
  • header: (Optional) Boolean (true / false). If true (default), the first row is treated as keys for the resulting JSON.
  • output_var / var: The pipeline variable where the extracted JSON string will be stored.

docs.title: 1. Reading Excel Data into a JSON API Payload
docs.text:
Extract configuration or bulk upload data from an Excel sheet and send it to an external API endpoint.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="FILE_PATH" type="string" value="./uploads/new_users.xlsx" />
    </variables>
    <flow>
        <!-- Reads the "Users" sheet into JSON (using row 1 as keys) -->
        <excel_read file="{{FILE_PATH}}" sheet="Users" output_var="USER_JSON_DATA" />

        <sql_bulk 
            method="POST" 
            uri="https://api.example.com/v1/users/bulk" 
            content_type="application/json" 
            data="{{USER_JSON_DATA}}" />
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: 2. Reading Excel Data Without Headers
docs.text:
Sometimes data files don't have headers. You can set header="false" to process the raw rows programmatically in a later script.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <flow>
        <excel_read file="./raw_data/metrics.xlsx" sheet="RawMetrics" header="false" output_var="RAW_DATA" />

        <!-- Process the array of arrays in a Go script -->
        <script lang="go">
            package main
            import (
                "fmt"
                "encoding/json"
                "host/vars"
            )
            func main() {
                rawData := vars.GetString("RAW_DATA")
                fmt.Printf("Successfully loaded raw data: %d bytes\n", len(rawData))
                // Add custom JSON unmarshaling and validation here
            }
        </script>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Overview of the <excel_write> Node in Flow
docs.text: The <excel_write> node in flow enables direct integration with .xlsx workbooks. You can extract data from Excel into JSON for APIs or downstream processing, and you can export database queries directly into styled, native Excel files.

docs.title: <excel_write>
docs.text:
• file: Target path on the local filesystem to save the .xlsx file. Supports interpolation.
  • sheet: (Optional) Name of the worksheet where data will be written. Defaults to Sheet1.
  • db: (Optional) Database connection name to execute the inline query against.
  • Inline Content: The SQL query used to pull data from the database and populate the Excel file.

docs.title: 1. Simple Database Export to Excel
docs.text:
Extract a report directly from a SQL database and save it as a native .xlsx file.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="erp_db" connection_string="sqlserver://user:pass@localhost:1433" />
    </databases>
    <flow>
        <excel_write file="./exports/customer_list.xlsx" sheet="Customers" db="erp_db">
            SELECT id, first_name, last_name, email, created_at 
            FROM dbo.customers 
            WHERE active = 1
            ORDER BY created_at DESC;
        </excel_write>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: 2. Dynamic Excel Generation with Variables
docs.text:
Use pipeline variables to dynamically name the output file and filter the SQL query.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="REPORT_MONTH" type="string" value="August_2026" />
        <variable name="DEPT_ID" type="int" value="42" />
    </variables>
    <flow>
        <!-- The file path and query both use template variables -->
        <excel_write file="./reports/finance/Expenses_{{REPORT_MONTH}}.xlsx" sheet="Expenses" db="finance_db">
            SELECT expense_id, amount, category, date_filed 
            FROM dbo.expenses 
            WHERE department_id = {{DEPT_ID}} 
              AND FORMAT(date_filed, 'MMMM_yyyy') = '{{REPORT_MONTH}}'
        </excel_write>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: 3. Multi-Sheet Export (Using Parallel execution)
docs.text:
Extract multiple datasets simultaneously from the database into different Excel files using the <parallel> node.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <flow>
        <parallel max_threads="3">
            <excel_write file="./exports/dashboard/Sales.xlsx" sheet="Sales_Data" db="warehouse">
                SELECT * FROM mart.fct_sales WHERE year = 2026;
            </excel_write>

            <excel_write file="./exports/dashboard/Inventory.xlsx" sheet="Stock" db="warehouse">
                SELECT item_code, quantity, warehouse_loc FROM mart.dim_inventory;
            </excel_write>

            <excel_write file="./exports/dashboard/Employees.xlsx" sheet="HR_Data" db="warehouse">
                SELECT emp_id, department, status FROM mart.dim_employees;
            </excel_write>
        </parallel>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: 4. Adding different tabs to the same Excel file
docs.text:
You can create multiple sheets within a single Excel file by specifying different sheet attributes in multiple <excel_write> nodes pointing to the same file.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
<pipeline description="Monthly Sales and Inventory Report Pipeline">
    <databases>
        <database name="sales_db" 
                  driver="postgres" 
                  connection_string="host=localhost port=5432 user=postgres password=secret dbname=sales sslmode=disable" 
                  description="Primary Analytics Database" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <!-- Tab 1: Executive Summary -->
        <excel_write id="export_summary" 
                     file="reports/Monthly_Executive_Report.xlsx" 
                     sheet="Summary KPI" 
                     db="sales_db"
                     description="Writes top-level monthly KPIs to the first tab">
            SELECT 
                DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month,
                COUNT(order_id) AS total_orders,
                SUM(total_amount) AS total_revenue
            FROM orders
            GROUP BY 1
            ORDER BY 1 DESC;
        </excel_write>

        <!-- Tab 2: Customer Breakdown -->
        <excel_write id="export_customers" 
                     file="reports/Monthly_Executive_Report.xlsx" 
                     sheet="Customer Details" 
                     db="sales_db"
                     description="Appends customer breakdown to a second tab">
            SELECT 
                customer_id,
                company_name,
                country,
                total_spent
            FROM customer_summary
            WHERE total_spent > 10000;
        </excel_write>

        <!-- Tab 3: Regional Inventory -->
        <excel_write id="export_inventory" 
                     file="reports/Monthly_Executive_Report.xlsx" 
                     sheet="Inventory Status" 
                     db="sales_db"
                     description="Appends inventory levels to a third tab">
            SELECT 
                warehouse_id,
                product_sku,
                stock_on_hand,
                reorder_level
            FROM warehouse_inventory;
        </excel_write>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Overview of the <file_read> Node in Flow
docs.text: The <file_read> in flow allow you to interact directly with the local filesystem. You can read configuration files or datasets into pipeline variables.

docs.title: <file_read>
docs.text:
• file / path / filename: Target path of the file to load. Supports {{VarName}} interpolation.
  • output_var / var: The pipeline variable where the file's contents will be stored as a string.

docs.title: 1. Reading a JSON Config and Sending it via HTTP
docs.text:
Load a configuration file into memory and POST it to a remote endpoint.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <scripts>
        <file_read file="./data/payload.json" output_var="JSON_DATA" />

        <sql_bulk 
            method="POST" 
            uri="https://api.example.com/sync" 
            content_type="application/json" 
            data="{{JSON_DATA}}" />
    </scripts>
</pipeline>

docs.title: 2. Reading a SQL Query from File and Executing It
docs.text:
Keep your SQL scripts organized in files, load them dynamically, and execute them on your database.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="primary_db" connection_string="sqlserver://user:pass@localhost:1433" />
    </databases>
    <scripts>
        <!-- Read SQL text into variable QUERY_TEXT -->
        <file_read file="./queries/nightly_cleanup.sql" output_var="QUERY_TEXT" />

        <!-- Execute the SQL query -->
        <sql db="primary_db" var="QUERY_TEXT" />
    </scripts>
</pipeline>

docs.title: 3. Modifying and Resaving a File using Scripts
docs.text:
Read an existing file, process or modify it using a script (like Go, Bash, or PowerShell), and save the results to a new file.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <scripts>
        <!-- 1. Read input CSV -->
        <file_read file="./data/raw_users.csv" output_var="RAW_CSV" />

        <!-- 2. Process it via shell script, outputting to CLEAN_CSV -->
        <script lang="bash" output_var="CLEAN_CSV">
            # Using grep to remove empty lines and invalid data
            echo "$RAW_CSV" | grep -v "^$" | grep -i "@example.com"
        </script>

        <!-- 3. Save processed results to a new file -->
        <file_save file="./data/clean_users.csv" var="CLEAN_CSV" />
    </scripts>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Overview of the <file_save> Node in Flow
docs.text: The <file_save> node in flow allows you to interact directly with the local filesystem. You can write generated templates, script outputs, or log data back to disk.

docs.title: <file_save>
docs.text:
• file / path / filename: Target path on the local filesystem. Supports {{VarName}} interpolation.
  • var / variable: (Optional) Source variable containing the text to write. If omitted, the inline text inside the element is used.
  • append: (Optional) Boolean (true / false). If true, text is appended; if false (default), the file is overwritten.

docs.title: Note: <file_save> automatically creates missing parent directories.
1. Rendering a Template and Saving the Output
docs.text:
Generate a dynamic HTML report using the <template> node and save the resulting variable to disk.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="REPORT_DATE" type="string" value="2026-08-25" />
    </variables>
    <scripts>
        <!-- Generate HTML content into REPORT_HTML -->
        <template id="gen_report" output_var="REPORT_HTML">
            <html>
                <body>
                    <h1>Daily Report: {{.REPORT_DATE}}</h1>
                    <p>All systems operational.</p>
                </body>
            </html>
        </template>

        <!-- Save the HTML to an output directory -->
        <file_save file="./output/reports/daily_{{REPORT_DATE}}.html" var="REPORT_HTML" />
    </scripts>
</pipeline>

docs.title: 2. Modifying and Resaving a File using Scripts
docs.text:
Read an existing file, process or modify it using a script (like Go, Bash, or PowerShell), and save the results to a new file.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <scripts>
        <!-- 1. Read input CSV -->
        <file_read file="./data/raw_users.csv" output_var="RAW_CSV" />

        <!-- 2. Process it via shell script, outputting to CLEAN_CSV -->
        <script lang="bash" output_var="CLEAN_CSV">
            # Using grep to remove empty lines and invalid data
            echo "$RAW_CSV" | grep -v "^$" | grep -i "@example.com"
        </script>

        <!-- 3. Save processed results to a new file -->
        <file_save file="./data/clean_users.csv" var="CLEAN_CSV" />
    </scripts>
</pipeline>

docs.title: <foreach> & <loop>
docs.text:
The <foreach> element (alias <loop>) executes nested pipeline steps iteratively for each record returned by a database driver query. It bridges relational query results with dynamic child task execution, automatically binding projected column values into the pipeline registry for use across subsequent SQL steps, scripts, templates, HTTP probes, file operations, and nested control groups.

Flow's <foreach> engine is engineered for high-throughput enterprise pipelines, supporting both constant-memory streaming for processing tens of millions of records without memory spikes, and in-memory buffering to release database locks upfront.

docs.title: Architecture & Lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A([Start Foreach Loop]) --> B{Driver Query Source?}
    B -- Inline SQL Body --> C[Parse Inline SQL Text]
    B -- var / variable Attribute --> D[Resolve Variable Query Text]

    C --> E[Execute Driver Query on Target DB]
    D --> E

    E --> F{Mode?}
    F -- stream='true' / mode='stream' --> G[Open Constant-Memory Cursor]
    F -- buffer='true' / mode='buffer' --> H[Buffer Rows in Memory up to 100k & Release DB Cursor]

    G --> I{Next Row Available?}
    H --> I

    I -- Yes --> J["Bind Column Variables<br/>{{col}}, {{COL}}, {{Col}}<br/>Set {{LOOP_INDEX}}"]
    J --> K[Execute Child Pipeline Nodes Sequentially]

    K --> L{Step Failed?}
    L -- Yes --> M{on_error Policy?}
    M -- stop (default) --> N[Abort Pipeline & Report Failure]
    M -- continue --> O[Log Warning & Advance Loop]
    M -- retry --> P[Retry Step up to retry_count]
    P --> K

    L -- No --> O
    O --> I

    I -- No (EOF) --> Q[Record Iteration Metrics in LAST_OUTPUT]
    Q --> R([Exit Foreach Block])

docs.title: XML Syntax & Attribute Reference
docs.text:
<foreach id="ProcessBatch"
         db="source_db"
         language="sql"
         stream="true"
         buffer="false"
         mode="stream"
         on_error="stop"
         description="Iterate over pending customer orders">
    SELECT order_id, customer_email, total_amount FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending';

    <group id="ProcessSingleOrder" transaction="true" db="source_db">
        <!-- Child nodes executed once per returned row -->
    </group>
</foreach>
Attribute Mandatory Default Description id Optional foreach_N Unique step identifier used in logs, execution metrics, and diagnostics. db / database Yes — Name of the configured database connection used to execute the driver query. language / lang Optional sql Driver query engine runtime. Defaults to sql. var / variable Optional — Name of a pipeline variable containing the driver SQL query. If non-empty, takes precedence over inline XML body text. stream Optional true Boolean enabling constant-memory streaming cursor mode. Consumes $O(1)$ RAM regardless of result set size. buffer Optional false Boolean enabling in-memory row buffering (capped at 100,000 rows). Reads all records upfront to close the database cursor early. mode Optional stream Explicit execution mode: 'stream' ($O(1)$ streaming cursor) or 'buffer' (in-memory buffer). condition / cond Optional — Inline boolean expression evaluated before executing the loop. If false, the loop is skipped. on_error Optional stop Failure policy when a child step fails: stop (halts pipeline), continue (logs warning and advances to next row), or retry. retry_count Optional 0 Number of times to retry failed child steps before triggering on_error. retry_interval Optional — Duration delay between retries (e.g., 2s, 500ms). timeout Optional — Execution deadline duration for the loop (e.g., 30s, 5m). description Optional — Human-readable explanation of the loop logic. Inline Content Conditional — The driver SQL query placed between <foreach> and child tags. Required when var is not specified.

docs.title: Streaming vs. Buffering Modes
docs.text:
Flow provides two execution architectures for iterating over driver queries:

flowchart LR
    subgraph Streaming ["Mode: 'stream' (Default)"]
        S1[(Database Cursor)] -->|Row by Row Stream| S2[Memory: O-1 Tiny Footprint]
        S2 -->|Direct Execution| S3[Child Steps]
    end

    subgraph Buffering ["Mode: 'buffer' (buffer='true')"]
        B1[(Database Cursor)] -->|Read All Rows Upfront| B2[Memory: Slices up to 100k]
        B2 -->|Cursor Closed Early| B3[Database Connection Freed]
        B2 -->|Iterate Buffered Slice| B4[Child Steps]
    end

docs.title: 1. Constant-Memory Streaming (mode="stream", stream="true")
docs.text:
• Default behavior: Ideal for massive tables (millions of rows).
  • Memory footprint: $O(1)$ constant overhead. Rows are fetched and processed on-the-fly via native database cursors.
  • Connection hold: Keeps the driver database connection open for the entire duration of the loop.

docs.title: 2. In-Memory Buffering (mode="buffer", buffer="true")
docs.text:
• Use case: Essential when child steps need to query or update the same database connection as the driver query without encountering connection pool starvation, cursor locks, or driver deadlocks.
  • Safety limit: Upfront row ingestion is capped at 100,000 rows to prevent process out-of-memory errors.
  • Early release: The database connection and cursor are released back to the pool before child steps start running.

docs.title: Variable Binding & Scoping
docs.text: For every row processed, <foreach> automatically binds all projected columns into the pipeline registry:

docs.title: 1. Case-Insensitive Column Variables
docs.text: Columns are registered in three naming conventions so child steps can reference them naturally: * Original column name: e.g., {{order_id}} * Uppercase name: e.g., {{ORDER_ID}} * Lowercase name: e.g., {{order_id}}

docs.title: 2. Built-in Loop Index (LOOP_INDEX)
docs.text:
• Flow sets the variable LOOP_INDEX to the zero-based iteration index (0, 1, 2, ...).
  • Access in SQL steps: SELECT {{LOOP_INDEX}} AS current_iteration;
  • Access in Go scripts: idx := vars.GetInt("LOOP_INDEX")
  • Access in templates: Iteration: {{ .LOOP_INDEX }}

docs.title: 3. Loop Result Diagnostics
docs.text: Upon completion, <foreach> writes summary statistics to the step output and LAST_OUTPUT, reporting: * rows: Total rows returned by driver query. * iterations: Total child iterations completed. * duration: Wall-clock processing time.

docs.title: Transaction Scoping with Foreach
docs.text:
How <foreach> interacts with database transactions depends on where <group transaction="true"> is placed:

flowchart TD
    subgraph PatternA ["Per-Iteration Transactions (Recommended)"]
        PA1["<foreach>"] --> PA2["<group transaction='true'>"]
        PA2 --> PA3["Commit / Rollback per Row"]
    end

    subgraph PatternB ["Overarching Transaction (Atomic Batch)"]
        PB1["<group transaction='true'>"] --> PB2["<foreach>"]
        PB2 --> PB3["Commit / Rollback across Entire Loop"]
    end
  1. Per-Iteration Transaction (Recommended for large jobs): Place <group transaction="true"> inside the <foreach>. Each iteration is an independent transaction. If row 5 fails with on_error="continue", rows 1–4 remain safely committed.
  2. Overarching Transaction (Atomic Batch): Place <foreach> inside <group transaction="true">. The entire loop is wrapped in one single transaction. If any iteration fails, all changes across all previous iterations are rolled back.

    [!WARNING] Do not use overarching transactions for loops spanning thousands of rows, as long-held table locks will degrade database performance.

docs.title: Example 1: Dynamic Table Replication Loop
docs.text:
Iterates through a database migration mapping table and bulk-streams each table using <sql_bulk>:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="ReplicationPlan" type="string" 
                  value="SELECT source_table, destination_table, column_filter FROM etl_transfer_map WHERE is_active = 1" />
    </variables>

    <databases>
        <database name="primary_oltp" driver="sqlserver" connection_string="sqlserver://prod-db:1433?database=AppDB" />
        <database name="reporting_dw" driver="postgres" connection_string="host=dw-db port=5432 user=etl dbname=reports sslmode=require" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <!-- Loop over each active mapping row -->
        <foreach id="ReplicateTables" db="primary_oltp" var="ReplicationPlan" stream="true">
            <group id="TransferSingleTable">
                <!-- Log progress with Go script -->
                <script id="LogIteration" language="go">
                    package main
                    import (
                        "fmt"
                        "host/vars"
                    )
                    func main() {
                        idx := vars.GetInt("LOOP_INDEX")
                        src := vars.GetString("source_table")
                        dst := vars.GetString("destination_table")
                        fmt.Printf("[Row #%d] Transferring table %s -> %s\n", idx+1, src, dst)
                    }
                </script>

                <!-- Truncate destination before copying -->
                <sql id="TruncateStaging" db="reporting_dw">
                    TRUNCATE TABLE {{destination_table}};
                </sql>

                <!-- Bulk stream from source to destination -->
                <sql_bulk id="BulkCopy" db="primary_oltp" target_db="reporting_dw"
                          target_table="{{destination_table}}" batch_size="50000">
                    SELECT {{column_filter}} FROM {{source_table}};
                </sql_bulk>
            </group>
        </foreach>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 2: Multi-Tenant Invoicing with Per-Iteration Transactions
docs.text:
Generates monthly invoices for active accounts, isolating each customer transaction with automatic rollback on error:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="billing_db" driver="postgres" connection_string="host=billing.internal user=postgres dbname=billing" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <foreach id="InvoiceGenerationLoop" db="billing_db" on_error="continue">
            SELECT account_id, account_tier, rate_per_unit 
            FROM accounts 
            WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' AND billing_cycle = 'MONTHLY';

            <!-- Independent atomic transaction for each account -->
            <group id="GenerateInvoiceTx" transaction="true" db="billing_db" timeout="10s">
                <!-- Calculate usage charges -->
                <sql id="InsertInvoiceRecord" db="billing_db" output_var="NewInvoiceId">
                    INSERT INTO invoices (account_id, billing_date, status)
                    VALUES ('{{account_id}}', CURRENT_DATE, 'PENDING')
                    RETURNING invoice_id;
                </sql>

                <!-- Create line items -->
                <sql id="GenerateLineItems" db="billing_db">
                    INSERT INTO invoice_items (invoice_id, description, amount)
                    SELECT '{{NewInvoiceId}}', service_name, quantity * {{rate_per_unit}}
                    FROM unbilled_usage
                    WHERE account_id = '{{account_id}}';
                </sql>

                <!-- Mark usage as billed -->
                <sql id="ClearUnbilledUsage" db="billing_db">
                    UPDATE unbilled_usage 
                    SET billed = true 
                    WHERE account_id = '{{account_id}}';
                </sql>
            </group>
        </foreach>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 3: Dynamic File Export with In-Memory Buffering
docs.text:
Buffers driver query results in memory to close the database connection immediately, then exports individual JSON files:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="EXPORT_DIR" type="string" value="./exports/customers" />
    </variables>

    <databases>
        <database name="crm_db" driver="mysql" connection_string="root:secret@tcp(127.0.0.1:3306)/crm" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <!-- In-memory buffering releases crm_db connection upfront -->
        <foreach id="ExportLoop" db="crm_db" buffer="true" mode="buffer">
            SELECT customer_code, full_name, email, credit_limit 
            FROM customers 
            WHERE sync_required = 1;

            <group id="WriteCustomerFile">
                <!-- Render customer JSON file -->
                <file_save id="SaveCustomerJson" 
                           file="{{EXPORT_DIR}}/{{customer_code}}.json" 
                           append="false">
                    {
                      "customer_code": "{{customer_code}}",
                      "name": "{{full_name}}",
                      "email": "{{email}}",
                      "credit_limit": {{credit_limit}},
                      "exported_at": "{{_TIMESTAMP}}"
                    }
                </file_save>
            </group>
        </foreach>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 4: External Webhook Notification with Assertion Quality Gate
docs.text:
Dispatches payment alerts via HTTP POST and asserts HTTP 200/201 response status:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="app_db" driver="sqlite" connection_string="file:app.db?cache=shared" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <foreach id="WebhookLoop" db="app_db" on_error="continue">
            SELECT event_id, webhook_url, payload_json 
            FROM outbound_webhooks 
            WHERE delivered = 0;

            <group id="DispatchEvent">
                <!-- Send HTTP Post -->
                <http_client id="SendWebhook" 
                             url="{{webhook_url}}" 
                             method="POST" 
                             content_type="application/json"
                             status_into="HTTP_STATUS" 
                             timeout="5s">
                    {{payload_json}}
                </http_client>

                <!-- Validate HTTP status -->
                <assert id="VerifyDelivery" var="HTTP_STATUS" equals="200" on_failure="warn" />

                <!-- Mark as processed if successful -->
                <sql id="MarkDelivered" db="app_db">
                    UPDATE outbound_webhooks SET delivered = 1 WHERE event_id = {{event_id}};
                </sql>
            </group>
        </foreach>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 5: High-Performance Key-Value Store Migration
docs.text:
Reads user authentication credentials and streams them into an embedded Badger/Bolt Key-Value store:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="auth_sql" driver="postgres" connection_string="host=localhost dbname=auth" />
        <database name="cache_kv" driver="badger" connection_string="./data/cache.badger" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <!-- Streaming cursor for hundreds of thousands of sessions -->
        <foreach id="MigrateSessions" db="auth_sql" stream="true">
            SELECT session_token, user_profile_json 
            FROM active_sessions;

            <kv id="PutSession" db="cache_kv" op="put" bucket="sessions" 
                key="{{session_token}}" value="{{user_profile_json}}" />
        </foreach>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: <group> Execution Group & Database Transactions Guide
docs.text: The <group> element organizes child pipeline steps into a sequential, cohesive execution block. It serves three critical functions in Flow pipelines: 1. Logical Step Organization: Cleanly groups related tasks under a shared identifier, descriptive label, and lifecycle scope. 2. Atomic Database Transactions & Dialect-Aware Savepoints: Coordinates multiple <sql> queries into an all-or-nothing transaction with automatic commit and rollback, plus dialect-aware savepoints for nested groups. 3. Conditional Execution & Error Resilience: Evaluates conditions before running child steps and governs fault tolerance via granular retry policies (on_error, retry_count, retry_interval).

docs.title: 1. Architectural Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Start(["Enter <group>"]) --> CondCheck{"Has Condition?<br/>(condition / if_var)"}

    CondCheck -- "Condition Fails" --> Skipped(["Skip Group & Children"])
    CondCheck -- "Passes or None" --> TxCheck{"transaction='true'?"}

    TxCheck -- "No" --> ExecSteps["Execute Child Steps Sequentially"]
    TxCheck -- "Yes" --> StackCheck{"Active Outer Tx<br/>on Same DB?"}

    StackCheck -- "No (Root Tx)" --> BeginTx["BeginTx(ctx)<br/>Push to Transaction Stack"]
    StackCheck -- "Yes (Nested)" --> CreateSP["Create Dialect Savepoint<br/>• MSSQL: SAVE TRANSACTION sp_N<br/>• ANSI: SAVEPOINT sp_N"]

    BeginTx --> ExecSteps
    CreateSP --> ExecSteps

    ExecSteps --> StepResult{"All Steps<br/>Succeeded?"}

    StepResult -- "Yes" --> TxSuccess{"transaction='true'?"}
    TxSuccess -- "No" --> Done(["Group Completed"])
    TxSuccess -- "Yes (Root)" --> CommitTx["Commit Transaction<br/>Pop Stack"] --> Done
    TxSuccess -- "Yes (Nested)" --> ReleaseSP["Release / Finalize Savepoint<br/>Pop Stack"] --> Done

    StepResult -- "No (Error/Timeout)" --> ErrorPolicy{"on_error Policy"}

    ErrorPolicy -- "retry (count > 0)" --> RollbackAttempt["Rollback Tx or SP<br/>Wait retry_interval"] --> ExecSteps
    ErrorPolicy -- "continue" --> RollbackCont["Rollback Tx or SP<br/>Log Warning & Continue"] --> Done
    ErrorPolicy -- "stop (Default)" --> RollbackFail["Rollback Tx or SP<br/>Abort Pipeline"] --> Fail(["Pipeline Error"])

docs.title: 2. Complete XML Syntax & Attribute Reference
docs.text:
<group id="ProcessBatch"
       transaction="true"
       db="finance_db"
       timeout="45s"
       on_error="retry"
       retry_count="3"
       retry_interval="5s"
       condition="{{IsActive}} == true"
       description="Executes accounting batch with atomic commit and retry">
    <!-- Sequential child steps: <sql>, <script>, <http_client>, <template>, etc. -->
</group>

docs.title: Attribute Reference
docs.text: Attribute Type Mandatory Default Description id string Yes (Recommended) generated Unique identifier for the group step, displayed in execution telemetry, logs, and flowcharts. transaction bool No false When true, wraps all child <sql> steps inside an atomic database transaction. tx bool No false Alias for transaction. db string Conditional — The configured database connection name to open the transaction against. Mandatory when transaction="true". database string No — Alias for db. timeout string No — Transaction deadline duration (e.g. 30s, 2m, 1h). Cancels the context and triggers an automatic rollback if exceeded. on_error string No stop Failure policy when a child step returns an error: stop (abort group and pipeline), continue (log and proceed to next sibling), or retry (reattempt group). retry_count int No 0 Number of retry attempts when on_error="retry". retry_interval string No 1s Delay between retry attempts (e.g. 500ms, 2s, 10s). condition string No — Inline boolean expression evaluated before execution (e.g. {{Env}} == 'prod', {{TotalCount}} > 0). cond string No — Alias for condition. if_var string No — Name of a pipeline variable to test for execution (e.g. RunBatch). Alias var. var string No — Alias for if_var. if_equals string No — Expected variable value required for the group to execute. Aliases: equals, if_val, val, value. equals string No — Alias for if_equals. if_val string No — Alias for if_equals. val string No — Alias for if_equals. value string No — Alias for if_equals. description string No — Descriptive summary of the group's purpose.

docs.title: 3. Database Transactions & Dialect-Aware Savepoints
docs.text:
Flow implements a thread-safe, stack-based transaction coordinator (activeTxs). It guarantees that all child database operations within the group succeed as a single atomic unit or roll back completely upon failure.

flowchart TD
    subgraph OuterGroup ["Outer <group id='financial_transfer' transaction='true' db='bank_db'>"]
        T1["BeginTx() on bank_db"] --> S1["1. UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 500 WHERE id = 1"]

        subgraph InnerGroup ["Inner <group id='nested_audit' transaction='true' db='bank_db'>"]
            SP["Create Savepoint (sp_1)<br/>• MSSQL: SAVE TRANSACTION sp_1<br/>• ANSI: SAVEPOINT sp_1"] --> S2["2. INSERT INTO transfer_audit_log VALUES (...)"]
            S2 --> SPCheck{"Audit Step Ok?"}
            SPCheck -- "Success" --> SPRelease["Release / Retain Savepoint"]
            SPCheck -- "Failure" --> SPRollback["ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT sp_1<br/>(Outer Tx remains intact)"]
        end

        S1 --> SP
        SPRelease --> S3["3. UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 500 WHERE id = 2"]
        SPRollback --> S3

        S3 --> FinalCheck{"All Steps Ok?"}
        FinalCheck -- "Success" --> CommitTx["Commit Outer Transaction"]
        FinalCheck -- "Failure" --> RollbackTx["Rollback Full Transaction"]
    end

docs.title: Dialect-Aware Savepoints
docs.text:
When an inner <group transaction="true"> targets the same database connection as an active outer transaction, Flow detects the nested state and automatically establishes a savepoint:

Database Driver Savepoint Command Rollback Command Release Command PostgreSQL (postgres, pgx) SAVEPOINT sp_N ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT sp_N RELEASE SAVEPOINT sp_N SQLite (sqlite3) SAVEPOINT sp_N ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT sp_N RELEASE SAVEPOINT sp_N MySQL / MariaDB (mysql) SAVEPOINT sp_N ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT sp_N RELEASE SAVEPOINT sp_N Oracle (godror) SAVEPOINT sp_N ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT sp_N — (Automatic on commit) Microsoft SQL Server (sqlserver, mssql) SAVE TRANSACTION sp_N ROLLBACK TRANSACTION sp_N — (T-SQL omits release syntax)

[!NOTE] If an inner group with a savepoint fails, Flow rolls back only to that savepoint, allowing the outer transaction to inspect the failure, execute alternative logic, or proceed to completion without corrupting the broader transaction.

docs.title: 4. Context Propagation & Execution Deadlines (timeout)
docs.text:
Database locks held by uncommitted transactions can degrade database performance and cause deadlocks. Flow binds every transaction group to a Go context.Context:

  • Granular Timeouts: Specify timeout="30s" or timeout="5m" on the group.
  • Automatic Rollback: If the timeout duration expires or an external cancellation signal arrives, the context is cancelled immediately. Flow executes an atomic deferred rollback, closing the transaction and releasing all table locks.
<group id="critical_update" transaction="true" db="crm_db" timeout="15s">
    <sql id="apply_discount" db="crm_db">
        UPDATE subscriptions SET discount_pct = 0.20 WHERE renew_date <= CURRENT_DATE;
    </sql>
</group>

docs.title: 5. Error Handling & Retry Policies
docs.text:
The <group> element supports localized resilience and fault recovery policies:

flowchart LR
    Step["Child Step Fails"] --> Policy{"on_error"}
    Policy -- "stop" --> Stop["Rollback Tx & Halt Pipeline"]
    Policy -- "continue" --> Cont["Rollback Tx & Log Warning<br/>Proceed to Next Node"]
    Policy -- "retry" --> CountCheck{"Retries Left?"}
    CountCheck -- "Yes" --> Delay["Sleep retry_interval"] --> Reattempt["Rollback Tx & Re-run Group"]
    CountCheck -- "No" --> Stop
  • on_error="stop" (Default): Any child failure halts the group, initiates an immediate database rollback, and fails the pipeline.
  • on_error="continue": If a child step fails, the group's transaction is rolled back safely, but the pipeline execution continues with the subsequent sibling nodes.
  • on_error="retry": When paired with retry_count="N" and retry_interval="Xs", transient failures (such as network drops or database deadlocks) trigger an immediate rollback followed by a clean re-execution of the group from the beginning.

docs.title: 6. Conditional Group Execution
docs.text: Instead of requiring an explicit <if><then>...</then></if> construct, <group> supports direct conditional attributes:

docs.title: 1. Simple Variable Equality Testing (if_var + if_equals)
docs.text:
<group id="RunProductionMigrations" if_var="Environment" if_equals="production">
    <sql db="app_db">ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS verified BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE;</sql>
</group>

docs.title: 2. Boolean Expressions (condition)
docs.text:
<group id="ProcessHighPriority" condition="{{PendingRecords}} > 1000 && {{DryRun}} == false">
    <sql db="warehouse_db">INSERT INTO processing_queue SELECT * FROM staging_records;</sql>
</group>

docs.title: Loops (<foreach>, <while>)
docs.text: When placed inside <foreach> or <while>, a <group transaction="true"> creates, commits, or rolls back an independent transaction on every individual iteration: * Failure in iteration N rolls back only iteration N. * Preceding iterations remain permanently committed. * Subsequent iterations continue according to the loop's error policy.

docs.title: Parallel Execution (<parallel>)
docs.text: When running inside <parallel max_threads="...">: * Flow provisions a cloned, thread-isolated execution context for each worker branch. * If a worker executes <group transaction="true">, its transaction is isolated to that worker's dedicated database connection. * Concurrent workers never share transaction states or collide on savepoint names.

docs.title: High-Throughput Bulk Copy Caution (<sql_bulk>)
docs.text:
[!WARNING] Do NOT wrap high-throughput streaming bulk copy (<sql_bulk target_table="..."> / StreamETL) inside a transaction-enabled <group transaction="true">.

SQL Server TDS bulk copy operates using its own internal batch-level commits (batch_size="10000"). Wrapping native TDS fast-load streams inside an outer group transaction causes driver command overlap, connection pool exhaustion, and extensive table lock contention.

docs.title: Example 1: Multi-Step Bank Transfer with Atomic Transaction & Timeout
docs.text:
Demonstrates debiting one account, crediting another, and writing an audit trail with an enforced 30-second deadline.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="SenderID" type="int" value="101" />
        <variable name="ReceiverID" type="int" value="202" />
        <variable name="TransferAmount" type="float" value="150.00" />
    </variables>

    <databases>
        <database name="core_banking" driver="postgres"
                  connection_string="postgresql://app_user:Secret123@db.internal:5432/banking?sslmode=require" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <!-- Atomic transaction block with 30s timeout -->
        <group id="transfer_funds_txn" transaction="true" db="core_banking" timeout="30s"
               description="Transfers funds atomically between accounts">

            <!-- Step 1: Deduct balance with balance constraint -->
            <sql id="debit_sender" db="core_banking">
                UPDATE accounts 
                SET balance = balance - {{TransferAmount}}, updated_at = NOW()
                WHERE account_id = {{SenderID}} AND balance >= {{TransferAmount}};
            </sql>

            <!-- Step 2: Ensure exactly 1 row was updated -->
            <assert id="check_debit_applied" var="debit_sender.rows_affected" equals="1"
                    message="Insufficient funds or invalid sender account ID" on_failure="halt" />

            <!-- Step 3: Credit destination account -->
            <sql id="credit_receiver" db="core_banking">
                UPDATE accounts 
                SET balance = balance + {{TransferAmount}}, updated_at = NOW()
                WHERE account_id = {{ReceiverID}};
            </sql>

            <!-- Step 4: Record immutable audit ledger -->
            <sql id="record_ledger_entry" db="core_banking">
                INSERT INTO transaction_ledger (from_acc, to_acc, amount, created_at)
                VALUES ({{SenderID}}, {{ReceiverID}}, {{TransferAmount}}, NOW());
            </sql>
        </group>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 2: Nested Savepoints (Outer Transaction with Inner Audit Group)
docs.text:
Demonstrates dialect-aware savepoints. If the nested audit log fails, the inner savepoint rolls back without interrupting the outer order processing.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="store_db" driver="sqlserver"
                  connection_string="sqlserver://sql.prod.net:1433?database=Store&integrated+security=true" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <!-- Root transaction boundary -->
        <group id="process_order_txn" transaction="true" db="store_db" timeout="1m">

            <!-- 1. Place order -->
            <sql id="insert_order" db="store_db">
                INSERT INTO orders (customer_id, total_amount) VALUES (4096, 299.95);
            </sql>

            <!-- 2. Nested transaction: uses T-SQL 'SAVE TRANSACTION savepoint_1' -->
            <group id="nested_notification_log" transaction="true" db="store_db" on_error="continue">
                <sql id="log_notification" db="store_db">
                    INSERT INTO notification_queue (order_id, channel) VALUES (4096, 'EMAIL');
                </sql>
            </group>

            <!-- 3. Finalize order status -->
            <sql id="finalize_order" db="store_db">
                UPDATE customer_profiles SET last_order_date = GETDATE() WHERE id = 4096;
            </sql>
        </group>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 3: Conditional Execution with Error Retries
docs.text:
Demonstrates verifying an external API health check before running a group that retries up to 3 times on transient database deadlocks.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="ApiHealthy" type="bool" value="false" />
    </variables>

    <databases>
        <database name="stage_db" driver="postgres"
                  connection_string="postgresql://app:pass@localhost:5432/staging" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <!-- Probe upstream API -->
        <http_client id="check_upstream" method="GET" url="https://api.partner.com/health" status_into="HttpStatus" />

        <script id="eval_status" language="go">
            <![CDATA[
            package main
            import "host/vars"
            func main() {
                if vars.GetInt("HttpStatus") == 200 {
                    vars.SetBool("ApiHealthy", true)
                }
            }
            ]]>
        </script>

        <!-- Conditional group with retry policy -->
        <group id="pull_partner_data"
               if_var="ApiHealthy" if_equals="true"
               on_error="retry" retry_count="3" retry_interval="4s"
               transaction="true" db="stage_db">

            <http_client id="fetch_orders" method="GET" url="https://api.partner.com/v1/orders" into="OrdersJson" />

            <sql id="stage_raw_orders" db="stage_db">
                INSERT INTO staging_raw_orders (payload, received_at)
                VALUES ('{{OrdersJson}}', NOW());
            </sql>
        </group>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 4: Transactional Loop inside <foreach>
docs.text:
Demonstrates streaming active user subscriptions and applying billing renewals, committing each user in its own independent transaction.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="billing_db" driver="mysql"
                  connection_string="root:secret@tcp(127.0.0.1:3306)/billing?parseTime=true" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <!-- Loop driver: streams user IDs needing renewal -->
        <foreach id="renew_subscribers" db="billing_db">
            <![CDATA[
            SELECT user_id, plan_cost, plan_tier 
            FROM subscriptions 
            WHERE status = 'active' AND next_billing_date <= CURDATE();
            ]]>

            <!-- Each row executes in its own isolated transaction -->
            <group id="apply_user_renewal" transaction="true" db="billing_db" timeout="15s" on_error="continue">
                <sql id="deduct_user_credits" db="billing_db">
                    UPDATE user_wallets 
                    SET balance = balance - {{plan_cost}} 
                    WHERE user_id = {{user_id}} AND balance >= {{plan_cost}};
                </sql>

                <assert id="check_wallet_deducted" var="deduct_user_credits.rows_affected" equals="1"
                        message="User {{user_id}} has insufficient credit balance" />

                <sql id="advance_billing_cycle" db="billing_db">
                    UPDATE subscriptions 
                    SET next_billing_date = DATE_ADD(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 1 MONTH)
                    WHERE user_id = {{user_id}};
                </sql>

                <sql id="log_billing_history" db="billing_db">
                    INSERT INTO billing_events (user_id, amount, tier, billed_at)
                    VALUES ({{user_id}}, {{plan_cost}}, '{{plan_tier}}', NOW());
                </sql>
            </group>
        </foreach>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 5: Concurrent Isolated Transactions in <parallel>
docs.text:
Demonstrates running multi-regional partition archiving concurrently across 3 worker threads, each maintaining an isolated transaction.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="eu_db" driver="postgres" connection_string="postgresql://app:pass@eu-db:5432/main" />
        <database name="us_db" driver="postgres" connection_string="postgresql://app:pass@us-db:5432/main" />
        <database name="ap_db" driver="postgres" connection_string="postgresql://app:pass@ap-db:5432/main" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <parallel max_threads="3">
            <!-- Worker Branch 1: EU Partition Archive -->
            <group id="archive_eu_txn" transaction="true" db="eu_db" timeout="2m">
                <sql db="eu_db">
                    INSERT INTO orders_archive SELECT * FROM orders WHERE created_at < '2025-01-01';
                </sql>
                <sql db="eu_db">
                    DELETE FROM orders WHERE created_at < '2025-01-01';
                </sql>
            </group>

            <!-- Worker Branch 2: US Partition Archive -->
            <group id="archive_us_txn" transaction="true" db="us_db" timeout="2m">
                <sql db="us_db">
                    INSERT INTO orders_archive SELECT * FROM orders WHERE created_at < '2025-01-01';
                </sql>
                <sql db="us_db">
                    DELETE FROM orders WHERE created_at < '2025-01-01';
                </sql>
            </group>

            <!-- Worker Branch 3: APAC Partition Archive -->
            <group id="archive_ap_txn" transaction="true" db="ap_db" timeout="2m">
                <sql db="ap_db">
                    INSERT INTO orders_archive SELECT * FROM orders WHERE created_at < '2025-01-01';
                </sql>
                <sql db="ap_db">
                    DELETE FROM orders WHERE created_at < '2025-01-01';
                </sql>
            </group>
        </parallel>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Core Execution Flow
docs.text:
1. Variable Snapshot & Interpolation: Reads current registry variables and replaces {{VarName}} placeholders in uri, url, headers, content_type, data, and inner element body text.
  2. Transport & Client Assembly: Constructs http.Transport with TLS/proxy settings and wraps it inside an http.Client with custom redirect and timeout policies via BuildClientAndRequest.
  3. Request Execution: Issues the HTTP request bound to the parent pipeline execution context (context.Context).
  4. Response Handling & State Persistence: Reads the response body and writes data to target pipeline variables (output_var, status_code_var), updating LAST_OUTPUT.

docs.title: 2.1 Core Request & Variable Attributes
docs.text: Attribute Type Default Description id xs:string Auto (http_N) Unique node identifier for logging and AST validation. uri / url xs:string Required Target endpoint URL. Supports variable interpolation ({{VarName}}). method xs:string GET HTTP verb (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, OPTIONS). data xs:string Optional Direct payload data. Takes precedence over element body content. headers xs:string Optional Custom request headers (K1:V1,K2:V2 or newline-separated). content_type xs:string Optional Shortcut header setter for Content-Type. var / variable / output_var / output_variable / out_var / into xs:string Optional Registry variable key to store the response body. status_code_var / status_code_variable / status_var / status_variable / status_into xs:string Optional Registry variable key to store the integer HTTP status code.

docs.title: 2.2 Go http.Client Settings
docs.text: Attribute Type Default Description timeout xs:string Unlimited Total request timeout duration (e.g., 5s, 30s, 2m). follow_redirects xs:boolean true Follow HTTP 3xx redirect responses automatically. max_redirects xs:nonNegativeInteger Unlimited Maximum redirect chain limit before erroring. cookie_jar xs:boolean false Enable in-memory cookiejar session state.

docs.title: 2.3 Go http.Transport & TLS Tuning
docs.text: Attribute Type Default Description proxy xs:string Optional Proxy URL (e.g., http://proxy.internal:8080). tls_insecure_skip_verify xs:boolean false Disable SSL/TLS certificate validation checks. tls_server_name xs:string Optional SNI host verification override. tls_min_version xs:string 1.2 Minimum TLS version (1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3). tls_max_version xs:string 1.3 Maximum TLS version restriction. tls_handshake_timeout xs:string Optional Maximum wait duration for TLS handshake. disable_keep_alives xs:boolean false Disable HTTP keep-alive connection reuse. disable_compression xs:boolean false Disable Accept-Encoding: gzip headers. max_idle_conns xs:nonNegativeInteger Default Global maximum idle connection pool capacity. max_idle_conns_per_host xs:nonNegativeInteger Default Host-level maximum idle connection limit. max_conns_per_host xs:nonNegativeInteger Unlimited Total connection pool limit per host. idle_conn_timeout xs:string Optional Maximum idle duration before closing pooled connection. response_header_timeout xs:string Optional Wait duration limit for server response headers. expect_continue_timeout xs:string Optional Wait time limit for 100-continue header responses. max_response_header_bytes xs:long Default Maximum allowed size of response headers. write_buffer_size xs:nonNegativeInteger Default Size of the write buffer in bytes. read_buffer_size xs:nonNegativeInteger Default Size of the read buffer in bytes. force_attempt_http2 xs:boolean Default Force HTTP/2 protocol negotiation on TLS connections.

docs.title: 3. Payload Resolution & Variable Interpolation
docs.text:
When preparing an outgoing payload (e.g., POST, PUT, PATCH), the engine applies a two-tier resolution strategy:

  1. Attribute Data (data="..."): If the data attribute is populated, it is selected as the payload body. {{VarName}} tokens inside the attribute are interpolated.
  2. Inner Body Content: If data is omitted, inner XML text is processed. Any {{VarName}} tags are replaced with corresponding values from the registry context.

docs.title: 4.1 SQL Driver Iteration (<foreach>)
docs.text:
Inside a <foreach> block, every returned database row populates registry variables with column values (bound in exact, lowercase, and uppercase forms) alongside LOOP_INDEX. <http_client> consumes these variables per iteration:

<foreach id="IterateUsers" db="app_db">
    SELECT user_id, email, account_tier FROM users WHERE sync_pending = 1;

    <http_client 
        id="PostUserToApi"
        uri="[https://api.example.com/v1/sync](https://api.example.com/v1/sync)"
        method="POST"
        content_type="application/json"
        data='{"id": {{user_id}}, "email": "{{email}}", "tier": "{{account_tier}}"}'
        output_var="ApiResponseBody"
        status_code_var="ApiResponseCode" />

    <sql id="LogSync" db="app_db">
        UPDATE users 
        SET synced = 1, sync_code = {{ApiResponseCode}} 
        WHERE user_id = {{user_id}};
    </sql>
</foreach>

docs.title: 4.2 Polling Loops (<while>)
docs.text:
Inside a <while> loop, <http_client> can poll remote job status endpoints until a termination condition is met: 

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="JobState" type="string" value="RUNNING" />
        <variable name="JobID" type="string" value="JOB-99201" />
    </variables>

    <flow>
        <while id="PollStatus" var="JobState" equals="RUNNING" max_iterations="20">
            <http_client 
                id="CheckStatus"
                uri="[https://api.example.com/v1/jobs/](https://api.example.com/v1/jobs/){{JobID}}"
                method="GET"
                output_var="JobState" />

            <script id="Sleep" language="go">
                package main
                import "time"
                func main() { time.Sleep(2 * time.Second) }
            </script>
        </while>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: 4.3 Concurrent Requests (<parallel>)
docs.text:
Inside <parallel> blocks, each child branch runs in an isolated worker thread with a cloned registry snapshot. Output variables updated by <http_client> in thread branches are automatically merged or namespaced (WORKER_<ID>_<VAR>) back to the main registry upon completion.

<parallel max_threads="2">
    <http_client 
        id="FetchServiceA"
        uri="[https://service-a.internal/health](https://service-a.internal/health)"
        output_var="HealthA" />

    <http_client 
        id="FetchServiceB"
        uri="[https://service-b.internal/health](https://service-b.internal/health)"
        output_var="HealthB" />
</parallel>

docs.title: Example A: SQL -> HTTP POST -> Go Response Parser
docs.text:
<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <flow>
        <!-- 1. Extract JSON payload from database -->
        <sql id="GetPayload" db="analytics_db" output_var="JsonPayload">
            SELECT JSON_OBJECT('sensor_id': id, 'reading': value) 
            FROM telemetry 
            WHERE processed = 0 
            LIMIT 1;
        </sql>

        <!-- 2. Post JSON payload to cloud endpoint -->
        <http_client 
            id="SendTelemetry"
            uri="[https://cloud.example.com/v1/telemetry](https://cloud.example.com/v1/telemetry)"
            method="POST"
            content_type="application/json"
            timeout="10s"
            data="{{JsonPayload}}"
            output_var="CloudResponse"
            status_code_var="CloudStatus" />

        <!-- 3. Parse cloud response in Go -->
        <script id="ParseResponse" language="go">
            package main
            import (
                "fmt"
                "host/vars"
            )
            func main() {
                status := vars.GetInt("CloudStatus")
                resp := vars.GetString("CloudResponse")
                fmt.Printf("Uploaded with status %d: %s\n", status, resp)
            }
        </script>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"

        <http_client

            method="POST"
