docs.title: Conditional Branching (<if>, <then>, <else>) in Flow 🔀
docs.text: Flow pipelines support conditional routing through native <if> blocks. Conditional branching enables dynamic ETL decision-making, such as executing data ingestion only when source timestamps diverge, routing failed API responses to fallback webhooks, bypassing destructive migrations outside maintenance windows, or running alternative database queries based on environment variables.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture & Branching Model
docs.text: Flow's conditional execution engine supports two primary patterns: 1. Explicit Branch Containers (<if>, <then>, <else>): A parent <if> block encapsulates two distinct sub-branches. When the condition evaluates to true, child nodes inside <then> are executed. When false, child nodes inside <else> are executed. 2. Inline Step Predicates (if_var, if_equals, condition): Many individual nodes (such as <group>, <sql>, <script>, <foreach>) support conditional attributes directly on the element, conditionally skipping the node if the predicate is not met without wrapping it in an <if> container.

docs.title: Execution Lifecycle & Flowchart
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Start(["Pipeline Execution Flow"]) --> Step1["Pre-Branch Execution<br/>(SQL Query / Script / HTTP Check)"]
    Step1 --> IfCond{"❓ If Condition<br/>(var == equals OR condition)"}
    IfCond -- "Yes / True" --> ThenBranch["<then><br/>Execute Truthy Steps"]
    IfCond -- "No / False" --> ElseBranch["<else><br/>Execute Falsy Steps / Fallback"]
    ThenBranch --> Rejoin(("Rejoin Flow"))
    ElseBranch --> Rejoin
    Rejoin --> NextStep["Subsequent Pipeline Steps"]

docs.title: 🛠️ XML Syntax & Attribute Reference
docs.text:
<if id="CheckStatus"
    var="JobStatus"
    equals="COMPLETED"
    condition="eq .JobStatus 'COMPLETED'"
    description="Evaluate pipeline state before downstream processing">
    <then>
        <!-- Child nodes executed when condition is truthy -->
    </then>
    <else>
        <!-- Optional child nodes executed when condition is falsy -->
    </else>
</if>

docs.title: Complete Attributes Reference
docs.text: Attribute Type Required Description id string Optional Unique identifier for this conditional step. Recommended for tracing and observability logging. var string Optional Variable name to evaluate from the pipeline variable registry. Case-insensitive lookup. if_var string Optional Canonical alias for var. equals string Optional Expected value to compare var against. Case-insensitive string comparison. Supports template placeholders (e.g. equals="{{TargetTimestamp}}"). val / value string Optional Canonical aliases for equals. if_val / if_equals string Optional Canonical aliases for equals. condition string Optional Dynamic boolean expression or template condition evaluated against the variable context. cond string Optional Canonical alias for condition. description string Optional Human-readable explanation of why this branch condition is being tested.

docs.title: Child Elements
docs.text:
• <then> (Optional, max 1): Container holding child nodes (<sql>, <sql_bulk>, <script>, <group>, <http_client>, etc.) executed strictly when the condition evaluates to true.
  • <else> (Optional, max 1): Container holding child nodes executed strictly when the condition evaluates to false.
  • Inline Child Nodes: If <then> is omitted, direct child elements placed inside <if> default to the truthy branch.

docs.title: ⚙️ Evaluation Mechanisms
docs.text: Flow provides three common ways to formulate conditional predicates:

docs.title: 1. Direct Variable Equality (var + equals)
docs.text:
The simplest and most resilient mode. Evaluates whether the variable in var matches equals: 

<if id="CheckActive" var="IsActive" equals="true">
    <then>
        <sql db="prod_db">UPDATE Users SET Verified = 1 WHERE Active = 1;</sql>
    </then>
</if>

Dynamic placeholder comparisons are also supported: 

<if id="CompareTimestamps" var="SOURCE_MAX_DATE" equals="{{TARGET_MAX_DATE}}">
    <then>
        <!-- Tables are already identical -->
    </then>
    <else>
        <!-- Tables differ: trigger synchronization -->
    </else>
</if>

docs.title: 2. Upstream Flag Computation (SQL CASE WHEN or Go Script)
docs.text:
For complex date arithmetic, regex matching, or multi-variable logic, compute a boolean flag in an upstream step and evaluate it: 

<!-- Step 1: SQL computation -->
<sql id="CheckStaleData" db="primary_db" output_var="NEEDS_SYNC">
    <![CDATA[
    SELECT CASE WHEN DATEDIFF(hour, MAX(ExportTime), GETDATE()) > 24 THEN 'true' ELSE 'false' END AS NEEDS_SYNC
    FROM dbo.SyncLog;
    ]]>
</sql>

<!-- Step 2: Conditional execution -->
<if id="SyncIfStale" var="NEEDS_SYNC" equals="true">
    <then>
        <group id="RunETL" transaction="true" db="primary_db">
            <!-- Sync steps -->
        </group>
    </then>
</if>

docs.title: 3. Expression Conditions (condition / cond)
docs.text:
Expression strings evaluate comparison rules against the current variable map: 

<if id="CheckThreshold" condition="{{PendingRecords}} > 1000">
    <then>
        <!-- High-priority batch worker -->
    </then>
</if>

docs.title: Example 1: Database Health & System DB Verification (if_than_else.xml)
docs.text:
Checks if system databases exist. If true, runs Group A steps; otherwise runs Group B fallback steps.

<pipeline description="Database verification and conditional execution"
    xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
    xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="PrimaryConn" type="string"
            value="sqlserver://PROD_SERVER:1433?database=AppDB&integrated+security=true&trustServerCertificate=true" />
    </variables>

    <databases>
        <database name="primary_db" connection_string="{{PrimaryConn}}" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <!-- Step 1: Query database system catalog and set ScriptAResult to 'true' or 'false' -->
        <sql id="ScriptA" db="primary_db" output_var="ScriptAResult"
            description="Query system databases to check if count is greater than zero">
            <![CDATA[
            SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) > 0 THEN 'true' ELSE 'false' END FROM sys.databases;
            ]]>
        </sql>

        <!-- Step 2: Explicit <if> / <then> / <else> branching -->
        <if id="RouteExecution" var="ScriptAResult" equals="true">
            <then>
                <group id="GroupA">
                    <sql id="GroupA_Step1" db="primary_db" description="Execute primary workflow">
                        <![CDATA[ SELECT 'Executing Primary Production Group' AS status; ]]>
                    </sql>
                    <script id="GroupA_Step2" language="go">
                        <![CDATA[
                        package main
                        import "fmt"
                        func main() { fmt.Println("Primary branch completed successfully") }
                        ]]>
                    </script>
                </group>
            </then>
            <else>
                <group id="GroupB">
                    <sql id="GroupB_Step1" db="primary_db" description="Fallback when no databases exist">
                        <![CDATA[ SELECT 'Executing Fallback Workflow' AS status; ]]>
                    </sql>
                </group>
            </else>
        </if>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 2: Concurrent Multi-Database Timestamp Check & Delta Sync
docs.text:
Executes queries across two databases in <parallel>, uses a lightweight comparison script to set NEEDS_ACTION, and conditionally performs bulk streaming replication.

<pipeline description="Parallel timestamp check with conditional delta replication"
    xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
    xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="TABLE" type="string" value="dbo.BillingExport" />
        <variable name="SOURCE_MAX_DATE" type="string" value="" />
        <variable name="TARGET_MAX_DATE" type="string" value="" />
        <variable name="NEEDS_ACTION" type="string" value="false" />
    </variables>

    <databases>
        <database name="source_db" connection_string="sqlserver://SOURCE_SRV:1433?database=Analytics&integrated+security=true&trustServerCertificate=true" />
        <database name="target_db" connection_string="sqlserver://TARGET_SRV:1433?database=Warehouse&integrated+security=true&trustServerCertificate=true" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <!-- Concurrent timestamp queries across both servers -->
        <parallel id="fetch_max_timestamps" max_threads="2" description="Query source and target databases in parallel">
            <sql id="get_source_max" db="source_db" output_var="SOURCE_MAX_DATE">
                <![CDATA[ SELECT ISNULL(MAX(ExportTime), '1970-01-01') AS SOURCE_MAX_DATE FROM {{TABLE}}; ]]>
            </sql>
            <sql id="get_target_max" db="target_db" output_var="TARGET_MAX_DATE">
                <![CDATA[ SELECT ISNULL(MAX(ExportTime), '1970-01-01') AS TARGET_MAX_DATE FROM {{TABLE}}; ]]>
            </sql>
        </parallel>

        <!-- Fast Go comparison script evaluating delta condition -->
        <script id="compare_timestamps" language="go" output_variable="NEEDS_ACTION">
            <![CDATA[
            package main
            import (
                "fmt"
                "host/vars"
            )
            func main() {
                src := vars.GetString("SOURCE_MAX_DATE")
                tgt := vars.GetString("TARGET_MAX_DATE")
                if src != "" && tgt != "" && src != tgt {
                    fmt.Println("true")
                } else {
                    fmt.Println("false")
                }
            }
            ]]>
        </script>

        <!-- Branch: Replicate delta when dates diverge, or log up-to-date notice -->
        <if id="check_sync_action" var="NEEDS_ACTION" equals="true">
            <then>
                <sql_bulk id="stream_delta_to_target" db="source_db" target_db="target_db" target_table="{{TABLE}}"
                    batch_size="25000" tablock="true" description="Replicate delta rows into warehouse">
                    <![CDATA[
                    SELECT * FROM {{TABLE}} WHERE ExportTime > '{{TARGET_MAX_DATE}}';
                    ]]>
                </sql_bulk>
            </then>
            <else>
                <script id="log_in_sync" language="go">
                    <![CDATA[
                    package main
                    import "fmt"
                    func main() { fmt.Println("Target warehouse is fully up to date. No sync required.") }
                    ]]>
                </script>
            </else>
        </if>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 3: External API Response Status & Fallback Service Router
docs.text:
Calls a primary external microservice; if the HTTP response is 200, parses the payload and persists to SQL; otherwise routes to a backup service.

<pipeline description="HTTP API failover router"
    xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
    xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="app_db" driver="sqlite" connection_string="./app_data.db" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <!-- Ingest from Primary Service -->
        <http_client id="fetch_primary_rates"
            url="https://primary.api.example.com/v1/rates"
            method="GET"
            into="RatesPayload"
            status_into="PrimaryStatus"
            timeout="5s"
            on_error="continue" />

        <if id="route_api_response" var="PrimaryStatus" equals="200">
            <then>
                <json_path id="extract_primary" source="RatesPayload" query="$.rates.USD" into="USDRate" />
                <sql id="save_primary" db="app_db">
                    INSERT INTO ExchangeRates (Currency, Rate, Source) VALUES ('USD', {{USDRate}}, 'PrimaryAPI');
                </sql>
            </then>
            <else>
                <!-- Fallback to Secondary Microservice -->
                <http_client id="fetch_backup_rates"
                    url="https://backup.api.example.com/rates/latest"
                    method="GET"
                    into="BackupPayload"
                    status_into="BackupStatus"
                    timeout="10s" />
                <json_path id="extract_backup" source="BackupPayload" query="$.rate" into="USDRate" />
                <sql id="save_backup" db="app_db">
                    INSERT INTO ExchangeRates (Currency, Rate, Source) VALUES ('USD', {{USDRate}}, 'BackupAPI');
                </sql>
            </else>
        </if>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 4: Environment Deployment Gate & Maintenance Window
docs.text:
Checks whether the active deployment is running in production and whether MAINTENANCE_WINDOW is set to open.

<pipeline description="Gated production batch operation"
    xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
    xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="DEPLOY_ENV" type="string" value="production" />
        <variable name="MAINTENANCE_WINDOW" type="string" value="open" />
    </variables>

    <databases>
        <database name="warehouse" driver="sqlite" connection_string="./warehouse.db" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <!-- Gated Execution -->
        <if id="gate_maintenance" var="MAINTENANCE_WINDOW" equals="open">
            <then>
                <group id="PerformHeavyMaintenance" transaction="true" db="warehouse">
                    <sql id="rebuild_indexes" db="warehouse">
                        VACUUM;
                    </sql>
                    <script id="notify_ops" language="powershell">
                        Write-Host "Production maintenance completed successfully."
                    </script>
                </group>
            </then>
            <else>
                <script id="skip_maintenance" language="powershell">
                    Write-Host "Maintenance window is CLOSED. Skipping heavy index rebuild."
                </script>
            </else>
        </if>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 5: Local File Cache Gate with Conditional Download
docs.text:
Checks if an output file exists and is populated. If not cached, downloads the dataset from a remote URL and caches it to disk.

<pipeline description="Local file cache with conditional remote download"
    xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
    xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="CacheFile" type="string" value="cache/catalog.json" />
        <variable name="CacheValid" type="string" value="false" />
    </variables>

    <flow>
        <!-- Check cache file on disk -->
        <script id="check_cache_exists" language="go" output_variable="CacheValid">
            <![CDATA[
            package main
            import (
                "fmt"
                "host/vars"
                "os"
            )
            func main() {
                path := vars.GetString("CacheFile")
                if fi, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil && fi.Size() > 0 {
                    fmt.Println("true")
                } else {
                    fmt.Println("false")
                }
            }
            ]]>
        </script>

        <if id="evaluate_cache" var="CacheValid" equals="true">
            <then>
                <file_read id="read_cache" file="{{CacheFile}}" into="CatalogData" />
            </then>
            <else>
                <!-- Fetch and write cache -->
                <http_client id="download_catalog" url="https://api.example.com/catalog.json" into="CatalogData" />
                <file_save id="persist_cache" file="{{CacheFile}}" var="CatalogData" mode="overwrite" />
            </else>
        </if>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Guide: JSONPath Extraction Node (<json_path>)
docs.text: The <json_path> node provides lightweight, native querying and filtering over JSON documents in the Flow Pipeline Engine. It supports reading inputs from files or environment variables, evaluates expressions using JSONPath syntax, and structures outputs in multiple formats.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
• id (string, optional): Unique step identifier for logging and tracking.
  • file (string, optional): Path to the source JSON file on disk. Supports variable interpolation (e.g. {{json_path}}).
  • var (string, optional): Name of the pipeline variable containing the raw JSON string to query.
  • jsonpath or path (string, optional): The JSONPath query expression to execute.
  • mode (string, optional): Defines the formatting style of the output:
  • "value" (default): Returns string values or stringified raw nodes. Multiple matched nodes are joined by newlines.
  • "json": Returns a single JSON-serialized element (if exactly one is matched).
  • "json_array": Returns all matching elements serialized as a single JSON array list.
  • output_var or out_var (string, required): Variable key to store the resulting output.

[!NOTE] If neither jsonpath nor path attributes are defined, the engine automatically extracts the JSONPath expression from the inner tag text of the node.

docs.title: 💡 Examples
docs.text: The following examples demonstrate common workflows using <json_path>.

docs.title: Example 1: Standard Extraction (Default "value" Mode)
docs.text:
Extracts simple scalar values from an external file and joins the matched results into a newline-separated string.

Source JSON File (books.json): 

{
  "store": {
    "books": [
      { "title": "Sayings of the Century", "category": "reference" },
      { "title": "Sword of Honour", "category": "fiction" }
    ]
  }
}

XML Pipeline Definition: 

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
  <variables>
    <variable name="src_file" type="string" value="books.json" />
  </variables>
<flow>
  <!-- Query all titles in default text-join mode -->
  <json_path id="get_titles" file="{{src_file}}" jsonpath="$.store.books[*].title" output_var="book_titles" />
</flow>
</pipeline>

Resulting Output (book_titles): 

Sayings of the Century
Sword of Honour

docs.title: Example 2: Extracting Lists (mode="json_array")
docs.text:
Extracts and serialized matched objects or numeric arrays as a structured JSON array suitable for passing to downstream APIs.

XML Pipeline Definition: 

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
  <flow>
  <!-- Extract all book categories as a serialized JSON string array -->
  <json_path id="get_categories" 
             file="books.json" 
             jsonpath="$.store.books[*].category" 
             mode="json_array" 
             output_var="categories_json" />
  </flow>
</pipeline>

Resulting Output (categories_json): 

["reference", "fiction"]

docs.title: Example 3: Extracting Single Objects (mode="json")
docs.text:
Extracts a specific nested object node and serializes it directly to a clean JSON string block.

XML Pipeline Definition: 

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
  <flow>
  <!-- Extract only the first book object -->
  <json_path id="get_first_book" 
             file="books.json" 
             jsonpath="$.store.books[0]" 
             mode="json" 
             output_var="first_book" />
  </flow>
</pipeline>

Resulting Output (first_book): 

{"title": "Sayings of the Century", "category": "reference"}

docs.title: Example 4: Expression Filters & Variable Interpolation
docs.text:
Combines expression-based filtering (such as price filters) with dynamic variable interpolation to query a document based on runtime pipeline values.

Source JSON File (store.json): 

{
  "store": {
    "bicycle": { "color": "red", "price": 19.95 },
    "unicycle": { "color": "blue", "price": 45.00 }
  }
}

XML Pipeline Definition: 

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
  <variables>
    <variable name="max_price" type="string" value="25.00" />
  </variables>

  <flow>
    <!-- Select only items with price less than the max_price variable value -->
    <json_path id="filter_by_price" 
               file="store.json" 
               jsonpath="$.store.*[?(@.price < {{max_price}})].color" 
               output_var="cheap_colors" />
  </flow>
</pipeline>

Resulting Output (cheap_colors): 

red

docs.title: Example 5: Inline Expression Definitions
docs.text:
For complex JSONPath syntax that contains many special characters, specify the query expression inside the tag body content rather than as an attribute.

XML Pipeline Definition: 

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
  <variables>
    <variable name="raw_payload" type="string" value='{"employees": [{"name": "Alice", "role": "developer"}, {"name": "Bob", "role": "manager"}]}' />
  </variables>
  <flow>
  <!-- Uses chardata body text as the JSONPath expression and stores output variables -->
  <json_path id="get_developers" var="raw_payload" output_var="dev_names">
    $.employees[?(@.role == "developer")].name
  </json_path>
  </flow>
</pipeline>

Resulting Output (dev_names): 

Alice

             file="books.json" 
             jsonpath="$.store.books[0]" 
             mode="json" 
             output_var="first_book" />
  </flow>
</pipeline>

Resulting Output (first_book): 

{"title": "Sayings of the Century", "category": "reference"}

docs.title: Example 4: Expression Filters & Variable Interpolation
docs.text:
Combines expression-based filtering (such as price filters) with dynamic variable interpolation to query a document based on runtime pipeline values.

Source JSON File (store.json): 

{
  "store": {
    "bicycle": { "color": "red", "price": 19.95 },
    "unicycle": { "color": "blue", "price": 45.00 }
  }
}

XML Pipeline Definition: 

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
  <variables>
    <variable name="max_price" type="string" value="25.00" />
  </variables>

  <flow>
    <!-- Select only items with price less than the max_price variable value -->
    <json_path id="filter_by_price" 
               file="store.json" 
               jsonpath="$.store.*[?(@.price < {{max_price}})].color" 
               output_var="cheap_colors" />
  </flow>
  </pipeline>

Resulting Output (cheap_colors): 

red

docs.title: Example 5: Inline Expression Definitions
docs.text:
For complex JSONPath syntax that contains many special characters, specify the query expression inside the tag body content rather than as an attribute.

XML Pipeline Definition: 

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
  <variables>
    <variable name="raw_payload" type="string" value='{"employees": [{"name": "Alice", "role": "developer"}, {"name": "Bob", "role": "manager"}]}' />
  </variables>
  <flow>
  <!-- Uses chardata body text as the JSONPath expression and stores output variables -->
  <json_path id="get_developers" var="raw_payload" output_var="dev_names">
    $.employees[?(@.role == "developer")].name
  </json_path>
  </flow>
</pipeline>

Resulting Output (dev_names): 

Alice

docs.title: Key-Value (KV) Store Integration
docs.text: This guide covers how to configure and execute operations against Key-Value databases within the flow pipeline orchestration library. The engine supports both embedded key-value stores (bbolt, BadgerDB) and server-based instances (Redis/Valkey, etcd).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The KV engine provides two primary execution nodes: * <kv>: Executes individual atomic operations (get, put/set, delete/del, scan/list). Returns logs and outputs compatible with standard <sql> nodes. * <kv_bulk>: Performs high-throughput streaming and ETL between SQL databases and Key-Value stores. Reports progress compatible with <sql_bulk> nodes.

docs.title: Supported Drivers
docs.text: Driver Name Type Connection String Syntax Primary Use Case bbolt / bolt Embedded /path/to/database.db Lightweight local caching, transactional state persistence badger Embedded /path/to/data_dir High-write throughput embedded storage redis / valkey Server redis://:password@localhost:6379/0 High-speed shared in-memory caching and messaging etcd Server http://127.0.0.1:2379,http://127.0.0.1:22379 Distributed consensus, dynamic configuration management

docs.title: Database Configuration
docs.text: Define KV connections inside the <databases> XML container. Connection strings support standard variable interpolation ({{VarName}}).

docs.title: Embedded Key-Value Database (bbolt)
docs.text:
For embedded stores like bbolt, pass the target file path in connection_string. The engine creates parent directories automatically if they do not exist.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">

<databases>
    <database 
        name="local_cache" 
        driver="bbolt" 
        connection_string="./data/app_cache.db" />
</databases>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Server-Based Key-Value Database (Redis)
docs.text:
<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
<databases>
    <database 
        name="redis_store" 
        driver="redis" 
        connection_string="redis://:secret_pass@127.0.0.1:6379/0" />
</databases>
</pipeline>

docs.title:
1.Single Operations ()

Executes point reads, writes, deletions, or range scans against a target bucket/namespace.

Attribute Required Default Description id No Auto Unique execution step identifier. db Yes — Target database connection handle. bucket No default Bucket name (bbolt/BadgerDB) or key prefix namespace (Redis/etcd). op No * Operation type: get, put/set, delete/del, scan/list. key No * Target record key. value No * Record value payload for write operations. var No — Environment variable containing a dynamic DSL string. output_var No LAST_OUTPUT Variable that receives the command output or value. * Note: Operations, keys, and values can be defined via XML attributes or inline body DSL text.

Result Formatting

<kv> returns standard result logs compatible with <sql> execution observability: - Write Ops (put, delete): Logs (1 row(s) affected). - Read Ops (get, scan): Formats tabular outputs (KEY\tVALUE\n...) and logs (N row(s) returned).

2. Bulk Operations ()

Streams data sets directly between relational SQL queries and Key-Value buckets. |Attribute|Required|Default|Description| | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | |id|No|Auto|Unique execution step identifier.| |db|Yes|—|Source database connection handle.| |target_db|No|db|Destination database connection handle (KV or SQL).| |target_bucket|No|—|Target KV bucket or namespace receiving streamed records.| |batch_size|No|10000|Number of key-value pairs written per commit chunk.| |output_var|No|—|Variable receiving the total count of transferred records.|

  • Note: Bulk operations are optimized for high-throughput data transfer between SQL and KV stores.
  • Note: The target_db and target_bucket attributes must be correctly specified to ensure successful data transfer.
Observability & Error Handling
docs.text: All and operations emit lifecycle telemetry events captured by standard observers and event sinks: * Attempt Tracking: Execution start/finish duration, row count metrics (read, written, affected), and attempt status (succeeded, failed, canceled). * Error Classification: File lock errors, invalid buckets, missing connection handles, or network disconnects are mapped to standard ErrorClass definitions (e.g., ErrorClassFileSystem, ErrorClassDatabase). * Redaction: Sensitive keys or value strings matching security patterns are masked in error outputs.

docs.title: Concurrent Step Execution: <parallel>
docs.text: The <parallel> component executes multiple child tasks or branches concurrently across an asynchronous worker thread pool. Rather than executing child tasks sequentially from top to bottom, <parallel> dispatches each child step into a separate goroutine and establishes a synchronized join barrier, ensuring all concurrent operations finish before the pipeline advances to the subsequent step.

docs.title: Architecture & Lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Start([Enter <parallel>]) --> PoolConfig["Initialize Worker Pool<br/>(max_threads=N, default: 4)"]
    PoolConfig --> Dispatch["Spawn Concurrent Worker Threads"]

    subgraph Concurrent Execution
        direction TB
        Dispatch --> BranchA["Branch 1: SQL Pre-check"]
        Dispatch --> BranchB["Branch 2: API HTTP Call"]
        Dispatch --> BranchC["Branch 3: Bulk ETL Extract"]
        Dispatch --> BranchD["Branch 4: File Processing"]
    end

    BranchA --> Barrier{{"Join Barrier / Sync Barrier<br/>(sync.WaitGroup)"}}
    BranchB --> Barrier
    BranchC --> Barrier
    BranchD --> Barrier

    Barrier --> ErrorCheck{"Any Branch Failed?"}
    ErrorCheck -- Yes --> ErrorPolicy["Apply on_error Policy<br/>(stop / continue / retry)"]
    ErrorCheck -- No --> Advance(["Advance to Next Pipeline Step"])
    ErrorPolicy --> Advance

docs.title: Attribute Reference
docs.text: Attribute Type Default Mandatory Description id string (generated) No Unique identifier for the parallel step. Used for logging, metrics, and tracing. max_threads positiveInteger 4 No Maximum number of concurrent worker threads/goroutines allowed to execute simultaneously. threads positiveInteger 4 No Alias for max_threads. Defines concurrency limit. concurrency positiveInteger 4 No Alias for max_threads. Defines concurrency limit. timeout string (none) No Maximum duration for all parallel tasks to complete (e.g. 30s, 5m, 1h). on_error string stop No Action taken if any child branch returns an error: stop (fail pipeline), continue (log and proceed), or retry. description string "" No Human-readable explanation of the parallel operations.

docs.title: 1. Synchronized Join Barrier
docs.text:
When <parallel> begins, child tasks are queued and assigned to the worker pool. The orchestrator halts forward progress on the main flow until all child branches have either completed successfully or terminated with an error.

flowchart LR
    Seq1["Sequential Step 1"] --> ParStart["<parallel> Entry"]
    ParStart --> Worker1["Worker Goroutine 1"]
    ParStart --> Worker2["Worker Goroutine 2"]
    ParStart --> Worker3["Worker Goroutine 3"]
    Worker1 --> Join(("Join Barrier"))
    Worker2 --> Join
    Worker3 --> Join
    Join --> Seq2["Sequential Step 2"]

docs.title: 2. Database Connection Pooling Considerations
docs.text:
When running multiple <sql> or <sql_bulk> nodes concurrently within <parallel>, ensure that the underlying <database> connection pool has enough capacity: - Increase max_open_conns on your <database> definition to match or exceed max_threads. - If max_threads="8" and max_open_conns="2", worker tasks will wait in a database queue, bottlenecking concurrency.

<database name="analytics_db" 
          connection_string="{{AnalyticsConnStr}}" 
          max_open_conns="10" 
          max_idle_conns="5" />

docs.title: 3. Variable Thread-Safety & Scoping
docs.text:
• Input Variables: All child steps can safely read pipeline variables ({{VarName}} or vars.Get*).
  • Output Variables: When concurrent steps write to variables (output_var), ensure each child step writes to an independent variable name (e.g. BRANCH_A_STATUS, BRANCH_B_STATUS) to avoid race conditions.

docs.title: Example 1: Parallel Health Check Across Multiple Systems
docs.text:
Query multiple databases concurrently to determine synchronization state before taking action.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
    xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="SourceConn" type="string" value="sqlserver://SRV01:1433?database=AppDB&integrated+security=true" />
        <variable name="TargetConn" type="string" value="sqlserver://SRV02:1433?database=ReportingDB&integrated+security=true" />
        <variable name="SOURCE_MAX_DATE" type="string" value="" />
        <variable name="TARGET_MAX_DATE" type="string" value="" />
    </variables>

    <databases>
        <database name="src_db" connection_string="{{SourceConn}}" max_open_conns="4" />
        <database name="tgt_db" connection_string="{{TargetConn}}" max_open_conns="4" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <!-- Execute both queries at the same time -->
        <parallel id="fetch_max_timestamps" max_threads="2" description="Query source and target databases in parallel">
            <sql id="get_source_max" db="src_db" output_var="SOURCE_MAX_DATE">
                SELECT ISNULL(MAX(UpdatedAt), '1970-01-01') AS SOURCE_MAX_DATE FROM dbo.Orders;
            </sql>
            <sql id="get_target_max" db="tgt_db" output_var="TARGET_MAX_DATE">
                SELECT ISNULL(MAX(UpdatedAt), '1970-01-01') AS TARGET_MAX_DATE FROM dbo.OrdersArchive;
            </sql>
        </parallel>

        <!-- Fast comparison script evaluating delta condition -->
        <script id="compare_timestamps" language="go" output_variable="NEEDS_ACTION"
            description="Evaluate whether source date exceeds target date">
            <![CDATA[
            package main
            import (
                "fmt"
                "host/vars"
            )
            func main() {
                src := vars.GetString("SOURCE_MAX_DATE")
                tgt := vars.GetString("TARGET_MAX_DATE")
                if src != "" && tgt != "" && src != tgt {
                    fmt.Println("true")
                } else {
                    fmt.Println("false")
                }
            }
            ]]>
        </script>

        <!-- Process findings: sync delta if dates diverge -->
        <if id="check_sync_action" var="NEEDS_ACTION" equals="true">
            <then>
                <sql_bulk id="sync_delta" db="src_db" target_db="tgt_db" target_table="dbo.OrdersArchive" batch_size="10000"
                    description="Bulk stream modified delta rows">
                    <![CDATA[
                    SELECT * FROM dbo.Orders WHERE UpdatedAt > '{{TARGET_MAX_DATE}}';
                    ]]>
                </sql_bulk>
            </then>
            <else>
                <script id="log_in_sync" language="go">
                    <![CDATA[
                    package main
                    import "fmt"
                    func main() { fmt.Println("Target archive is fully up to date. No sync needed.") }
                    ]]>
                </script>
            </else>
        </if>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 2: Concurrent API Ingestion and Staging
docs.text:
Fetch disparate datasets from external REST endpoints in parallel, save them to local storage, and extract JSON payloads.

<pipeline description="Fetch multiple external data feeds concurrently"
    xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
    xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="ApiKey" type="string" value="secret_live_token" />
        <variable name="RatesJson" type="string" value="" />
        <variable name="UsersJson" type="string" value="" />
    </variables>

    <flow>
        <parallel id="parallel_ingestion" max_threads="4" description="Download currency and user data simultaneously">
            <!-- Branch 1: Exchange Rates -->
            <http_client id="fetch_rates" url="https://api.example.com/v1/rates" method="GET" into="RatesJson">
                <headers>
                    <header name="Authorization">Bearer {{ApiKey}}</header>
                </headers>
            </http_client>

            <!-- Branch 2: Active User Profiles -->
            <http_client id="fetch_users" url="https://api.example.com/v1/users/active" method="GET" into="UsersJson">
                <headers>
                    <header name="Authorization">Bearer {{ApiKey}}</header>
                </headers>
            </http_client>
        </parallel>

        <!-- Parse responses after both downloads finish -->
        <json_path id="extract_usd_rate" source="var" var="RatesJson" query="$.rates.USD" into="USD_RATE" />
        <json_path id="extract_user_count" source="var" var="UsersJson" query="$.total_count" into="TOTAL_USERS" />
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 3: Multi-Table Archive & Cleanup Operations
docs.text:
Execute independent maintenance statements concurrently across large reporting tables.

<pipeline description="Parallel table maintenance"
    xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
    xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="warehouse_db" 
                  connection_string="sqlserver://WH01:1433?database=Warehouse&integrated+security=true" 
                  max_open_conns="10" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <parallel id="nightly_maintenance" max_threads="3" timeout="15m" description="Run archive purges concurrently">
            <sql id="purge_audit_logs" db="warehouse_db">
                DELETE FROM dbo.AuditLog WHERE CreatedAt < DATEADD(DAY, -90, GETUTCDATE());
            </sql>
            <sql id="purge_session_cache" db="warehouse_db">
                DELETE FROM dbo.SessionCache WHERE ExpiresAt < GETUTCDATE();
            </sql>
            <sql id="rebuild_stage_indexes" db="warehouse_db">
                ALTER INDEX ALL ON dbo.StagingEvents REBUILD;
            </sql>
        </parallel>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 4: Concurrent File Transformations
docs.text:
Read multiple local data files simultaneously, run transformation scripts, and export formatted reports.

<pipeline description="Parallel report extraction"
    xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
    xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <flow>
        <parallel id="generate_department_reports" max_threads="3">
            <excel_read id="read_finance" file="./data/finance_q3.xlsx" sheet="Summary" output_var="FINANCE_DATA" />
            <excel_read id="read_sales" file="./data/sales_q3.xlsx" sheet="Summary" output_var="SALES_DATA" />
            <file_read id="read_hr_csv" path="./data/hr_headcount.csv" into="HR_DATA" />
        </parallel>

        <assert id="validate_finance_loaded" var="FINANCE_DATA" condition="ne .FINANCE_DATA \"\"" message="Finance data missing" />
        <assert id="validate_sales_loaded" var="SALES_DATA" condition="ne .SALES_DATA \"\"" message="Sales data missing" />
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 5: High-Throughput Bulk Replication Across Multiple Target Tables
docs.text:
Stream extracts concurrently from a core database into multiple target tables on an analytics server.

<pipeline description="Concurrent multi-table replication"
    xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
    xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="oltp_db" connection_string="sqlserver://OLTP:1433?database=Core&integrated+security=true" max_open_conns="8" />
        <database name="olap_db" connection_string="sqlserver://OLAP:1433?database=Analytics&integrated+security=true" max_open_conns="8" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <parallel id="bulk_replicate_all" max_threads="3" timeout="30m">
            <sql_bulk id="copy_customers" db="oltp_db" target_db="olap_db" target_table="dbo.DimCustomers" batch_size="25000" tablock="true">
                SELECT CustomerID, AccountNumber, Name, TerritoryID, ModifiedDate FROM Sales.Customer;
            </sql_bulk>
            <sql_bulk id="copy_products" db="oltp_db" target_db="olap_db" target_table="dbo.DimProducts" batch_size="25000" tablock="true">
                SELECT ProductID, Name, ProductNumber, StandardCost, ListPrice FROM Production.Product;
            </sql_bulk>
            <sql_bulk id="copy_territories" db="oltp_db" target_db="olap_db" target_table="dbo.DimTerritory" batch_size="5000" tablock="true">
                SELECT TerritoryID, Name, CountryRegionCode, [Group] FROM Sales.SalesTerritory;
            </sql_bulk>
        </parallel>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Best Practices & Troubleshooting
docs.text:
[!TIP] Right-size max_threads: Default is 4. Avoid setting max_threads higher than the number of available CPU cores or database connection limits, as excess goroutines cause thread thrashing and connection pool exhaustion.

[!IMPORTANT] Independent Output Variables: Never configure two parallel branches to output into the same variable name. Each concurrent branch should write to a uniquely named variable.

[!WARNING] Deadlock Prevention: If multiple concurrent branches interact with the same database, ensure they modify disjoint sets of rows or tables to prevent database transaction deadlocks.

docs.title: Preflight Nodes: Setup and Validation
docs.text:
Preflight nodes are designed to run environment checks, initializations, and structural assertions before the main data-streaming pipelines (<flow>) are executed. This ensures that resources are available, configurations are correct, and the pipeline fails fast before performing heavy ETL operations.

[!IMPORTANT] No Flow Execution during Preflight: Running a <preflight> block does not execute the main <flow> pipeline nodes. It is intended as a non-destructive runtime validation/test run to guarantee that running in a specific environment with those precise variables and configuration will execute exactly as intended. Once validation is complete, the pipeline can later be run in production without the preflight overhead.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Separation of Concerns: Preflight nodes and flow nodes are separated during XML parsing into PreflightNodes and FlowNodes respectively.
  2. Preflight-Only Execution: Preflight checks are executed by passing cfg.PreflightNodes to the pipeline Executor. The <flow> block is ignored during this execution step.
  3. Fail-Fast Design: If any preflight node fails or returns an error, the execution can be halted immediately, preventing the main <flow> from running with incorrect or missing parameters.

docs.title: Is the Flow Executed During Preflight?
docs.text:
[!CAUTION] NO. The main <flow> block is never executed when running a preflight check.

Preflight is explicitly intended as a runtime validation and test run. Its core purposes are: * To ensure that the application can run in the target environment. * To verify that all required environment variables are set and reachable. * To confirm that the specific configuration file compiles and executes safely.

Once the preflight validation passes successfully, you can be highly confident that running the same configuration file later with the preflight block omitted (or skipped) will execute exactly as intended.

docs.title: Is Preflight Executed When Running the Flow?
docs.text:
[!IMPORTANT] NO. The <preflight> block is never executed when running the flow normally.

The executor only executes the slice of nodes explicitly passed to Execute(ctx, nodes). If you wish to run the pipeline, you must choose whether to run preflight validation, flow execution, or both:

// OPTION A: Run flow only (Skipping preflight checks entirely)
results, err := executor.Execute(ctx, cfg.FlowNodes)

// OPTION B: Safe Run (Preflight checks first, then Flow)
_, err := executor.Execute(ctx, cfg.PreflightNodes)
if err == nil {
    results, err := executor.Execute(ctx, cfg.FlowNodes)
}

docs.title: XML Schema Syntax
docs.text:
A preflight block is defined using the <preflight> element. Within this block, you can place standard pipeline AST nodes such as <script>, <file_save>, <file_read>, and <assert>:

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <preflight>
        <!-- Preflight tasks here -->
    </preflight>

    <flow>
        <!-- Main ETL flow here -->
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 1: Environment Verification
docs.text:
This example checks if the correct database connectivity is established and that critical environment variables are set before proceeding.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="ENV" type="string" value="staging" />
    </variables>

    <preflight>
        <!-- 1. Assert that we are not in production if running tests -->
        <assert id="check_env" var="ENV" equals="production" operator="!=" message="Warning: Running in production!" on_failure="warn" />

        <!-- 2. Verify we can fetch the system status -->
        <script id="ping_service" language="go">
            package main
            import (
                "net/http"
                "os"
            )
            func main() {
                resp, err := http.Head("https://api.yourdomain.com/health")
                if err != nil || resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
                    println("API service is offline")
                    os.Exit(1)
                }
            }
        </script>
    </preflight>

    <flow>
        <!-- Flow starts only if preflight check passes -->
        <script id="load_data" language="go">
            package main
            func main() {
                println("Streaming data...")
            }
        </script>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 2: Directory Preparation
docs.text:
This example ensures that the destination folder structure exists and logs a marker file before downloading bulk records.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="EXPORT_DIR" type="string" value="./exports" />
    </variables>

    <preflight>
        <!-- 1. Run shell script to create directories -->
        <script id="make_dir" language="bash">
            mkdir -p {{EXPORT_DIR}}
        </script>

        <!-- 2. Write a marker indicating preflight run started -->
        <file_save id="preflight_marker" file="{{EXPORT_DIR}}/preflight.log" append="false">
            Preflight started. Ready to receive files.
        </file_save>
    </preflight>

    <flow>
        <file_save id="data_payload" file="{{EXPORT_DIR}}/records.json">
            {"id": 1, "name": "ETL Payload"}
        </file_save>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 3: Schema & Version Assertion
docs.text:
This example reads a remote configuration file or local manifest to assert that the pipeline version is supported.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <preflight>
        <!-- 1. Read local version manifest -->
        <file_read id="read_manifest" file="manifest.json" output_var="MANIFEST_DATA" />

        <!-- 2. Use JSONPath to extract the required version -->
        <json_path id="get_version" var="MANIFEST_DATA" jsonpath="$.version" output_var="CURRENT_VERSION" />

        <!-- 3. Assert that the version meets minimum compatibility -->
        <assert id="check_version" var="CURRENT_VERSION" equals="2.0.0" operator="==" message="Unsupported pipeline version" on_failure="halt" />
    </preflight>

    <flow>
        <script id="execute_migration" language="go">
            package main
            func main() {
                println("Running migration flow...")
            }
        </script>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Split Example: Pipeline Structure vs. Environment Configuration
docs.text: It is common to separate your static pipeline execution structure (pipeline.xml) from dynamic, environment-specific databases and variables (config.xml). Below is an example demonstrating this setup.

docs.title: 1. config.xml (Environment Setup & Env-Specific Preflights)
docs.text:
This file defines environment-specific databases, parameters, and preflight validation checks tailored strictly to this staging environment (e.g., verifying that the staging API is online).

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="ENV" type="string" value="staging" />
        <variable name="API_ENDPOINT" type="string" value="https://staging.api.service.com" />
    </variables>

    <databases>
        <database name="primary_db" driver="postgres" connection_string="host=localhost port=5432 user=db_user dbname=staging_db sslmode=disable" />
    </databases>

    <!-- Staging environment preflight verification -->
    <preflight>
        <script id="verify_staging_api" language="go">
            package main
            import (
                "net/http"
                "os"
            )
            func main() {
                resp, err := http.Head("https://staging.api.service.com/health")
                if err != nil || resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
                    println("Staging API is unreachable!")
                    os.Exit(1)
                }
            }
        </script>
    </preflight>
</pipeline>

docs.title: 2. pipeline.xml (Pipeline Logic & General Preflight)
docs.text:
This file defines the general validation logic (within <preflight>) and the heavy data movement tasks (within <flow>), completely independent of hardcoded credentials.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <preflight>
        <!-- Ensure we are running against correct environment configuration -->
        <assert id="assert_staging" var="ENV" equals="staging" operator="==" message="Incorrect environment detected!" on_failure="halt" />

        <!-- Verify database connection from config.xml before flowing -->
        <sql id="verify_db" db="primary_db">
            SELECT 1;
        </sql>
    </preflight>

    <flow>
        <!-- Execute ETL query against primary_db defined in config.xml -->
        <sql id="stream_records" db="primary_db">
            SELECT * FROM users_staging;
        </sql>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: 3. Orchestrating Split Files in Go
docs.text:
To parse and execute both files together, load them sequentially into your ParseXMLConfig parser, merge the PreflightNodes from both PipelineConfig outputs, and run them sequentially:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "io/ioutil"
    "log"
    "github.com/etl-madness/flow"
)

func main() {
    // Read and parse environmental config
    configData, _ := ioutil.ReadFile("config.xml")
    envCfg, _ := flow.ParseXMLConfig(configData)

    // Read and parse structural pipeline
    pipelineData, _ := ioutil.ReadFile("pipeline.xml")
    pipeCfg, _ := flow.ParseXMLConfig(pipelineData)

    // Initialize Registry with both databases and variables
    registry := flow.NewRegistry()
    registry.InitVariables(envCfg.Variables)
    registry.InitDatabases(envCfg.Databases)

    executor := flow.NewExecutor(registry)

    // Merge env-specific and pipeline-specific preflights
    allPreflights := append(envCfg.PreflightNodes, pipeCfg.PreflightNodes...)

    // Safe Test Run / Preflight
    log.Println("Running combined preflight validation...")
    _, err := executor.Execute(context.Background(), allPreflights)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("Preflight failed! Flow aborted: %v", err)
    }

    // Execution of flow (only reaches here if all preflight checks pass)
    log.Println("Preflight passed successfully. Executing pipeline flow...")
    _, err = executor.Execute(context.Background(), pipeCfg.FlowNodes)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("Flow execution failed: %v", err)
    }
}

docs.title: <script> Node Reference & Cross-Platform Guide
docs.text:
The <script> node executes dynamic code within an ETL Madness Flow pipeline. It bridges declarative XML workflow orchestration with programmatic logic, enabling custom transformations, system checks, file manipulations, API integrations, and database operations.

Flow supports multiple scripting engines, ranging from its built-in zero-dependency Go interpreter (which runs identically on Windows, Linux, and macOS without requiring any compiler or runtime installation) to platform shells (PowerShell, Bash, POSIX sh, Zsh, Cmd) and .NET Script (CSX).

docs.title: 1. Complete Attribute Specification
docs.text:
The <script> node accepts the following attributes:

Attribute XML Schema Type Default Description id xs:string Auto (script_N) Unique step identifier used for logging, telemetry, and execution flow tracking. language / lang xs:string powershell (in Builder) The script engine or interpreter runtime (e.g., go, powershell, pwsh, bash, sh, cmd, git-bash, zsh, csx, sql). output_var / output_variable / out_var xs:string None Pipeline variable name that receives the captured standard output (stdout) of the script. var / variable xs:string None Name of an existing pipeline variable containing the script code to execute. When specified, overrides the XML body content. timeout xs:string None Maximum execution duration before terminating the script (e.g., 10s, 45s, 5m, 1h). description xs:string None Human-readable explanation displayed in logs, Mermaid flowcharts, and HTML execution summaries. on_error xs:string stop Failure policy when the script exits with a non-zero code (stop, continue, retry). retry_count xs:int 0 Number of retry attempts when on_error="retry". retry_interval xs:string 1s Delay duration between retry attempts (e.g., 2s, 10s). db / database xs:string None Database connection alias for language="sql" or database-bound operations. target_db xs:string None Destination database connection alias for cross-database streaming. target_table xs:string None Target table name for streaming operations. batch_size xs:int 500 Chunk batch size for bulk data operations.

docs.title: 2. Supported Runtimes & Cross-Platform Compatibility Matrix
docs.text:
Runtime / Engine language Value(s) Windows Linux macOS Dependencies Notes Interpreted Go go ✅ ✅ ✅ None (Built into Flow binary via Yaegi) Recommended for multi-platform pipelines. Native access to Go standard library, host/vars, and host/db. PowerShell Core pwsh ✅ ✅ ✅ pwsh in PATH Modern cross-platform PowerShell (v7+). Runs identically across OS platforms. Windows PowerShell powershell ✅ ❌ ❌ Pre-installed on Windows (powershell.exe) Windows PowerShell 5.1. Executes with -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass. GNU Bash bash ⚠️ ✅ ✅ /bin/bash or bash in PATH Native on Linux/macOS. Requires Git Bash, MSYS2, or WSL on Windows. POSIX Shell shell, sh ⚠️ ✅ ✅ /bin/sh or sh in PATH Lightweight POSIX script. On Windows falls back to available sh.exe or cmd.exe. Windows Command cmd ✅ ❌ ❌ Windows native (cmd.exe /c) Legacy batch scripts (.bat / .cmd). Windows only. Git Bash git-bash, gitbash ✅ ⚠️ ⚠️ Git for Windows installed Specifically targets Git's Bash binary on Windows (C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe). Z Shell zsh ❌ ✅ ✅ /bin/zsh Default login shell on modern macOS; standard on Linux. C# Script (.NET) csx, dotnet-script ✅ ✅ ✅ dotnet-script CLI tool Executes C# code with Roslyn compiler. Requires .NET SDK and dotnet-script. SQL Script sql ✅ ✅ ✅ Configured <database> in pipeline Executes native SQL against target database connection.

[!TIP] Cross-Platform Recommendation: For pipelines intended to run seamlessly across Windows, Linux containers, and macOS runners, prefer language="go". Because the Go interpreter is embedded directly within the Flow executable, your pipeline requires zero external software or interpreter installations on target machines.

docs.title: 3. Variable Passing & Output Capture Mechanics
docs.text:
There are two primary mechanisms for sharing data between the Flow pipeline and scripts:

flowchart LR
    subgraph FlowEngine ["Flow Engine Context"]
        Registry["Pipeline Variable Registry<br/>{{VarName}}"]
    end

    subgraph ScriptExecution ["Script Step Execution"]
        Direction1["1. Pre-Execution Interpolation<br/>{{VarName}} replaced in source text"]
        Direction2["2. Host API Access<br/>host/vars.GetString('VarName')"]
        Direction3["3. Output Variable Capture<br/>stdout captured into output_var"]
    end

    Registry --> Direction1 --> ScriptExecution
    Registry <--> Direction2 <--> ScriptExecution
    ScriptExecution --> Direction3 --> Registry

docs.title: 1. Template Interpolation ({{VarName}})
docs.text: Before any script runs, Flow scans the script content and replaces all {{VarName}} placeholders with their current runtime values. - Works across all script languages (go, bash, powershell, cmd, csx). - Evaluated prior to passing code to the interpreter.

docs.title: 2. Built-in Host APIs (Go Scripts Only)
docs.text:
Go scripts can import the built-in host package "host/vars" for dynamic, typed interaction with the pipeline variable registry:

package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "host/vars"
)

func main() {
    // Read typed variables
    server := vars.GetString("ServerHost")
    port   := vars.GetInt("ServerPort")
    active := vars.GetBool("IsProduction")
    rate   := vars.GetFloat("ExchangeRate")

    // Write back directly to the pipeline registry
    vars.Set("ProcessedCount", 42)
    vars.SetString("StatusMessage", "All records validated")
}

docs.title: 3. Capturing Output via output_var
docs.text: Any content written to standard output (stdout / fmt.Print / Write-Host / echo / Console.Write) is captured by the engine and stored in the variable named by output_var: - Subsequent pipeline steps can reference this variable via {{VariableName}} or vars.GetString("VariableName"). - Trailing newlines (\r\n or \n) are trimmed automatically to prevent formatting discrepancies.

docs.title: 4. Cross-Platform Scripting Best Practices
docs.text:
When writing scripts designed to run on multiple operating systems:

  1. Path Separators: Avoid hardcoding \ or /.
  2. In Go: Use filepath.Join("folder", "file.csv") or filepath.FromSlash(path).
  3. In PowerShell: Use Join-Path $folder $file.
  4. In Bash: Always use forward slashes /.
  5. Line Endings (CRLF vs. LF):
  6. Windows outputs \r\n; Unix outputs \n.
  7. When checking string equality in conditions (<if>), trim whitespace or normalize returns.
  8. Quoting and CDATA:
  9. Always wrap script source inside an XML <![CDATA[ ... ]]> block to avoid XML entity conflicts (<, >, &, ").
  10. Environment Variables:
  11. Windows environment variable names are case-insensitive; Linux and macOS are strictly case-sensitive.
  12. Use pipeline variables ({{MyVar}} or vars.GetString("MyVar")) instead of system environment variables whenever possible.

docs.title: Example 1: Universal Cross-Platform File Inspection (language="go")
docs.text:
This script inspects a directory, calculates file sizes and MD5 hashes, and outputs a JSON summary. It runs identically on Windows, Linux, and macOS with zero external dependencies.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="TargetDir" type="string" value="./data_inbound" />
        <variable name="FileManifest" type="string" value="" />
    </variables>

    <flow>
        <script id="ScanDirectory" language="go" output_var="FileManifest">
            <![CDATA[
            package main

            import (
                "crypto/md5"
                "encoding/hex"
                "encoding/json"
                "fmt"
                "io"
                "os"
                "path/filepath"
                "time"
                "host/vars"
            )

            type FileInfo struct {
                Name      string    `json:"name"`
                Path      string    `json:"path"`
                SizeBytes int64     `json:"size_bytes"`
                MD5       string    `json:"md5"`
                Modified  time.Time `json:"modified"`
            }

            func getFileMD5(filePath string) (string, error) {
                f, err := os.Open(filePath)
                if err != nil {
                    return "", err
                }
                defer f.Close()

                h := md5.New()
                if _, err := io.Copy(h, f); err != nil {
                    return "", err
                }
                return hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil)), nil
            }

            func main() {
                dir := vars.GetString("TargetDir")
                if dir == "" {
                    dir = "."
                }

                var files []FileInfo
                entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
                if err != nil {
                    fmt.Printf("[]")
                    return
                }

                for _, entry := range entries {
                    if entry.IsDir() {
                        continue
                    }
                    fullPath := filepath.Join(dir, entry.Name())
                    info, err := entry.Info()
                    if err != nil {
                        continue
                    }

                    hash, _ := getFileMD5(fullPath)
                    files = append(files, FileInfo{
                        Name:      entry.Name(),
                        Path:      filepath.ToSlash(fullPath),
                        SizeBytes: info.Size(),
                        MD5:       hash,
                        Modified:  info.ModTime().UTC(),
                    })
                }

                jsonBytes, _ := json.MarshalIndent(files, "", "  ")
                fmt.Print(string(jsonBytes))
            }
            ]]>
        </script>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 2: OS Detection and Dynamic Platform Routing
docs.text:
Determines the host operating system at runtime using Go's built-in runtime.GOOS, registers the OS name into a pipeline variable, and conditionally executes platform-specific actions.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="CurrentOS" type="string" value="" />
        <variable name="HostCores" type="int" value="1" />
    </variables>

    <flow>
        <!-- Step 1: Detect Operating System and Core Count -->
        <script id="DetectHostEnvironment" language="go">
            <![CDATA[
            package main

            import (
                "fmt"
                "runtime"
                "host/vars"
            )

            func main() {
                osName := runtime.GOOS       // "windows", "linux", "darwin"
                arch   := runtime.GOARCH     // "amd64", "arm64"
                cpus   := runtime.NumCPU()

                vars.SetString("CurrentOS", osName)
                vars.Set("HostCores", cpus)

                fmt.Printf("Detected Host OS: %s (%s) with %d CPUs\n", osName, arch, cpus)
            }
            ]]>
        </script>

        <!-- Step 2: Windows Branch -->
        <if id="CheckWindows" var="CurrentOS" equals="windows">
            <then>
                <script id="WindowsLog" language="powershell">
                    <![CDATA[
                    Write-Host "Running on Windows. System Drive: $env:SystemDrive"
                    ]]>
                </script>
            </then>
        </if>

        <!-- Step 3: Linux / macOS Branch -->
        <if id="CheckUnix" var="CurrentOS" equals="linux">
            <then>
                <script id="LinuxLog" language="bash">
                    <![CDATA[
                    echo "Running on Linux. Kernel: $(uname -r), Uptime: $(uptime -p 2>/dev/null || uptime)"
                    ]]>
                </script>
            </then>
        </if>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 3: Cross-Platform Zip Archive Generator (language="go")
docs.text:
Compresses ETL export files into a .zip archive across all platforms without calling external tools like zip, tar, or 7-Zip.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="SourceFolder" type="string" value="./exports" />
        <variable name="ZipFile" type="string" value="./exports_archive.zip" />
        <variable name="ArchivedFilesCount" type="int" value="0" />
    </variables>

    <flow>
        <script id="CreateZipArchive" language="go">
            <![CDATA[
            package main

            import (
                "archive/zip"
                "fmt"
                "io"
                "os"
                "path/filepath"
                "host/vars"
            )

            func main() {
                srcDir  := vars.GetString("SourceFolder")
                zipPath := vars.GetString("ZipFile")

                zipFile, err := os.Create(zipPath)
                if err != nil {
                    fmt.Printf("Failed to create zip file: %v\n", err)
                    return
                }
                defer zipFile.Close()

                archive := zip.NewWriter(zipFile)
                defer archive.Close()

                count := 0
                err = filepath.Walk(srcDir, func(path string, info os.FileInfo, err error) error {
                    if err != nil || info.IsDir() {
                        return err
                    }

                    relPath, err := filepath.Rel(srcDir, path)
                    if err != nil {
                        return err
                    }

                    header, err := zip.FileInfoHeader(info)
                    if err != nil {
                        return err
                    }
                    header.Name = filepath.ToSlash(relPath)
                    header.Method = zip.Deflate

                    writer, err := archive.CreateHeader(header)
                    if err != nil {
                        return err
                    }

                    file, err := os.Open(path)
                    if err != nil {
                        return err
                    }
                    defer file.Close()

                    _, err = io.Copy(writer, file)
                    if err == nil {
                        count++
                    }
                    return err
                })

                vars.Set("ArchivedFilesCount", count)
                fmt.Printf("Successfully packaged %d files into %s\n", count, zipPath)
            }
            ]]>
        </script>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 4: REST API Integration with Bearer Token (language="go")
docs.text:
Issues an HTTP POST request to an external token authority, parses the response JSON, and saves the bearer token into the pipeline registry for downstream <http_client> steps.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="AuthEndpoint" type="string" value="https://auth.internal.example.com/oauth/token" />
        <variable name="ClientId" type="string" value="flow-etl-worker" />
        <variable name="ClientSecret" type="string" value="{{SECURE_CLIENT_SECRET}}" />
        <variable name="AccessToken" type="string" value="" />
    </variables>

    <flow>
        <script id="FetchAuthToken" language="go" timeout="30s">
            <![CDATA[
            package main

            import (
                "bytes"
                "encoding/json"
                "fmt"
                "io"
                "net/http"
                "time"
                "host/vars"
            )

            type TokenResponse struct {
                AccessToken string `json:"access_token"`
                TokenType   string `json:"token_type"`
                ExpiresIn   int    `json:"expires_in"`
            }

            func main() {
                url    := vars.GetString("AuthEndpoint")
                id     := vars.GetString("ClientId")
                secret := vars.GetString("ClientSecret")

                payload := map[string]string{
                    "client_id":     id,
                    "client_secret": secret,
                    "grant_type":    "client_credentials",
                }
                bodyBytes, _ := json.Marshal(payload)

                client := &http.Client{Timeout: 15 * time.Second}
                resp, err := client.Post(url, "application/json", bytes.NewBuffer(bodyBytes))
                if err != nil {
                    fmt.Printf("HTTP Request failed: %v\n", err)
                    return
                }
                defer resp.Body.Close()

                respData, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
                if resp.StatusCode < 200 || resp.StatusCode >= 300 {
                    fmt.Printf("Auth server returned status %d: %s\n", resp.StatusCode, string(respData))
                    return
                }

                var tokenResp TokenResponse
                if err := json.Unmarshal(respData, &tokenResp); err != nil {
                    fmt.Printf("Failed to decode token JSON: %v\n", err)
                    return
                }

                vars.SetString("AccessToken", tokenResp.AccessToken)
                fmt.Printf("Successfully acquired token (expires in %d sec)\n", tokenResp.ExpiresIn)
            }
            ]]>
        </script>

        <!-- Downstream HTTP step consumes the generated token -->
        <http_client id="FetchProtectedData"
                     url="https://api.internal.example.com/v1/customers"
                     method="GET"
                     headers="Authorization:Bearer {{AccessToken}},Accept:application/json"
                     output_var="CustomersJSON" />
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 5: Cross-Platform PowerShell Core (language="pwsh")
docs.text:
Demonstrates modern PowerShell Core (pwsh) syntax that runs identically on Linux, Windows, and macOS to calculate disk storage metrics.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="DiskSpaceReport" type="string" value="" />
    </variables>

    <flow>
        <script id="CheckFreeDiskSpace" language="pwsh" output_var="DiskSpaceReport">
            <![CDATA[
            # Cross-platform .NET DriveInfo works on Windows, Linux, and macOS
            $drives = [System.IO.DriveInfo]::GetDrives() | Where-Object { $_.IsReady -and $_.DriveType -eq 'Fixed' }

            $report = @()
            foreach ($d in $drives) {
                $totalGB = [math]::Round($d.TotalSize / 1GB, 2)
                $freeGB  = [math]::Round($d.AvailableFreeSpace / 1GB, 2)
                $pctFree = [math]::Round(($freeGB / $totalGB) * 100, 1)

                $report += [PSCustomObject]@{
                    RootDirectory = $d.RootDirectory.FullName
                    TotalGB       = $totalGB
                    FreeGB        = $freeGB
                    PercentFree   = $pctFree
                }
            }

            $report | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
            ]]>
        </script>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 6: Cross-Platform POSIX Shell Script (language="sh")
docs.text:
A strictly POSIX-compliant shell script that runs under any Bourne-compatible shell (/bin/sh, bash, dash, zsh) across Unix environments and Windows Git Bash.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="StagingDir" type="string" value="./staging_data" />
        <variable name="CleanResult" type="string" value="" />
    </variables>

    <flow>
        <script id="CleanupOldStagingFiles" language="sh" output_var="CleanResult">
            <![CDATA[
            # POSIX-compliant file purging: removes .tmp files older than 7 days
            TARGET_DIR="{{StagingDir}}"

            if [ -d "$TARGET_DIR" ]; then
                DELETED_COUNT=$(find "$TARGET_DIR" -type f -name "*.tmp" -mtime +7 -exec rm -f {} + -print | wc -l)
                echo "Cleaned up $DELETED_COUNT stale staging files in $TARGET_DIR"
            else
                mkdir -p "$TARGET_DIR"
                echo "Created missing staging directory: $TARGET_DIR"
            fi
            ]]>
        </script>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 7: C# Scripting via .NET Script (language="csx")
docs.text:
Executes C# code using dotnet-script, utilizing LINQ and System.Text.Json to process a variable payload.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="RawScores" type="string" value="95,82,78,99,88,91,65,74" />
        <variable name="ScoreStats" type="string" value="" />
    </variables>

    <flow>
        <script id="ComputeScoreStats" language="csx" output_var="ScoreStats">
            <![CDATA[
            using System;
            using System.Linq;
            using System.Text.Json;

            string raw = "{{RawScores}}";
            var scores = raw.Split(',', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries)
                            .Select(s => int.Parse(s.Trim()))
                            .ToList();

            var stats = new
            {
                Count = scores.Count,
                Min = scores.Min(),
                Max = scores.Max(),
                Average = Math.Round(scores.Average(), 2),
                Median = scores.OrderBy(x => x).Skip(scores.Count / 2).First()
            };

            Console.Write(JsonSerializer.Serialize(stats));
            ]]>
        </script>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 8: Database Connection Health & Latency Probe (language="go" with "host/db")
docs.text:
Uses the built-in "host/db" integration package to inspect an active database connection pool, measure network round-trip ping latency in milliseconds, and record health status.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="production_db"
                  driver="postgres"
                  connection_string="host=db.example.internal port=5432 user=flow_user password=SecretPassword dbname=analytics sslmode=require" />
    </databases>

    <variables>
        <variable name="DbPingLatencyMs" type="int" value="0" />
        <variable name="DbStatus" type="string" value="UNKNOWN" />
    </variables>

    <flow>
        <script id="ProbeDatabaseHealth" language="go" timeout="10s">
            <![CDATA[
            package main

            import (
                "context"
                "fmt"
                "time"
                "host/db"
                "host/vars"
            )

            func main() {
                conn, err := db.Get("production_db")
                if err != nil {
                    vars.SetString("DbStatus", "CONNECTION_POOL_NOT_FOUND")
                    fmt.Printf("Database pool error: %v\n", err)
                    return
                }

                ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
                defer cancel()

                start := time.Now()
                err = conn.PingContext(ctx)
                durationMs := int(time.Since(start).Milliseconds())

                vars.Set("DbPingLatencyMs", durationMs)

                if err != nil {
                    vars.SetString("DbStatus", "PING_FAILED")
                    fmt.Printf("Database ping failed after %d ms: %v\n", durationMs, err)
                } else {
                    vars.SetString("DbStatus", "HEALTHY")
                    fmt.Printf("Database connection healthy (ping latency: %d ms)\n", durationMs)
                }
            }
            ]]>
        </script>

        <assert id="EnsureDatabaseHealthy"
                var="DbStatus"
                equals="HEALTHY"
                message="Production database connection failed latency health probe!"
                on_failure="halt" />
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Example 9: Dynamic Script Execution from a Variable (var="...")
docs.text:
Executes code stored inside a pipeline variable rather than an inline XML body. This pattern enables dynamic scripts generated by earlier pipeline steps or loaded from an external repository or encrypted payload.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <variables>
        <variable name="DynamicGoCode" type="string">
            <value>
                package main
                import (
                    "fmt"
                    "time"
                )
                func main() {
                    fmt.Printf("Dynamic execution at UTC: %s\n", time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339))
                }
            </value>
        </variable>
        <variable name="DynamicOutput" type="string" value="" />
    </variables>

    <flow>
        <!-- The var attribute directs Flow to execute the Go code stored in DynamicGoCode -->
        <script id="RunDynamicCode"
                language="go"
                var="DynamicGoCode"
