docs.title: Command-Line Arguments Reference: flow.exe, crypto_tool, and db_importer
docs.text:
This document provides a comprehensive command-line reference for all three executable utilities in the ETL Madness Flow ecosystem:

  1. flow.exe: The primary pipeline execution engine, preflight validator, XML/AST schema verifier, visual builder server, and database import/export manager.
  2. crypto_tool: Standalone utility for AES-256-GCM encryption/decryption, digital signature signing/verification (OpenSSL, OpenPGP, PKCS#7/CMS), and cryptographic keypair generation.
  3. db_importer: Dedicated CLI utility to import XML pipelines, options, and configs into SQL Server repositories (or export to file/stdout), featuring automatic UTF-8/UTF-16 encoding handling and at-rest encryption.

docs.title: Ecosystem Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph SecurityLayer["1. Cryptography & Packaging"]
        CT["crypto_tool"]
        CT -->|"Encrypt (AES-256-GCM)"| ENC["Encrypted XML<br>(FLOWENC:v1:...)"]
        CT -->|"Sign (OpenSSL / PGP / PKCS#7)"| SIG["Signed Package<br>(FLOWSIGNED:v1:... or .sig)"]
    end

    subgraph StorageLayer["2. Repository Storage"]
        DBI["db_importer"]
        DB["SQL Server / Database<br>(dbo.flow_*_content)"]
        ENC --> DBI
        SIG --> DBI
        DBI -->|"MERGE / Upsert"| DB
    end

    subgraph RuntimeLayer["3. Execution Engine"]
        FLOW["flow.exe"]
        DB -->|"sql:// or db:// URI"| FLOW
        ENC -->|"Local file / HTTP"| FLOW
        SIG -->|"Local file / HTTP"| FLOW
        FLOW -->|"Telemetry & Events"| SINK["Audit Tables / DB Sink"]
    end

docs.title: Shared Secret Resolution Precedence
docs.text:
When encryption or decryption operations are performed, all three utilities resolve passphrases and cryptographic keys using the identical precedence hierarchy:

flowchart TD
    P1["1. Key File (-key-file <path>)<br>Safest: reads key directly from protected file"] -->|"If not provided"| P2["2. Command-Line Flag (-secure-key or -key)<br>Emits warning: exposed in system process listings"]
    P2 -->|"If not provided"| P3["3. XML Options Profile (<secure-key>)<br>(flow.exe only via -options profile)"]
    P3 -->|"If not provided"| P4["4. FLOW_SECURE_KEY<br>Environment variable"]
    P4 -->|"If not provided"| P5["5. SECURE_KEY<br>Fallback generic environment variable"]

    classDef safe fill:#e6fffa,stroke:#047857,stroke-width:2px;
    classDef warn fill:#fffbeb,stroke:#b45309,stroke-width:2px;
    classDef env fill:#f0f9ff,stroke:#0284c7,stroke-width:2px;
    class P1 safe;
    class P2 warn;
    class P3,P4,P5 env;

[!WARNING] Process Listing Security Warning: Passing encryption keys or passphrases directly on the command line via -secure-key exposes secrets to other users and processes on the system (e.g., via ps aux, Get-Process, or Windows Task Manager). In production, automated schedulers, and CI/CD pipelines, always pass keys using -key-file or the FLOW_SECURE_KEY environment variable.

docs.title: Supported Resource URIs
docs.text:
Arguments in flow.exe that load resources (-file, -options, -config, -import-file) support uniform resource resolution:

Resource Type Format Example Local File Standard relative or absolute path -file ".\pipelines\finance.xml" HTTP / HTTPS http://... or https://... -file "https://internal.repo/pipelines/etl.xml" HTTP Basic Auth https://Basic%20<base64>@host/... -file "https://Basic%20dXNlcjpwYXNz@internal.repo/etl.xml" SQL Server Query sql://sqlserver@<dsn>#<SELECT_QUERY> -options "sql://sqlserver@localhost:1433?database=ETL#SELECT OptionsXML FROM dbo.flow_options_content WHERE Name='PROD'" Generic DB Alias db://<driver>@<dsn>#<SELECT_QUERY> -file "db://postgres@app_user:pass@db:5432/app#SELECT pipeline_xml FROM flow_pipelines WHERE name='BILLING'"

docs.title: Common Exit Codes
docs.text:
All three tools conform to standard operating system exit codes:

  • 0: Success (pipeline ran successfully, schema/AST valid, verification passed, or import/export completed).
  • 1: Failure (execution error, validation error, signature verification failed, decryption key missing/invalid, or database connection error).

docs.title: 1. flow.exe: Core Pipeline Engine & Builder Server
docs.text: flow.exe is the central executable. It executes ETL pipelines, runs preflight validations, starts an interactive HTMX web server for visual pipeline authoring, transforms pipeline definitions via XSLT into diagrams, and manages local or external repository persistence.

docs.title: Command Syntax
docs.text: .\flow.exe [options...]

docs.title: Full Flag Reference Table
docs.text: Flag Type Default Category Description -file string scripts.xml Execution Path or URI to XML file containing scripts, databases, and workflow nodes. Supports local files, HTTP/HTTPS URLs, and sql:// / db:// database queries. -options string "" Execution Path or URI to an XML options defaults file (<flow_cli_options><options>...). Values in this file set flag defaults without overriding flags explicitly passed on the CLI. -config string "" Execution Optional path or URI to a CONFIG.xml file containing variable and database connection overrides. Merged hierarchically with the base file. -format string csv Execution Output formatting applied to execution results. Supported: csv, text, json, jsonpretty (or prettyjson), markdown (or md, table), and stream. -vars string "" Execution Comma-separated key=value runtime variable overrides (e.g., -vars "TargetTable=tbl_prod,Threshold=500"). Recursively expands {{var}} placeholders up to 3 levels deep. -validate bool false Validation Validates XML schema (XSD if specified) and AST semantic structure without executing any pipeline nodes. Exits with code 0 on success. -preflight bool false Validation Executes preflight validation nodes only (<preflight> section), skipping the main pipeline <flow> nodes. -xsd string "" Validation Path to an XML Schema Definition (.xsd) file used to validate the pipeline XML via xmllint prior to parsing. -node-output bool false Diagnostic When logging to a database (log_db), persists each node's execution output (ResultsString with credential redaction) to the node_output column on node.finished rows in pipeline_events. Off by default. -debug bool false Diagnostic Enables verbose console logging, including connection string resolution, driver dialect detection, digital signature verification metadata, and sink telemetry. -gopath string $GOPATH Runtime GOPATH directory for dynamic package imports used by the embedded Yaegi Go interpreter engine. Defaults to the host GOPATH environment variable. -xslt string "" Visualization Path to custom XSLT stylesheet. Transforms pipeline XML while injecting an auto-generated Mermaid workflow diagram. Exits immediately after transformation. -out string "" Visualization Output file path for XSLT-transformed XML produced by -xslt. -encrypted bool false Security Indicates that input files/database resources are AES-256-GCM encrypted and must be decrypted prior to parsing, or instructs -export-file / -import-file to encrypt. -secure-key string "" Security Symmetric encryption or decryption key/passphrase. Emits a security warning to stderr; falls back to FLOW_SECURE_KEY or SECURE_KEY. -key-file string "" Security Path to file containing symmetric key/passphrase. Preferred over -secure-key to prevent exposing secrets in system process tables. -verify-signature bool false Security Enforces digital signature verification before decrypting or executing the pipeline. -public-key string "" Security Path to public key file (PEM format; RSA, ECDSA, Ed25519) for digital signature verification. -cert string "" Security Path to X.509 certificate file (PEM or DER format) for signature verification (PKCS#7/CMS or X.509 RSA/ECDSA). -ca-cert string "" Security Path to root CA certificate file for signature verification certificate chain validation. -keyring string "" Security Path to OpenPGP armored public keyring file for GPG signature verification. -signature string "" Security Path to detached digital signature file (.sig, .asc, .p7s). When omitted, companion files with matching basenames are automatically checked. -builder bool false Builder UI Starts the interactive local HTMX visual pipeline builder web server and opens the UI. -builder-port int 0 Builder UI Port for the visual builder web server. Default 0 chooses an ephemeral dynamic port. Can be set via FLOW_BUILDER_PORT or PORT environment variables. -builder-db string flow_builder.db Builder UI SQLite database file path used for visual builder local project storage. -purge-db bool false Builder UI Purges all pipeline data from the SQLite visual builder database, re-initializes defaults, and exits. -import-file string "" Repository Path to a pipeline, options, or config XML file to import into the SQLite builder database or an external database specified by -dsn. -import-name string "" Repository Custom record name for item imported with -import-file. Defaults to the source file basename without extension. -import-type string pipeline Repository Item type for -import-file: pipeline, options, or config. -export-file string "" Repository Destination file path to export a pipeline, options, or config file (or - for standard output stdout). -export-name string "" Repository Name of the pipeline, options, or config to export from the database (required when -export-file is specified). -export-type string pipeline Repository Item type for -export-file: pipeline, options, or config. -dsn string "" Repository External database DSN for direct database-to-database repository import and export (supports SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite).

docs.title: Output Formats (-format)
docs.text: Format Output Description csv (Default) Standard comma-separated table displaying ScriptID, ReturnCode, Duration, and ResultsString. text Human-readable plain text tabular format. json Compact JSON array containing all ScriptResult objects. jsonpretty / prettyjson Formatted multi-line JSON with 4-space indentation. markdown / md / table GitHub Flavored Markdown table. stream Real-time console event streaming mode (ExecuteRun engine) with live node transitions, parent/child execution relationships, and audit sink telemetry.

docs.title: Environment Variables Recognized by flow.exe
docs.text:
• FLOW_SECURE_KEY: Primary symmetric passphrase used to decrypt encrypted scripts, options, and configs.
  • SECURE_KEY: Secondary fallback passphrase if FLOW_SECURE_KEY is unset.
  • FLOW_BUILDER_PORT: Default port for the HTMX builder server when -builder-port is not explicitly passed.
  • PORT: Generic fallback port for web services (e.g., in cloud environments like Cloud Run or Heroku).
  • GOPATH: Go workspace directory used by Yaegi to import third-party packages in interpreted script blocks.
  • USER / USERNAME: Captured for execution audit logs in dbo.pipeline_runs.
  • HOSTNAME / COMPUTERNAME: Captured for execution audit logs in dbo.pipeline_runs.

docs.title: 2. crypto_tool: Cryptographic Utility
docs.text: crypto_tool is a self-contained, zero-dependency command-line utility for encryption, decryption, digital signing, signature verification, and keypair generation.

docs.title: Command Syntax
docs.text: crypto_tool [options...]

docs.title: Full Flag Reference Table
docs.text: Flag Alias Type Default Category Description -action — string encrypt Operation Cryptographic operation to perform: encrypt, decrypt, gen-key, sign, verify, or gen-keypair. -gen-key — bool false Operation Shortcut flag for -action gen-key. Generates a 256-bit cryptographically secure symmetric key. -in — string "" I/O Input file path (use "-" or leave empty for standard input stdin). -out — string "" I/O Output file path (use "-" or leave empty for standard output stdout). Output files containing secret keys are written with 0600 permissions. -secure-key -key string "" Symmetric Passphrase or raw key for AES-256-GCM encryption or decryption. Emits a security warning to stderr; falls back to FLOW_SECURE_KEY or SECURE_KEY. -key-file — string "" Symmetric Path to file containing encryption/decryption key/passphrase. Prevents exposing secrets in operating system process listings. -binary — bool false Symmetric / Sig Output raw binary ciphertext or ASN.1 signature bytes instead of the default text-safe armored envelope (FLOWENC:v1:... or FLOWSIG:v1:...). -sig-type — string openssl Signing Digital signature format for -action sign: openssl (RSA/ECDSA/Ed25519), pgp (OpenPGP), or pkcs7 (CMS / PKCS#7 / Windows Authenticode). -private-key -priv string "" Signing Private key file path (PEM or OpenPGP format) used to generate digital signatures. -passphrase — string "" Signing Passphrase for decrypting password-protected private keys (PKCS#1, PKCS#8, or OpenPGP). -cert — string "" Sign / Verify X.509 certificate file path (PEM or DER format). Required when creating PKCS#7 signatures (-sig-type pkcs7); used for cert-based verification. -wrap — bool false Signing Wraps both the digital signature and input content into a single unified FLOWSIGNED:v1:... envelope. Eliminates the need for detached .sig files. -signature -sig string "" Verification Detached signature file path for -action verify. If omitted, automatically checks for companion files <in>.sig, <in>.asc, or <in>.p7s. -public-key -pub string "" Verification Public key file path (PEM or OpenPGP format) for signature verification. -ca-cert — string "" Verification Root or intermediate CA certificate file path used to validate certificate chains during PKCS#7 or X.509 verification. -keyring — string "" Verification OpenPGP armored public keyring file path for OpenPGP/GPG signature verification. -keypair-type — string rsa Keygen Asymmetric keypair type for -action gen-keypair: rsa, ecdsa (P-256), ed25519, or pgp (aliases: gpg, openpgp). -bits — int 2048 Keygen Bit length for RSA keypair generation (e.g., 2048, 3072, 4096). -out-priv — string private_key.pem Keygen Output file path for generated private key. File permissions are automatically restricted to 0600 (owner read/write only). -out-pub — string public_key.pem Keygen Output file path for generated public key (written with 0644 permissions). -out-cert — string "" Keygen Optional output path to generate a self-signed X.509 certificate during keypair generation (valid for 365 days). -cn — string Flow Code Signer Keygen Common Name (CN) embedded in the generated X.509 certificate or OpenPGP user identity.

docs.title: 3. db_importer: MSSQL Database XML Importer & Exporter
docs.text: db_importer is a dedicated utility for migrating pipelines, options profiles, and variable configs into and out of relational database storage (SQL Server dbo.flow_*_content tables). It includes automatic UTF-8 and UTF-16 character encoding translation and supports transparent at-rest encryption.

docs.title: Command Syntax
docs.text: .\db_importer.exe [options...]

docs.title: Full Flag Reference Table
docs.text: Flag Type Default Category Description -action string import Operation Database operation to execute: import (upserts record into table) or export (extracts record from table). -export bool false Operation Shortcut boolean flag to perform an export operation (equivalent to -action export). -dsn string sqlserver://sa:Password123!@localhost:1433?database=master&trustServerCertificate=true Connection Connection string for SQL Server instance (URL format or ADO/ODBC connection string). -file string github_ai_credit_usage.xml I/O Path to input XML file to import, or destination path for exported XML. Use "-" or leave empty to read from stdin (import) or write to stdout (export). -name string github_ai_credit_usage Target Unique logical name key of the record in the database (Name column in target table). Used for upsert matching and queries. -table string pipeline Target Target table and column mapping: pipeline, options, or config. See Database Mapping below. -desc string Imported via Go importer Metadata Descriptive text stored in the Description column of the table (import only). -encrypted bool false Security When importing: encrypts content into an armored FLOWENC:v1:... envelope before inserting into the database.When exporting: decrypts encrypted database content before writing to file or stdout. -secure-key string "" Security Passphrase or key for AES-256-GCM encryption/decryption. Emits a security warning to stderr; falls back to FLOW_SECURE_KEY or SECURE_KEY. -key-file string "" Security Path to file containing the encryption key/passphrase. Preferred over -secure-key to avoid exposing secrets in process tables.

docs.title: Target Table Mappings
docs.text: -table Value Database Table Target XML Payload Column Record Identifier Column pipeline (Default) dbo.flow_pipeline_content PipelineXML (NVARCHAR(MAX)) Name (VARCHAR(120)) options dbo.flow_options_content OptionsXML (NVARCHAR(MAX)) Name (VARCHAR(120)) config dbo.flow_config_content ConfigXML (NVARCHAR(MAX)) Name (VARCHAR(120))

docs.title: Encoding & Security Features
docs.text:
• BOM & UTF-16 Auto-Detection: Automatically detects and decodes UTF-8 BOM (0xEF 0xBB 0xBF), UTF-16 Little Endian BOM (0xFF 0xFE), and UTF-16 Big Endian BOM (0xFE 0xFF). Files generated by PowerShell or Windows editors are cleanly ingested without manual conversion.
  • Idempotent Upsert (MERGE): Imports use an atomic MERGE INTO statement on SQL Server. If the record name already exists, its Description and XML payload are updated in place; otherwise, a new record is inserted.
  • Hardened File Permissions: Exported decrypted files written to disk are automatically locked down with 0600 permissions (owner read/write only).

docs.title: Basic Pipeline Execution with Markdown Output
docs.text: .\flow.exe -file ".\pipelines\nightly_billing.xml" -format markdown

docs.title: Passing Runtime Overrides (-vars and -config)
docs.text:
.\flow.exe `
  -file ".\pipelines\etl.xml" `
  -config ".\configs\production.xml" `
  -vars "BatchDate=2026-10-10,MaxRetries=5,TargetSchema=stage" `
  -debug

docs.title: Preflight Checks & Schema Validation Only
docs.text:
# Validate XSD schema and AST without executing
.\flow.exe -file ".\pipelines\etl.xml" -xsd ".\xsd\pipeline.xsd" -validate

# Execute only the preflight nodes (smoke tests, DB pings)
.\flow.exe -file ".\pipelines\etl.xml" -preflight

docs.title: Running Directly from a SQL Database Query
docs.text:
.\flow.exe `
  -file "sql://sqlserver@sqlserver://sa:Password123!@localhost:1433?database=ETL&trustServerCertificate=true#SELECT PipelineXML FROM dbo.flow_pipeline_content WHERE Name='BILLING_JOB'" `
  -options "sql://sqlserver@sqlserver://sa:Password123!@localhost:1433?database=ETL&trustServerCertificate=true#SELECT OptionsXML FROM dbo.flow_options_content WHERE Name='PROD_OPTIONS'" `
  -key-file "C:\secrets\flow_master.key"

docs.title: Starting the HTMX Visual Builder
docs.text:
# Launch visual builder on a specific port with custom SQLite storage
.\flow.exe -builder -builder-port 8080 -builder-db "C:\flow\builder_workspace.db"

# Reset / purge the builder SQLite database
.\flow.exe -purge-db -builder-db "C:\flow\builder_workspace.db"

docs.title: Generating a Mermaid Diagram via XSLT
docs.text: .\flow.exe -file ".\pipelines\order_processing.xml" -xslt ".\transforms\mermaid.xslt" -out ".\docs\diagram.xml"

docs.title: Symmetric Encryption & Key Generation
docs.text:
# 1. Generate a cryptographically secure 256-bit AES key
crypto_tool -gen-key -out master.key

# 2. Encrypt an XML pipeline (outputs text-armored FLOWENC:v1:... file)
crypto_tool -action encrypt -in pipeline.xml -out pipeline.xml.enc -key-file master.key

# 3. Decrypt the file
crypto_tool -action decrypt -in pipeline.xml.enc -out pipeline.xml -key-file master.key

docs.title: Generating Asymmetric Keypairs & Certificates
docs.text:
# RSA Keypair + Self-Signed X.509 Certificate
crypto_tool -action gen-keypair -keypair-type rsa -bits 2048 \
  -out-priv release_priv.pem -out-pub release_pub.pem -out-cert release_cert.pem \
  -cn "Production Code Signer"

# ECDSA (P-256) Keypair
crypto_tool -action gen-keypair -keypair-type ecdsa -out-priv ec_priv.pem -out-pub ec_pub.pem

# OpenPGP / GPG Armored Keypair
crypto_tool -action gen-keypair -keypair-type pgp -out-priv gpg_priv.asc -out-pub gpg_pub.asc -cn "ETL Admin"

docs.title: Signing Files
docs.text:
# OpenSSL Detached Signature (.sig)
crypto_tool -action sign -in pipeline.xml -out pipeline.xml.sig -private-key release_priv.pem -sig-type openssl

# PKCS#7 / CMS Detached Signature (.p7s)
crypto_tool -action sign -in pipeline.xml -out pipeline.xml.p7s -private-key release_priv.pem -cert release_cert.pem -sig-type pkcs7

# Self-Contained Signed Package (FLOWSIGNED:v1:... envelope)
crypto_tool -action sign -in pipeline.xml -out pipeline.xml.signed -private-key release_priv.pem -wrap

docs.title: Verifying Signatures
docs.text:
# Verify detached signature
crypto_tool -action verify -in pipeline.xml -signature pipeline.xml.sig -public-key release_pub.pem

# Verify self-contained unified envelope and extract payload
crypto_tool -action verify -in pipeline.xml.signed -public-key release_pub.pem -out verified_pipeline.xml

docs.title: Importing XML Pipelines into SQL Server
docs.text:
# Plain XML import
.\db_importer.exe `
  -dsn "sqlserver://sa:Password123!@localhost:1433?database=ETL&trustServerCertificate=true" `
  -table pipeline `
  -name "github_billing" `
  -file ".\pipelines\github_billing.xml" `
  -desc "Production GitHub Billing Workflow"

# Encrypted import (stored encrypted at rest in SQL Server)
.\db_importer.exe `
  -dsn "sqlserver://sa:Password123!@localhost:1433?database=ETL&trustServerCertificate=true" `
  -table options `
  -name "OPTIONS_FINANCE" `
  -file ".\options\finance_options.xml" `
  -encrypted `
  -key-file "C:\secrets\flow_master.key"

docs.title: Exporting from SQL Server to File or Stdout
docs.text:
# Export and automatically decrypt to local file with 0600 permissions
.\db_importer.exe `
  -action export `
  -dsn "sqlserver://sa:Password123!@localhost:1433?database=ETL&trustServerCertificate=true" `
  -table pipeline `
  -name "github_billing" `
  -file ".\exported_pipeline.xml" `
  -encrypted `
  -key-file "C:\secrets\flow_master.key"

# Pipe exported XML directly to stdout
.\db_importer.exe -export -table pipeline -name "github_billing" -file - | xmllint --format -

docs.title: Recipe 1: Production CI/CD Release (Encrypt-then-Sign)
docs.text:
Secure pipeline distribution workflow where untrusted files are cryptographically verified before decryption keys are ever accessed:

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Developer as Build / CI Pipeline
    participant Crypto as crypto_tool
    participant Importer as db_importer
    participant SQL as SQL Server Repo
    participant Engine as flow.exe (Prod Host)

    Developer->>Crypto: crypto_tool -action encrypt -in pipeline.xml -out pipeline.xml.enc -key-file secret.key
    Developer->>Crypto: crypto_tool -action sign -in pipeline.xml.enc -out pipeline.xml.signed -private-key priv.pem -wrap
    Developer->>Importer: db_importer -table pipeline -name "DAILY_JOB" -file pipeline.xml.signed
    Importer->>SQL: MERGE INTO dbo.flow_pipeline_content
    Engine->>SQL: Query via sql:// URI
    Engine->>Engine: 1. Verify Digital Signature (release_pub.pem)
    Engine->>Engine: 2. Decrypt AES-256-GCM (FLOW_SECURE_KEY)
    Engine->>Engine: 3. Parse AST & Execute Workflow

Step-by-step commands:

# 1. Encrypt the pipeline definition
crypto_tool -action encrypt -in pipeline.xml -out pipeline.xml.enc -key-file prod.key

# 2. Sign the encrypted package into a unified FLOWSIGNED envelope
crypto_tool -action sign -in pipeline.xml.enc -out pipeline.xml.signed -private-key release_priv.pem -wrap

# 3. Import the signed package into SQL Server repository
db_importer -dsn "sqlserver://sa:Password@db:1433?database=ETL" -table pipeline -name "NIGHTLY_SYNC" -file pipeline.xml.signed

# 4. Execute on production server (verifies signature first, then decrypts)
export FLOW_SECURE_KEY="YourSecurePassphrase"
flow.exe \
  -file "sql://sqlserver@db:1433?database=ETL#SELECT PipelineXML FROM dbo.flow_pipeline_content WHERE Name='NIGHTLY_SYNC'" \
  -public-key "/etc/flow/release_pub.pem"

docs.title: Recipe 2: Options Profile Overrides (-options)
docs.text:
You can create an XML options file conforming to xsd/options.xsd to pre-configure defaults for production hosts:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<flow_cli_options>
    <options>
        <format>markdown</format>
        <debug>true</debug>
        <verify-signature>true</verify-signature>
        <public-key>C:\flow\keys\release_pub.pem</public-key>
        <encrypted>true</encrypted>
    </options>
</flow_cli_options>

Execute flow.exe referencing the options file:

.\flow.exe -options "C:\flow\prod_options.xml" -file "C:\flow\pipelines\job.xml" -key-file "C:\secrets\key.txt"

[!NOTE] Any flag provided explicitly on the command line (e.g., -format json) will override the value defined inside -options.

docs.title: Configuration & Execution Hierarchy
docs.text: go-flow uses a hierarchical configuration model to separate pipeline logic from environment-specific settings. This allows you to maintain a single pipeline definition while deploying it across different environments (Dev, Staging, Prod) simply by swapping configuration files or CLI arguments.

docs.title: Configuration Hierarchy
docs.text:
The engine merges settings in a specific order of precedence. Later stages override earlier ones:

Base XML (--file) $\rightarrow$ Options XML (--options) $\rightarrow$ Config XML (--config) $\rightarrow$ CLI Variables (--vars)

docs.title: Precedence Table
docs.text: Level Source Purpose Precedence Example 1. Pipeline --file Core logic, node definitions, default variables. Lowest scripts.xml 2. Options --options Default CLI flag behavior (ports, formats). Low defaults.xml 3. Config --config Env-specific overrides (DB strings, API keys). High prod_env.xml 4. Runtime --vars Immediate, one-off overrides for a specific run. Highest --vars "Limit=10"

docs.title: Execution Flow Diagram
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[Start Execution] --> B{Load pipeline.xml}
    B --> C{Merge options.xml}
    C --> D{Merge config.xml}
    D --> E{Apply --vars CLI flags}
    E --> F[Final Resolved Context]
    F --> G[AST Validation]
    G --> H[Pipeline Execution]

    style A fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style F fill:#bbf,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style H fill:#bfb,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px

docs.title: Practical Examples
docs.text: Assume we have a core pipeline file main.xml that defines a variable BatchSize and a database connection PrimaryDB.

docs.title: 1. Default Execution (Developer Mode)
docs.text:
Runs using only the defaults defined in the script file. 

./flow.exe --file main.xml
* BatchSize: 500 (from main.xml) * DB: localhost (from main.xml)

docs.title: 2. Environment-Based Execution (Production)
docs.text:
Overrides the base settings with a production configuration file. 

./flow.exe --file main.xml --config prod_config.xml
* BatchSize: 5000 (overridden by prod_config.xml) * DB: prod-sql-server.internal (overridden by prod_config.xml)

docs.title: 3. Ad-hoc Debugging Execution
docs.text:
Uses the production config but overrides a specific variable via CLI for a quick test. 

./flow.exe --file main.xml --config prod_config.xml --vars "BatchSize=10,DebugMode=true"
* BatchSize: 10 (overridden by --vars) * DB: prod-sql-server.internal (from prod_config.xml) * DebugMode: true (added via --vars)

docs.title: 4. Standardized Runner (Using Options File)
docs.text:
Uses an options file to standardize the output format, port, and even the default config file used across all team members.

Example corporate_defaults.xml: 

<flow_cli_options>
    <option name="format" value="jsonpretty" />
    <option name="builder-port" value="9000" />
    <option name="config" value="dev_config.xml" />
</flow_cli_options>

Execution: 

./flow.exe --file main.xml --options corporate_defaults.xml
* Format: jsonpretty (from corporate_defaults.xml) * Port: 9000 (from corporate_defaults.xml) * Config: dev_config.xml (automatically loaded because it's specified in the options file) * DB: dev-db.local (loaded via the config file specified in the options)

Override Example: If you want to use the corporate defaults but target Production instead: 

./flow.exe --file main.xml --options corporate_defaults.xml --config prod_config.xml
* Config: prod_config.xml (CLI flag --config overrides the value inside corporate_defaults.xml)

docs.title: Summary of File Roles
docs.text:
• scripts.xml: The "Source Code". Defines what happens.
  • options.xml: The "Tool Settings". Defines how the CLI behaves.
  • config.xml: The "Environment". Defines where the data is.
  • --vars: The "Tweak". Defines specifics for this exact run.

docs.title: Database Logging Setup for Pipeline Runs and Events

docs.title: Node Output Logging (node_output)
docs.text:
By default, go-flow does not persist node execution output to the pipeline_events table (-node-output is false).

When enabled via the -node-output command-line flag, <node-output>true</node-output> in an options XML file, or the Log Node Output to DB (-node-output) checkbox in the Visual Builder Runner tab: - If log_db is configured and the pipeline_events table contains a node_output column, go-flow records each node's execution output (ScriptResult.ResultsString) into pipeline_events.node_output on 'node.finished' event rows. - Sensitive key-value patterns (password, pwd, token, secret, authorization) are automatically redacted ([REDACTED]) before writing to the database. - Oversized node outputs are UTF-8 safely truncated at 64 KB (65536 bytes, or the detected database column length if narrower) with a \n...[TRUNCATED] suffix so database UPDATE statements and UI payloads never fail due to size. - Other lifecycle events (run.started, node.started, run.finished) leave node_output as NULL.

docs.title: Session Identity and Auditing Columns
docs.text:
When logging pipeline events or runs to a database, the telemetry subsystem records session-level audit columns:

Column Description Dialect Resolution os_user_name / user_name OS user executing the process (go-flow) user.Current() / Windows environment db_user_name Database user identity authenticated to the database. In pipeline_runs, captures the logging database connection user. In pipeline_events, captures the individual step's database connection user (or source_user->target_user for cross-database <sql_bulk> transfers). MSSQL: SYSTEM_USERPostgreSQL: CURRENT_USERMySQL: CURRENT_USER()Oracle: SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV', 'SESSION_USER')SQLite: os.Getpid() / "sqlite" spid / sspid Server Process ID (SPID) or database session ID. In pipeline_runs, captures the logging database session SPID. In pipeline_events, captures the individual step's database session SPID (or source_spid->target_spid for cross-database <sql_bulk> transfers). MSSQL: @@SPIDPostgreSQL: pg_backend_pid()MySQL: CONNECTION_ID()Oracle: SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV', 'SID')SQLite: os.Getpid() application_name / app_name Application name executing the pipeline or connected to the database session. In pipeline_runs, captures the logging database session application name. In pipeline_events, captures the individual step's database session application name (or source_app->target_app for cross-database <sql_bulk> transfers). MSSQL: ISNULL(APP_NAME(), '')PostgreSQL: COALESCE(current_setting('application_name', true), '')MySQL: COALESCE(@@session.program_name, '')Oracle: COALESCE(SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV', 'MODULE'), SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV', 'CLIENT_PROGRAM_NAME'), '')Fallback/SQLite: Binary executable name (flow) node_output Execution output (ResultsString) of a completed node, populated on 'node.finished' events only when -node-output is enabled. Populated when -node-output is set and node_output column exists on pipeline_events

Backward Compatibility: If an existing database table was created with earlier schemas that lack os_user_name, db_user_name, spid, sspid, application_name, or node_output, go-flow automatically detects available columns and performs inserts without error. If pipeline_events.spid retains a legacy numeric type (BIGINT), cross-database bulk transfers automatically fall back to the numeric source_spid so database inserts never fail. When the columns exist, they are automatically populated.

docs.title: Database Transactions in Flow Pipelines
docs.text: Flow supports wrapping sequential SQL script execution inside an atomic database transaction. This ensures that a group of SQL scripts either succeeds together or rolls back completely if an error occurs.

docs.title: 1. Configuration Syntax
docs.text: Transactions are declared at the <group> node level using two attributes: * transaction="true": Enables transaction wrapping for all SQL script nodes inside the group. * db="..." (or database="..."): Specifies the target database handle to run the transaction on.

docs.title: Basic Example
docs.text:
<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="sales_db" driver="postgres" connection_string="postgresql://..." />
    </databases>
    <flow>
        <group id="update_sales_txn" transaction="true" db="sales_db">
            <sql id="deduct_inventory" db="sales_db">
                UPDATE inventory SET stock = stock - 1 WHERE item_id = 42;
            </sql>
            <sql id="record_sale" db="sales_db">
                INSERT INTO sales (item_id, qty) VALUES (42, 1);
            </sql>
        </group>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: 2. Dynamic Loops & Nested Transactions (<foreach>)
docs.text:
If a group with transaction="true" is placed inside a <foreach> loop, Flow begins, executes, and commits/rolls back a new transaction per loop iteration. 

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <flow>
        <!-- Loop driver gets item IDs -->
        <foreach id="process_items" db="sales_db">
            SELECT item_id, price FROM active_promotions;

            <!-- A transaction is started and finished for each promotion processed -->
            <group id="apply_promo_txn" transaction="true" db="sales_db">
                <sql id="update_price" db="sales_db">
                    UPDATE products SET price = {{price}} WHERE id = {{item_id}};
                </sql>
                <sql id="log_history" db="sales_db">
                    INSERT INTO pricing_log (product_id, new_price) VALUES ({{item_id}}, {{price}});
                </sql>
            </group>
        </foreach>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: 3. Parallel Execution & Isolation (<parallel>)
docs.text:
When running concurrent tasks in a <parallel> block: * Flow isolates each parallel branch inside its own execution context with a unique cloned executor. * If a <group transaction="true"> is placed inside a parallel branch, its active transaction is completely isolated to that branch's worker connection. * This prevents race conditions or shared transaction states across parallel threads.

<pipeline xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <flow>
        <parallel max_threads="2">
            <!-- Branch 1: isolated txn on sales_db -->
            <group transaction="true" db="sales_db">
                <sql db="sales_db">INSERT INTO logs VALUES ('Thread A started');</sql>
                <sql db="sales_db">UPDATE stats SET count = count + 1;</sql>
            </group>

            <!-- Branch 2: isolated txn on sales_db -->
            <group transaction="true" db="sales_db">
                <sql db="sales_db">INSERT INTO logs VALUES ('Thread B started');</sql>
                <sql db="sales_db">UPDATE stats SET count = count + 1;</sql>
            </group>
        </parallel>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: 3.5 Context Propagation & Automatic Rollback
docs.text: All transactions in Flow are fully contextualized using Go's context.Context API: * Transactions are initiated with BeginTx(ctx, nil). * If the pipeline's active context is cancelled or times out, the active transactions are automatically aborted and safely rolled back. * This prevents database locks, stale transactions, and uncommitted orphaned states across timeouts and unexpected cancellations.

docs.title: 4. Interaction with SQL Server Bulk Copy (StreamETL)
docs.text: Flow has high-performance support for Microsoft SQL Server native TDS bulk streaming copy via the StreamETL function (<sql_bulk target_table="..."> tag).

docs.title: How Bulk Copy Works
docs.text: The MS SQL Server bulk copy utility loads data efficiently by writing data pages directly to the database without the overhead of standard row-by-row transaction logs. It utilizes the mssql.CopyIn interface.

docs.title: Bulk Copy Batch-Level Transactions
docs.text: Unlike standard sequential SQL scripts, SQL Server bulk copy manages its own internal transactions to flush rows in high-speed chunks (defined by batch_size, which defaults to 10000 rows). Each batch flush: 1. Opens a separate, native bulk transaction. 2. Writes the chunk of rows. 3. Commits that batch chunk immediately to disk.

docs.title: Impact of Mixing Group Transactions and Bulk Copy
docs.text:
[!WARNING] While a standard <group transaction="true"> is excellent for atomic transactional integrity on conventional queries, you should avoid placing high-throughput bulk copy stream scripts (<sql_bulk target_table="...">) inside a transaction-enabled group.

Here is how configuration options impact bulk copy:

  1. Atomicity vs. Recovery: If a bulk copy script is wrapped inside an outer group transaction, standard driver behaviors might force all streamed batches to use the same underlying physical connection. However, because bulk copying relies on native SQL Server TDS fast-load streams, mixing outer group transactions with internal batch commits can cause locking, socket blocks, or driver-level command overlap errors.
  2. TABLOCK (Minimal Logging): By default, bulk insert operations use the tablock option to lock the target table during inserts. This minimizes transactional logging and maximizes throughput. However, if a table lock is acquired within a long-running standard transaction, concurrent queries targeting that table are fully blocked until the entire transaction group is either committed or rolled back.
  3. Check Constraints & Triggers: By default, constraints checking (check_constraints) and triggers (fire_triggers) are turned off to speed up ingestion. Enabling them forces SQL Server to run validations, which increases logging overhead and log-write lock contention. Under an outer group transaction, this logging overhead can lead to rapid database transaction log depletion.

docs.title: Summary Best Practice
docs.text:
• Use <group transaction="true"> for transactional business logic, updates, inserts, and system state steps.
  • Do NOT use outer group transactions for high-volume data streams (StreamETL). Instead, let the streaming engine handle batch-level transaction commits naturally.

docs.title: Comprehensive Pipeline Debugging Guide: Assert, Go & CSX Script Patterns
docs.text: This guide provides an end-to-end reference for inspecting, debugging, pausing, and validating dynamic ETL workflows in Flow. It details the two primary scripting engines—Embedded Go (language="go") and C# .NET Script (language="csx")—demonstrating how to observe pipeline state, trace loop mutations, prompt operators interactively, and diagnose execution issues across platforms.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
1. Architectural Overview & Scripting Engines
  2. Variable Discovery & State Observation
  3. Pattern 1: Inspect Specific Variables & Early Exit
  4. Pattern 2: Interactive Breakpoints & Operator Prompts
  5. Pattern 3: Per-Iteration Loop Inspection (<foreach>)
  6. Pattern 4: State Mutation & Polling Verification (<while>)
  7. Pattern 5: Declarative Assertions & Diagnostic Dumps (<assert>)
  8. Engine Comparison: Go (host/vars) vs. CSX (Environment)
  9. CLI Diagnostic Flags & Best Practices
  10. Debugging Quick Reference Table

docs.title: 1. Architectural Overview & Scripting Engines
docs.text:
Flow provides two distinct script execution models for pipeline logic, debugging, and data transformation:

flowchart TD
    Registry[("Pipeline Variable Registry<br/>(Thread-Safe Key/Value Store)")]

    subgraph GoEngine ["1. Yaegi Go Interpreter (In-Process)"]
        GoInterp["Yaegi Interpreter Context"]

    end

    subgraph CsxEngine ["2. .NET Script CSX (Subprocess)"]

    end

    Registry <-->|Direct In-Memory Access| HostVars
    HostVars <--> GoInterp
    GoInterp --> GoStdout

    Registry -->|Snapshot on Step Start| EnvInjection

    DotnetScript --> CsxStdout

    GoStdout -->|Captured by output_var| Registry
    CsxStdout -->|Captured by output_var| Registry

docs.title: The Two Execution Environments
docs.text:
1. Embedded Go (language="go"):
  2. Engine: Traefik Yaegi Go interpreter running in-process.
  3. Performance: Near-instantaneous ($O(\mu\text{s})$ initialization) with zero process fork overhead.
  4. Variable Interface: Direct memory binding via the synthetic "host/vars" package.

  5. Portability: Completely self-contained within flow.exe; requires no external Go compiler or runtime.

  6. C# .NET Script (language="csx"):

  7. Engine: Cross-platform dotnet-script CLI executed via external process invocation.
  8. Performance: High-power runtime with access to full .NET Base Class Libraries (BCL), LINQ, System.Text.Json, and NuGet packaging.
  9. Variable Interface: Flow snapshots all registry variables and injects them as OS environment variables into the child process environment.
  10. Portability: Runs on any system where the .NET SDK / dotnet-script tool is installed.

docs.title: 2. Variable Discovery & State Observation
docs.text: When debugging complex pipelines, inspecting the live state of all pipeline variables is essential.

docs.title: Go: vars.GetAll()
docs.text:
In embedded Go scripts, the synthetic "host/vars" package provides vars.GetAll(), returning a copy of the current variable map:

import (
    "fmt"
    "os"
    "sort"
    "host/vars"
)

allVars := vars.GetAll()
keys := make([]string, 0, len(allVars))
for k := range allVars {
    keys = append(keys, k)
}
sort.Strings(keys)

for _, name := range keys {
    fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "  %-20s = %v\n", name, allVars[name])
}

docs.title: CSX: Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable
docs.text:
In C# scripts, all pipeline variables are injected into the child process environment. You can query specific variables by name or enumerate known pipeline variables in sorted order:

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;

var pipelineVarNames = new[] {
    "DBPath", "DEPARTMENT", "FormattedRow", "ID", "LAST_OUTPUT", "LOOP_INDEX",
    "MinSalary", "NAME", "SALARY", "department", "id", "log_db_cs", "name", "salary"
};

var keys = new List<string>();
foreach (var name in pipelineVarNames)
{
    if (Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(name) != null)
    {
        keys.Add(name);
    }
}
keys.Sort(StringComparer.Ordinal);

foreach (var name in keys)
{
    var val = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(name);
    Console.WriteLine($"  {name,-20} = {val}");
}

docs.title: 3. Pattern 1: Inspect Specific Variables & Early Exit
Purpose
docs.text: When developing or troubleshooting a pipeline, you often need to verify that specific configuration variables (such as connection strings, file paths, or template outputs) were parsed correctly, and optionally halt before downstream destructive actions occur.

docs.title: Baseline Implementations
docs.text:
• Go Reference: ../examples/debug_specific_vars_and_exit_pipeline.xml
  • CSX Reference: ../examples/debug_specific_vars_and_exit_csx_pipeline.xml

<script id="DumpVarsAndExit" language="go">

        package main

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: In production troubleshooting or staging verifications, you may wish to inspect all live variables and prompt an operator whether to continue or abort. If aborted, the script halts execution and emits a structured JSON diagnostic payload.

docs.title: Baseline Implementations
docs.text:
• Go Reference: ../examples/debug_and_ask_continue_pipeline.xml
  • CSX Reference: ../examples/debug_and_ask_continue_csx_pipeline.xml

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Flow as Flow Engine
    participant Script as Script (Go or CSX)
    participant Console as Terminal / Operator

    Flow->>Script: Execute DumpVarsAndPause
    Script->>Console: Print Table of All Variables
    Script->>Console: "Enter Y to cancel or N to continue [default: N]: "
    Console-->>Script: User Input (e.g., 'Y' or 'N' / Enter)
    alt User Enters 'Y' (Cancel)
        Script->>Console: "Cancellation requested. Halting pipeline..."
        Script-->>Flow: Abort via panic() or throw Exception(jsonPayload)
        Flow-->>Console: Pipeline Halts with Error / Diagnostic Dump
    else User Enters 'N' or Enter (Continue)
        Script->>Console: "Continuing pipeline..."
        Script-->>Flow: Return code 0 (Success)
        Flow->>Flow: Proceed to Next Pipeline Step
    end

docs.title: Embedded Go (language="go")
docs.text:
<script id="DumpVarsAndPause" language="go">
    <![CDATA[
        package main

        import (
            "bufio"
            "encoding/json"
            "fmt"
            "os"
            "sort"
            "strings"
            "host/vars"
        )

        func main() {
            fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, "\n========== Pipeline Variables ==========")
            allVars := vars.GetAll()
            keys := make([]string, 0, len(allVars))
            for k := range allVars {
                keys = append(keys, k)
            }
            sort.Strings(keys)
            for _, name := range keys {
                fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "  %-20s = %v\n", name, allVars[name])
            }
            fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, "========================================")

            fmt.Fprint(os.Stdout, "\nEnter Y to cancel or N to continue [default: N]: ")
            os.Stdout.Sync()

            reader := bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin)
            rawInput, _ := reader.ReadString('\n')
            choice := strings.TrimSpace(strings.ToUpper(rawInput))

            if choice == "Y" {
                fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, "Cancellation requested. Halting pipeline...")
                jsonBytes, _ := json.Marshal(allVars)
                panic(string(jsonBytes))
            }

            fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, "Continuing pipeline...")
        }
    ]]>
</script>

docs.title: C# Script (language="csx")
docs.text:
<script id="DumpVarsAndPause" language="csx">
    <![CDATA[
        using System;
        using System.Collections.Generic;
        using System.Text.Json;

        Console.WriteLine("\n========== Pipeline Variables ==========");

        var pipelineVarNames = new[] {
            "DBPath", "DEPARTMENT", "FormattedRow", "ID", "LAST_OUTPUT", "LOOP_INDEX",
            "MinSalary", "NAME", "SALARY", "department", "id", "log_db_cs", "name", "salary"
        };

        var keys = new List<string>();
        foreach (var name in pipelineVarNames)
        {
            if (Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(name) != null)
            {
                keys.Add(name);
            }
        }
        keys.Sort(StringComparer.Ordinal);

        var allVars = new Dictionary<string, string>();
        foreach (var name in keys)
        {
            string val = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(name) ?? "";
            allVars[name] = val;
            Console.WriteLine($"  {name,-20} = {val}");
        }
        Console.WriteLine("========================================");

        Console.Write("\nEnter Y to cancel or N to continue [default: N]: ");
        string rawInput = Console.ReadLine() ?? "";
        string choice = rawInput.Trim().ToUpper();

        if (choice == "Y")
        {
            Console.WriteLine("Cancellation requested. Halting pipeline...");
            string jsonString = JsonSerializer.Serialize(allVars);
            throw new Exception(jsonString);
        }

        Console.WriteLine("Continuing pipeline...");
    ]]>
</script>

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: In cursor-driven database loops (<foreach>), data bugs often occur on specific rows (e.g., unexpected nulls, boundary values, or character encoding mismatches). Placing an inspection script inside the loop captures variable state on every single pass.

docs.title: Baseline Implementations

• Go Reference: ../examples/debug_and_exit_pipeline.xml
  • CSX Reference: ../examples/debug_and_exit_csx_pipeline.xml

docs.title: Embedded Go (language="go")
docs.text:
<foreach id="SelectEmployees" db="sample_db">
    <![CDATA[
        SELECT id, name, department, salary
        FROM employees
        WHERE salary >= {{MinSalary}}
        ORDER BY id;
    ]]>
    <template id="FormatEmployeeRow" output_var="FormattedRow">

    <!-- In-loop debugging script -->
    <script id="DumpVarsPerLoop" language="go">
        <![CDATA[
            package main

                "fmt"

                "sort"
                "host/vars"
            )

            func main() {
                loopIdx := vars.GetInt("LOOP_INDEX")

                fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, header)

                    keys = append(keys, k)
                }
                sort.Strings(keys)
                for _, name := range keys {
                    fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "  %-20s = %v\n", name, allVars[name])
                }

            }

    </script>

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: <while> loops are commonly used for polling asynchronous jobs or processing paginated batches. Debugging while loops requires: 1. Observing variables at each WHILE_INDEX iteration pass. 2. Verifying accumulator logic (e.g. ProcessedCount = ProcessedCount + 25). 3. Ensuring termination conditions correctly evaluate and break the loop.

docs.title: Baseline Implementations
docs.text:
• Go Reference: ../examples/debug_while_loop_pipeline.xml
  • CSX Reference: ../examples/debug_while_loop_csx_pipeline.xml

docs.title: While Loop Workflow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Start([Enter while: JobStatus == 'RUNNING']) --> Step1["Step 1: DumpVarsInWhile<br/>Inspect state at WHILE_INDEX"]
    Step1 --> Step2["Step 2: IncrementProcessedCount<br/>output_var='ProcessedCount' (+25)"]
    Step2 --> Step3{"Step 3: UpdateLoopStatus<br/>Is WHILE_INDEX >= 2?"}
    Step3 -- "No (Index 0, 1)" --> KeepRunning["Output 'RUNNING' to JobStatus"]
    Step3 -- "Yes (Index 2)" --> MarkCompleted["Output 'COMPLETED' to JobStatus"]
    KeepRunning --> LoopCheck{"Condition Check:<br/>JobStatus == 'RUNNING'?"}
    MarkCompleted --> LoopCheck
    LoopCheck -- "True" --> Step1
    LoopCheck -- "False" --> ExitLoop["Exit While Loop"]
    ExitLoop --> FinalDump["Step 4: DumpFinalVarsAfterWhile<br/>Audit final mutated state"]

docs.title: Step 1: Dump Variables at Current WHILE_INDEX
docs.text:
<!-- Go Version -->
<script id="DumpVarsInWhile" language="go">
    <![CDATA[
        package main
        import ("fmt"; "os"; "sort"; "host/vars")

        func main() {
            idx := vars.GetInt("WHILE_INDEX")
            fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "\n========== Variables at WHILE_INDEX %d ==========\n", idx)
            allVars := vars.GetAll()
            // ... Sort & Print Keys ...
        }
    ]]>
</script>

<!-- CSX Version -->
<script id="DumpVarsInWhile" language="csx">
    <![CDATA[
        using System;
        using System.Collections.Generic;

        int idx = int.TryParse(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("WHILE_INDEX"), out var i) ? i : 0;
        Console.WriteLine($"\n========== Variables at WHILE_INDEX {idx} ==========");
        // ... Sort & Print Keys ...
    ]]>
</script>

docs.title: Step 2: Simulate Processing & Mutate Accumulator via output_var
docs.text:
Flow captures anything written to standard output (stdout) and updates the variable specified by output_var:

<!-- Go Version -->
<script id="IncrementProcessedCount" language="go" output_var="ProcessedCount">
    <![CDATA[
        package main
        import ("fmt"; "host/vars")

        func main() {
            count := vars.GetInt("ProcessedCount") + 25
            fmt.Print(count) // Captured directly by ProcessedCount
        }
    ]]>
</script>

<!-- CSX Version -->
<script id="IncrementProcessedCount" language="csx" output_var="ProcessedCount">
    <![CDATA[
        using System;

        int count = int.TryParse(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("ProcessedCount"), out var c) ? c : 0;
        count += 25;
        Console.Write(count); // Captured directly by ProcessedCount
    ]]>
</script>

docs.title: Step 3: Update Loop Termination Condition via output_var
docs.text:
<!-- Go Version -->
<script id="UpdateLoopStatus" language="go" output_var="JobStatus">
    <![CDATA[
        package main
        import ("fmt"; "host/vars")

        func main() {
            idx := vars.GetInt("WHILE_INDEX")
            if idx >= 2 {
                fmt.Print("COMPLETED")
            } else {
                fmt.Print("RUNNING")
            }
        }
    ]]>
</script>

<!-- CSX Version -->
<script id="UpdateLoopStatus" language="csx" output_var="JobStatus">
    <![CDATA[
        using System;

        int idx = int.TryParse(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("WHILE_INDEX"), out var i) ? i : 0;
        if (idx >= 2) {
            Console.Write("COMPLETED");
        } else {
            Console.Write("RUNNING");
        }
    ]]>
</script>

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: While embedded scripts offer maximum flexibility, Flow's native <assert> tag provides a zero-code declarative mechanism for fail-fast debugging. By asserting expected state invariants between steps, you prevent silent data corruption, catch logic regressions immediately, and trigger automated diagnostic dumps when unexpected values arise.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    ExecStep["Execute Pipeline Step<br/>(e.g. While Loop or SQL)"] --> CheckAssert{"<assert> Evaluation<br/>Does 'var' match 'equals'?"}

    CheckAssert -- "Match (Passed)" --> Proceed["Continue Normal Pipeline Execution"]
    CheckAssert -- "Mismatch (Failed)" --> Policy{"on_failure Policy"}

    Policy -- "warn" --> LogWarn["Log Warning Message"]
    LogWarn --> SetDirty["Set fail_var = fail_val<br/>(e.g. DEBUG_DIRTY = true)"]
    SetDirty --> Proceed

    Policy -- "halt (default)" --> HasOnFailure{"Nested <on_failure> Defined?"}
    HasOnFailure -- "Yes" --> RunDiag["Execute Diagnostic Scripts<br/>(Go or CSX state dump)"]
    RunDiag --> HaltPipeline[/"Halt Execution (Exit Code != 0)"/]
    HasOnFailure -- "No" --> HaltPipeline

docs.title: Key <assert> Attributes for Debugging
docs.text: Attribute Options / Default Description var (required) Name of the pipeline registry variable to evaluate. equals / value (required) Expected value (case-insensitive string comparison). message "" Informative error or diagnostic message logged upon failure. on_failure halt (default) | warn halt stops the pipeline immediately; warn logs the failure and continues. fail_var "" Optional variable name to set upon failure (e.g., DEBUG_ALERT). fail_val "true" Value assigned to fail_var when assertion fails. <on_failure> (child block) Container of child nodes (<script>, <sql>, etc.) executed exclusively if the assertion fails.

docs.title: Example 1: Post-Loop Invariant Validation (Fail-Fast)
docs.text:
Verify that the while loop terminated because JobStatus reached "COMPLETED" and that the expected batch count (ProcessedCount == "75") was reached:

<flow>
    <!-- While Loop Execution -->
    <while id="MonitorWhileLoop" var="JobStatus" equals="RUNNING" max_iterations="5">
        <!-- ... child steps mutating ProcessedCount and JobStatus ... -->
    </while>

    <!-- Fail-fast assertion: Ensure JobStatus is COMPLETED -->
    <assert id="VerifyJobCompleted" 
            var="JobStatus" 
            equals="COMPLETED" 
            message="State Error: Expected JobStatus to be COMPLETED after while loop!" 
            on_failure="halt" />

    <!-- Fail-fast assertion: Verify exact processed record volume -->
    <assert id="VerifyProcessedVolume" 
            var="ProcessedCount" 
            equals="75" 
            message="Volume Mismatch: Expected ProcessedCount to reach exactly 75!" 
            on_failure="halt" />
</flow>

docs.title: Example 2: Automated Diagnostic Dumps via <on_failure>
docs.text: When an assertion fails, standard execution halts. By nesting an embedded Go or CSX <script> inside <on_failure>, you can automatically dump all live variables to stderr or generate a structured JSON post-mortem diagnostic report before the process exits.

docs.title: Embedded Go (language="go") inside <on_failure>
docs.text:
<assert id="ValidateBatchThreshold" 
        var="ProcessedCount" 
        equals="75" 
        on_failure="halt" 
        message="Critical Assertion Failed: ProcessedCount did not reach expected threshold!">
    <on_failure>
        <!-- Automated diagnostic post-mortem dump -->
        <script id="PostMortemDiagnosticGo" language="go">
            <![CDATA[
                package main

                import (
                    "encoding/json"
                    "fmt"
                    "os"
                    "sort"
                    "host/vars"
                )

                func main() {
                    fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "\n========================================================")
                    fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, " [POST-MORTEM DIAGNOSTIC DUMP: ASSERTION FAILURE]")
                    fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "========================================================")

                    allVars := vars.GetAll()
                    keys := make([]string, 0, len(allVars))
                    for k := range allVars {
                        keys = append(keys, k)
                    }
                    sort.Strings(keys)

                    for _, name := range keys {
                        fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  %-22s = %v\n", name, allVars[name])
                    }

                    // Serialize failure context to JSON for log ingestion
                    jsonPayload, _ := json.MarshalIndent(allVars, "", "  ")
                    fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\nSerialized State:\n%s\n", string(jsonPayload))
                    fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "========================================================")
                }
            ]]>
        </script>
    </on_failure>
</assert>

docs.title: C# Script (language="csx") inside <on_failure>
docs.text:
<assert id="ValidateBatchThreshold" 
        var="ProcessedCount" 
        equals="75" 
        on_failure="halt" 
        message="Critical Assertion Failed: ProcessedCount did not reach expected threshold!">
    <on_failure>
        <!-- Automated diagnostic post-mortem dump -->
        <script id="PostMortemDiagnosticCSX" language="csx">
            <![CDATA[
                using System;
                using System.Collections.Generic;
                using System.Text.Json;

                Console.Error.WriteLine("\n========================================================");
                Console.Error.WriteLine(" [POST-MORTEM DIAGNOSTIC DUMP: ASSERTION FAILURE]");
                Console.Error.WriteLine("========================================================");

                var knownKeys = new[] {
                    "DBPath", "JobStatus", "LAST_OUTPUT", "MinSalary",
                    "ProcessedCount", "TargetBatch", "Threshold", "WHILE_INDEX"
                };

                var report = new Dictionary<string, object> {
                    ["TimestampUtc"] = DateTime.UtcNow.ToString("o"),
                    ["FailureReason"] = "ProcessedCount did not match expected threshold of 75"
                };

                var varSnapshot = new Dictionary<string, string>();
                foreach (var key in knownKeys)
                {
                    string val = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(key) ?? "(null)";
                    varSnapshot[key] = val;
                    Console.Error.WriteLine($"  {key,-22} = {val}");
                }
                report["Variables"] = varSnapshot;

                string json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(report, new JsonSerializerOptions { WriteIndented = true });
                Console.Error.WriteLine("\nStructured Diagnostic JSON:\n" + json);
                Console.Error.WriteLine("========================================================");
            ]]>
        </script>
    </on_failure>
</assert>

docs.title: Example 3: Non-Halting Soft Assertions with Warning Flags (on_failure="warn")
docs.text:
In staging or non-critical diagnostic workflows, you can flag state anomalies without breaking execution. A downstream script checks the flag to decide whether to trigger deeper diagnostics:

<!-- Log warning and set DEBUG_ANOMALY=true if salary threshold was altered -->
<assert id="CheckExpectedSalaryFilter" 
        var="MinSalary" 
        equals="100000.00" 
        on_failure="warn" 
        message="Warning: MinSalary was overridden from default baseline!" 
        fail_var="DEBUG_ANOMALY" 
        fail_val="true" />

<!-- Downstream diagnostic step checks flag -->
<script id="ConditionalDiagnostics" language="csx">
    <![CDATA[
        using System;

        string isAnomaly = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("DEBUG_ANOMALY");
        if (isAnomaly == "true")
        {
            Console.WriteLine("[DEBUG NOTICE] Pipeline running under non-standard configuration!");
        }
    ]]>
</script>

docs.title: 8. Engine Comparison: Go (host/vars) vs. CSX (Environment)
docs.text: Feature / Behavior Embedded Go (language="go") C# .NET Script (language="csx") Execution Architecture In-process Yaegi interpreter Subprocess (dotnet-script) Startup Overhead Negligible ($\sim 1\text{ ms}$) Process startup ($\sim 800 - 1000\text{ ms}$) External Dependencies None (embedded in flow.exe) .NET SDK + dotnet-script tool Read Pipeline Variable vars.GetString("Key")vars.GetInt("Key")vars.GetFloat("Key")vars.GetBool("Key") Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("Key") Enumerate All Variables allVars := vars.GetAll() Query environment or iterate known pipeline variable list Mutate Variable Print to stdout + output_var="VarName" Console.Write(...) + output_var="VarName" Interactive Console Read bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin).ReadString('\n') Console.ReadLine() Halt with Error panic("reason") or os.Exit(1) throw new Exception("reason") or Environment.Exit(1) Declarative Assertion <assert var="K" equals="V" /> <assert var="K" equals="V" /> Assertion Failure Hook <on_failure> with <script language="go"> <on_failure> with <script language="csx"> Clean Normal Exit Normal function return Normal script completion Rich Library Access Standard Go packages (fmt, strings, time, etc.) Full .NET BCL, LINQ, System.Text.Json, NuGet

docs.title: 9. CLI Diagnostic Flags & Best Practices
docs.text: Flow provides command-line flags to assist with pipeline debugging without altering pipeline XML:

docs.title: 1. Schema & Structure Validation (-validate)
docs.text:
Validates that the XML conforms to the Flow XSD schema and that all required attributes are present without executing any queries or scripts: 

./flow -file examples/debug_while_loop_csx_pipeline.xml -validate

docs.title: 2. Preflight Only (-preflight)
docs.text:
Executes only <preflight> assertions (e.g. database connectivity, directory existence) and exits: 

./flow -file my_pipeline.xml -preflight

docs.title: 3. Verbose Execution Logging (-debug)
docs.text:
Enables internal engine debug logging, showing SQL query preparation, timing, and variable substitutions: 

./flow -file examples/debug_and_exit_csx_pipeline.xml -debug

docs.title: 4. Overriding Variables at Runtime (-vars)
docs.text:
Inject test parameters or override thresholds dynamically without editing the file: 

./flow -file examples/debug_and_ask_continue_csx_pipeline.xml -vars "MinSalary=120000.00"

docs.title: 5. Structured Output Inspection (-format)
docs.text:
Format step results as JSON, Pretty JSON, or Markdown for log aggregators or documentation: 

./flow -file examples/debug_specific_vars_and_exit_csx_pipeline.xml -format jsonpretty

docs.title: 10. Debugging Quick Reference Table
docs.text: Objective Go (language="go") Snippet CSX (language="csx") Snippet Print single variable fmt.Println(vars.GetString("VarName")) Console.WriteLine(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("VarName")); Parse integer variable val := vars.GetInt("LOOP_INDEX") int val = int.Parse(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("LOOP_INDEX") ?? "0"); Format multiline output fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "Val: %s\n", val) Console.WriteLine($"Val: {val}"); Store script result fmt.Print(result) with output_var="Target" Console.Write(result); with output_var="Target" Prompt user reader.ReadString('\n') string input = Console.ReadLine(); Trigger failure halt panic("Validation failed") throw new Exception("Validation failed"); Dump JSON payload bytes, _ := json.Marshal(allVars); panic(string(bytes)) string json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(vars); throw new Exception(json); Assert and fail-fast <assert var="Status" equals="COMPLETED" on_failure="halt" /> (Declarative XML tag; language-agnostic) Assert with warning flag <assert var="Env" equals="prod" on_failure="warn" fail_var="DIRTY" /> (Declarative XML tag; language-agnostic) Post-mortem state dump <on_failure> wrapping Go diagnostic dump <on_failure> wrapping CSX System.Text.Json dump

docs.title: Cross-Platform Encryption Guide for Flow
docs.text:
Flow provides native, cross-platform AES-256-GCM encryption and decryption across Windows, Linux, macOS, and FreeBSD with zero external runtime dependencies.

This system allows you to protect sensitive pipeline configurations, connection strings, credentials, and XML option files both at rest in the filesystem and inside database repositories (dbo.flow_pipeline_content, dbo.flow_options_content, dbo.flow_config_content, or SQLite builder databases).

docs.title: 1. Cryptographic Architecture
docs.text:
• Cipher: AES-256 in Galois/Counter Mode (AES-256-GCM), providing authenticated encryption with associated data (AEAD).
  • Key Derivation: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 100,000 iterations and a cryptographically secure 16-byte random salt generated via crypto/rand.
  • Tamper Proofing: 128-bit (16-byte) authentication tag; any modification, bit flip, or truncated payload is automatically rejected with an authentication error before any processing occurs.
  • Pure Go Implementation: Implemented with Go's standard library (crypto/aes, crypto/cipher, crypto/rand, crypto/sha256) and pure-Go PBKDF2 (golang.org/x/crypto/pbkdf2). No CGO, Windows DPAPI, or macOS Keychain dependencies required.
  • In-Memory Zeroization: Derived symmetric AES key buffers are zeroed out (ZeroBytes) immediately upon cipher initialization to prevent plaintext key exposure in memory dumps.

docs.title: 2. Text-Safe Envelope Specification
docs.text:
To ensure encrypted data can be safely stored in database string columns (such as SQL Server NVARCHAR(MAX) or SQLite TEXT) without Unicode or byte-encoding corruption, Flow formats ciphertexts into an armored text envelope:

FLOWENC:v1:<base64(salt || nonce || ciphertext || auth_tag)>
  • FLOWENC:v1: Header prefix identifying the envelope version.
  • salt: 16-byte random salt used during PBKDF2 derivation.
  • nonce: 12-byte standard GCM initialization vector / nonce.
  • ciphertext: AES-256-GCM encrypted payload.
  • auth_tag: 16-byte authentication tag verifying payload integrity.

The envelope prefix enables flow.exe, db_importer, and crypto_tool to automatically detect encrypted files and provide helpful error messages if a key is missing.

docs.title: 3. Key Management & Precedence
docs.text:
Encryption and decryption keys can be passed through key files, CLI flags, or environment variables:

Priority Method Description 1 (Highest) -key-file <path> Path to a secure key file. Recommended to avoid exposing plaintext passphrases in OS process listings (ps, Task Manager). 2 -secure-key <key> Command-line parameter supplied directly to flow.exe, db_importer, or crypto_tool. (Note: emits a warning to stderr recommending -key-file). 3 FLOW_SECURE_KEY Environment variable (ideal for containerized and automated production runs). 4 SECURE_KEY Generic fallback environment variable.

[!TIP] For production automation and scheduled jobs, always supply keys via -key-file or FLOW_SECURE_KEY. Passing plaintext keys via CLI arguments (-secure-key) makes them visible to other local processes and unprivileged users inspecting process arguments.

docs.title: 4. Standalone Tool: crypto_tool
docs.text: Flow includes a dedicated CLI utility located in crypto_tool/ to generate keys and perform offline encryption/decryption.

docs.title: Generate a Cryptographically Secure Key
docs.text:
# Generate a new 256-bit base64-encoded key
crypto_tool -gen-key

docs.title: Encrypt a File
docs.text:
# Encrypt an XML pipeline to text-armored format
crypto_tool -action encrypt -in pipeline.xml -out pipeline.xml.enc -secure-key "MySecretPassphrase123!"

# Encrypt using an environment variable
export FLOW_SECURE_KEY="MySecretPassphrase123!"
crypto_tool -action encrypt -in config.xml -out config.xml.enc

docs.title: Decrypt a File
docs.text: crypto_tool -action decrypt -in pipeline.xml.enc -out pipeline.xml -secure-key "MySecretPassphrase123!"

docs.title: Raw Binary Mode (Optional)
docs.text:
If you specifically need a raw binary file instead of the armored text envelope: 

crypto_tool -action encrypt -in secret.bin -out secret.enc -binary -secure-key "Key123"

docs.title: 5. Database Importer: db_importer
docs.text: The db_importer tool imports and exports pipelines, options, and configs to/from SQL Server repositories, with support for encryption at rest:

docs.title: Import and Encrypt into SQL Server
docs.text:
# Encrypts the local file before inserting/merging into dbo.flow_pipeline_content
db_importer -dsn "sqlserver://sa:Password123!@localhost:1433?database=master" \
            -table pipeline \
            -name "daily_customer_sync" \
            -file "pipelines/sync.xml" \
            -encrypted \
            -secure-key "MySecretPassphrase123!"

docs.title: Export from SQL Server and Decrypt
docs.text:
# Fetches from dbo.flow_pipeline_content, decrypts in memory, and writes plain XML to disk
db_importer -action export \
            -dsn "sqlserver://sa:Password123!@localhost:1433?database=master" \
            -table pipeline \
            -name "daily_customer_sync" \
            -file "sync_decrypted.xml" \
            -encrypted \
            -secure-key "MySecretPassphrase123!"

docs.title: 6. Running Encrypted Pipelines with flow.exe
docs.text: flow.exe can execute encrypted pipelines, options, and configuration overrides whether they reside on disk, an HTTP endpoint, or inside a SQL database.

docs.title: Running Encrypted Files from Disk
docs.text: flow.exe -file pipeline.xml.enc -encrypted -secure-key "MySecretPassphrase123!"

docs.title: Running Encrypted Pipelines from a Database
docs.text:
flow.exe -encrypted -secure-key "MySecretPassphrase123!" \
         -file "sql://sqlserver@localhost:1433?database=master#SELECT PipelineXML FROM dbo.flow_pipeline_content WHERE Name = 'daily_customer_sync'"

docs.title: Running Encrypted Options from a Database
docs.text:
flow.exe -encrypted -secure-key "MySecretPassphrase123!" \
         -options "sql://sqlserver@localhost:1433?database=master#SELECT OptionsXML FROM dbo.flow_options_content WHERE Name = 'PROD_OPTIONS'"

docs.title: Auto-Detection
docs.text: If flow.exe loads a file or database record beginning with FLOWENC:v1:, it automatically detects that the resource is encrypted and uses the configured key (-secure-key or FLOW_SECURE_KEY) without requiring the -encrypted flag.

docs.title: 7. flow.exe Draft Import & Export
docs.text: flow.exe can also export and import drafts directly from the local SQLite builder database (flow_builder.db) or external databases:

docs.title: Exporting an Encrypted Pipeline Draft
docs.text:
flow.exe -export-file pipeline_backup.xml.enc \
         -export-name "daily_etl" \
         -export-type pipeline \
         -encrypted \
         -secure-key "MySecretPassphrase123!"

docs.title: Importing an Encrypted Draft into Builder Storage
docs.text:
# Decrypts the draft on import so it can be visually inspected and edited in the builder
flow.exe -import-file pipeline_backup.xml.enc \
         -import-name "daily_etl" \
         -import-type pipeline \
         -secure-key "MySecretPassphrase123!"

docs.title: 8. Digital Signatures & Security Architecture
docs.text:
Flow includes comprehensive digital signature creation and verification supporting OpenSSL (RSA, ECDSA, Ed25519), OpenPGP / GPG, and PKCS#7 / CMS in pure Go with zero OS dependencies.

  • Decoupled Security Pipeline: Signature verification occurs prior to decryption (Verify -> Decrypt -> Parse -> Execute), preventing tampered or unauthorized payloads from being processed.
  • Full Documentation: See SIGNATURES.md for complete instructions, key generation guides, and engine flags (-verify-signature, -public-key, -cert, -ca-cert, -keyring, -signature).

docs.title: Pipeline Failure Response & Error Propagation
docs.text:
By default, go-flow uses fail-fast execution. When a node fails, the remaining nodes in the pipeline will not continue.

This document details how failure propagation, cooperative cancellation, transactional rollbacks, and explicit recovery blocks work across every orchestration primitive in the flow runtime engine.

docs.title: Summary Matrix
docs.text: Orchestration Context Default Behavior on Node Failure Remaining Sibling Nodes Downstream Pipeline Nodes Special Recovery / Cleanup Sequential (<flow>, <preflight>, <group>, <if>) Fail-Fast Skipped immediately Skipped None (unless inside <assert>) Parallel (<parallel>) Cooperative Cancel Queued tasks skipped; in-flight workers receive ctx.Done() Skipped after wg.Wait() Worker variables only merged after barrier Loops (<foreach>, <while>) Abort Loop Remaining children in current iteration & future iterations skipped Skipped Active DB cursor closed immediately Transactional Group (<group transaction="true">) Rollback & Halt Skipped immediately Skipped Automatic ROLLBACK (or ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT if nested) Assertion (<assert on_failure="halt">) Run Fallback, Then Halt Skipped Skipped Executes nested <on_failure> child nodes before halting Assertion (<assert on_failure="warn"> / "continue") Warn & Continue Executed normally Executed normally Sets fail_var/fail_val and runs <on_failure> children

docs.title: 1. Sequential Nodes (<flow>, <preflight>, <group>, <if>)
docs.text:
In Executor.executeNodes, pipeline nodes are evaluated sequentially inside a for loop. Each node handler returns a boolean hasErr:

  • As soon as any node returns hasErr == true, executeNodes emits the node failure event to registered sinks (pipeline_events), appends the ScriptResult, and immediately returns true to its caller.
  • All subsequent sibling nodes and parent containers are bypassed.
  • Executor.executeRun records the overall run status as failed in pipeline_runs, and go-flow exits with return code 1.
flowchart TD
    Start(["Start Pipeline Run"]) --> N1["Execute Node 1"]
    N1 --> Check1{"hasErr == true?"}
    Check1 -- "No (Success)" --> N2["Execute Node 2"]
    Check1 -- "Yes (Failed)" --> EmitFail["Emit Node Failed Event<br/>(pipeline_events)"]

    N2 --> Check2{"hasErr == true?"}
    Check2 -- "No (Success)" --> N3["Execute Node 3"]
    Check2 -- "Yes (Failed)" --> EmitFail

    N3 -. "Skipped on Node 1/2 Failure" .-> EmitFail
    EmitFail --> FinishRun["Mark Run Status = 'failed'<br/>(pipeline_runs)"]
    FinishRun --> Exit1(["OS Exit(1)"])

docs.title: 2. Parallel Blocks (<parallel>)
docs.text:
In Executor.executeParallelNode, child nodes run concurrently across a bounded worker pool (max_threads, defaulting to 4) sharing a derived cancellable context (pCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)).

When any child worker fails (childErr == true): 1. Immediate Context Cancellation: The failing worker sets an atomic flag (hasErr.Store(true)) and invokes cancel() on pCtx. 2. Queued Siblings Skipped: The dispatcher loop checks hasErr.Load() || pCtx.Err() != nil before acquiring the semaphore and immediately stops scheduling any remaining unstarted child nodes in the <parallel> block. 3. In-Flight Siblings Notified: Currently executing sibling goroutines receive the cancellation signal via pCtx.Done(), which aborts context-aware operations (such as SQL queries via QueryContext/ExecContext, shell/CSX scripts via exec.CommandContext, HTTP requests, and loops). 4. Join Barrier & Halt: wg.Wait() waits for all active workers to finish cleaning up. Because executeParallelNode returns true, no downstream nodes after <parallel> will execute.

sequenceDiagram
    participant Main as Main Executor
    participant Pool as <parallel> Dispatcher (pCtx)
    participant W1 as Worker 1 (Fails)
    participant W2 as Worker 2 (In-Flight)
    participant W3 as Worker 3 (Queued)

    Main->>Pool: Enter <parallel max_threads="2">
    Pool->>W1: Spawn Worker 1 (pCtx)
    Pool->>W2: Spawn Worker 2 (pCtx)
    Note over W3: Waiting for semaphore slot

    W1--xPool: Node fails (childErr = true)
    Pool->>Pool: hasErr.Store(true) & cancel(pCtx)
    Pool-->>W2: pCtx.Done() signal delivered
    Pool--xW3: Dispatcher breaks loop (Worker 3 never starts)
    W2-->>Pool: Aborts context-aware op & exits
    Pool->>Main: wg.Wait() completes -> returns hasErr = true
    Note over Main: Downstream pipeline nodes skipped

docs.title: 3. Iterative Loops (<foreach>, <while>)
docs.text:
Both <foreach> (Executor.executeForEachNode, in both streaming and buffered modes) and <while> (Executor.executeWhileNode) evaluate their child nodes sequentially on each iteration via e.executeNodes(ctx, node.Children, results).

  • If any child node fails during iteration $k$:
  • Remaining child nodes in iteration $k$ are skipped.
  • For <foreach>, the active database sql.Rows cursor is immediately closed (rows.Close()).
  • Subsequent iterations ($k+1, \dots, N$) are aborted.
  • The error bubbles up and halts the rest of the pipeline.
flowchart TD
    LoopStart(["Enter <foreach> / <while>"]) --> Cond{"Next Row /<br/>Condition True?"}
    Cond -- "No" --> LoopDone(["Loop Complete (Continue Pipeline)"])
    Cond -- "Yes" --> Child1["Iteration k: Child Node 1"]
    Child1 --> CheckC1{"hasErr?"}
    CheckC1 -- "No" --> Child2["Iteration k: Child Node 2"]
    CheckC1 -- "Yes" --> AbortLoop["Close DB Cursor (if <foreach>)<br/>Skip Child Node 2 & Future Iterations"]
    Child2 --> CheckC2{"hasErr?"}
    CheckC2 -- "No" --> Cond
    CheckC2 -- "Yes" --> AbortLoop
    AbortLoop --> Halt(["Bubble Error Up & Halt Pipeline"])

docs.title: 4. Transactional Groups (<group transaction="true">)
docs.text:
When a <group> has transaction="true" and a target db configured:

  • Top-Level Transaction: Begins a database transaction (dbConn.BeginTx) and pushes it onto the executor's active transaction stack for that database.
