Pipeline variable interpolation is supported. sheet No Worksheet name to read. Defaults to the workbook's first worksheet. header No Boolean that controls whether the first row contains column names. Defaults to true; the first row becomes the JSON object keys. output_var Conditional Name of the pipeline variable that receives the serialized JSON. This is the preferred output variable name. var Conditional Alias for output_var, used when output_var is empty.

Notes: - Provide output_var or var to retain the JSON under a named pipeline variable; the value is also stored in LAST_OUTPUT. - With header="false", the current runtime produces an empty JSON array because it serializes rows only when a header row is enabled.

docs.title: <json_path>
docs.text:
The <json_path> element extracts values or nodes from JSON supplied by a file or pipeline variable.

Attribute / field Mandatory Description id No Unique identifier for the JSON-path step. If omitted, Flow generates an identifier in the form json_path_N. file Conditional Path to the source JSON file. Supports pipeline variable interpolation and takes precedence over var. var Conditional Name of the pipeline variable containing source JSON. Used when file is not set. path Conditional JSONPath query expression. Takes precedence over jsonpath; required when query content is not supplied inline. jsonpath Conditional Alias for path, used when path is empty. mode No Output format: value (default) joins matched values with newlines; json returns a single match as JSON or multiple matches as an array; json_array always returns matches as a JSON array. output_var Conditional Name of the pipeline variable that receives the extracted value. This is the preferred output variable name. out_var Conditional Alias for output_var, used when output_var is empty. content Conditional Inline JSONPath query placed between the opening and closing <json_path> tags. Used when neither path nor jsonpath is set.

Notes: - Supply one JSON source (file or var), one JSONPath expression, and one output attribute (output_var or out_var). - Extracted output is stored in the selected output variable and in LAST_OUTPUT.

docs.title: <yaml_path>
docs.text:
The <yaml_path> element extracts values or nodes from YAML supplied by a file or pipeline variable.

Attribute / field Mandatory Description id No Unique identifier for the YAML-path step. If omitted, Flow generates an identifier in the form yaml_path_N. file Conditional Path to the source YAML file. Supports pipeline variable interpolation and takes precedence over var. var Conditional Name of the pipeline variable containing source YAML. Used when file is not set. path Conditional Path query expression evaluated against the YAML converted to normalized JSON. Takes precedence over yamlpath; required when query content is not supplied inline. yamlpath Conditional Alias for path, used when path is empty. mode No Output format: value (default) joins matched values with newlines; json returns a single match as JSON or multiple matches as an array; json_array always returns matches as a JSON array; yaml serializes matched nodes as YAML. output_var Conditional Name of the pipeline variable that receives the extracted value. This is the preferred output variable name. out_var Conditional Alias for output_var, used when output_var is empty. content Conditional Inline path query placed between the opening and closing <yaml_path> tags. Used when neither path nor yamlpath is set.

Notes: - Supply one YAML source (file or var), one path expression, and one output attribute (output_var or out_var). - Extracted output is stored in the selected output variable and in LAST_OUTPUT.

docs.title: <xml_xpath>
docs.text:
Flow implements XML-path extraction with the <xml_xpath> element. It evaluates an XPath expression against XML supplied by a file or pipeline variable.

Attribute / field Mandatory Description id No Unique identifier for the XML-path step. file Conditional Path to the source XML file. Supports pipeline variable interpolation and takes precedence over var. var Conditional Name of the pipeline variable containing source XML. Used when file is not set. xpath Conditional XPath expression to evaluate. Required when the expression is not supplied as inline content. mode No Output format: text (default) joins each matched node's inner text with newlines; xml joins serialized matched nodes with newlines; json_array returns the matched outputs as a JSON array of strings. output_var Yes Name of the pipeline variable that receives the extracted output. content Conditional Inline XPath expression placed between the opening and closing <xml_xpath> tags. Used when xpath is not set.

Notes: - Supply one XML source (file or var), one XPath expression, and output_var. - Extracted output is stored in output_var and in LAST_OUTPUT.

docs.title: <http_client>
docs.text:
The <http_client> element sends an HTTP request and can store its response body and status code in pipeline variables.

Attribute / field Mandatory Description id No Unique identifier for the HTTP-client step. If omitted, Flow generates an identifier in the form http_N. uri Conditional Target request URL. Takes precedence over url; one endpoint attribute is required. url Conditional Alias for uri, used when uri is empty. method No HTTP method. Defaults to GET. data No Request payload. Takes precedence over inline content and supports pipeline variable interpolation. content Conditional Inline request payload placed between the opening and closing <http_client> tags. Used when data is empty. headers No Custom headers as comma-, semicolon-, or newline-separated Name: Value pairs. content_type No Sets the request Content-Type header. var No Response-body variable name. This alias has the highest precedence. variable No Alias for the response-body variable, used when var is empty. output_var No Alias for the response-body variable, used when var and variable are empty. output_variable No Alias for the response-body variable, used when earlier aliases are empty. out_var No Alias for the response-body variable, used when all earlier aliases are empty. status_code_var No Variable name that receives the HTTP status code. This alias has the highest precedence. status_code_variable No Alias for status_code_var. status_var No Alias for status_code_var. status_variable No Alias for status_code_var. timeout No Total request timeout as a Go duration, such as 30s or 2m. follow_redirects No Whether to automatically follow redirect responses. max_redirects No Maximum number of redirects permitted before the request fails. cookie_jar No Enables an in-memory cookie jar for the request client. proxy No HTTP proxy URL. tls_insecure_skip_verify No Disables TLS certificate verification. Use only for trusted development or test endpoints. tls_handshake_timeout No Maximum TLS handshake duration. tls_server_name No Server name used for TLS SNI and certificate verification. tls_min_version / tls_max_version No Minimum or maximum permitted TLS version. disable_keep_alives / disable_compression No Disable connection reuse or automatic compression handling. max_idle_conns / max_idle_conns_per_host / max_conns_per_host No Connection-pool limits. idle_conn_timeout / response_header_timeout / expect_continue_timeout No Transport timeouts expressed as Go durations. max_response_header_bytes No Maximum response-header size in bytes. write_buffer_size / read_buffer_size No HTTP transport buffer sizes in bytes. force_attempt_http2 No Forces HTTP/2 negotiation when supported by the transport.

Notes: - Endpoint, header, content type, and payload values support pipeline variable interpolation. - The response body is always stored in LAST_OUTPUT; provide a response output alias to store it under a named variable.

docs.title: Example Pipeline Description
docs.text:
This section provides an example of how to describe a pipeline, including its purpose, the databases it interacts with, and the scripts it executes. A well-documented pipeline helps in understanding its workflow and facilitates maintenance and collaboration.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<pipeline description="Monthly Sales and Inventory Report Pipeline" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etl-madness/flow/main/xsd/pipeline.xsd">
    <databases>
        <database name="sales_db" 
                  driver="postgres" 
                  connection_string="host=localhost port=5432 user=postgres password=secret dbname=sales sslmode=disable" 
                  description="Primary Analytics Database" />
    </databases>

    <flow>
        <!-- Tab 1: Executive Summary -->
        <excel_write id="export_summary" 
                     file="reports/Monthly_Executive_Report.xlsx" 
                     sheet="Summary KPI" 
                     db="sales_db"
                     description="Writes top-level monthly KPIs to the first tab">
            SELECT 
                DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month,
                COUNT(order_id) AS total_orders,
                SUM(total_amount) AS total_revenue
            FROM orders
            GROUP BY 1
            ORDER BY 1 DESC;
        </excel_write>

        <!-- Tab 2: Customer Breakdown -->
        <excel_write id="export_customers" 
                     file="reports/Monthly_Executive_Report.xlsx" 
                     sheet="Customer Details" 
                     db="sales_db"
                     description="Appends customer breakdown to a second tab">
            SELECT 
                customer_id,
                company_name,
                country,
                total_spent
            FROM customer_summary
            WHERE total_spent > 10000;
        </excel_write>

        <!-- Tab 3: Regional Inventory -->
        <excel_write id="export_inventory" 
                     file="reports/Monthly_Executive_Report.xlsx" 
                     sheet="Inventory Status" 
                     db="sales_db"
                     description="Appends inventory levels to a third tab">
            SELECT 
                warehouse_id,
                product_sku,
                stock_on_hand,
                reorder_level
            FROM warehouse_inventory;
        </excel_write>
    </flow>
</pipeline>

docs.title: Developer Guide: Adding Modal Tooltips & Documentation Popups to Builder Nodes
docs.text:
This guide explains how to add modal tooltips, interactive documentation popups, and context-aware help links to nodes and form fields in the Flow Pipeline Builder.

It covers both lightweight HTML tooltips and full interactive modal dialogs (similar to the Database Connection Strings Guide), detailing the complete end-to-end architecture across catalog metadata, backend API endpoints, embedded files, frontend templates, markdown rendering, and automated testing.

docs.title: 1. Architectural Overview
docs.text:
Flow Builder supports three tiers of node and attribute assistance:

Tier Component Type Interaction Purpose Tier 1: Inline Attribute Tooltips Native title & helper text Mouse hover / subtitle Brief attribute explanation (1–2 sentences), parameter defaults, variable substitution notes. Tier 2: Field-Level Modal Links Interactive link / button Click Contextual popup trigger next to a specific field label (e.g., 📖 Connection String Guide or Driver Reference ↗). Tier 3: Section / Node-Level Popups Header action button Click Full documentation modal with real-time search, quick-jump pills, syntax examples, and one-click form insertion (⚡ Use Example).

docs.title: Component Flow Diagram
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph Metadata ["1. Component Catalog"]
        Catalog["builder/catalog.go<br/>ComponentMeta & ComponentField"]
    end

    subgraph Backend ["2. Backend Server & Assets"]
        DocFile["docs/your_topic.md<br/>Markdown Resource"]
        Embed["builder/templates.go<br/>//go:embed"]
        Server["builder/server.go<br/>GET /api/docs/{topic}"]
    end

    subgraph Frontend ["3. Builder UI Engine"]
        CanvasPartial["builder/tmpl/partials/canvas_nodes.html<br/>Section Trigger Button"]
        NodeModal["builder/tmpl/index.html<br/>renderModalFields() Helper Link"]
        DocModal["#your-docs-modal or #db-docs-modal<br/>Interactive Modal Dialog"]
        Renderer["renderMarkdownToHtml()<br/>Markdown Parser & Syntax Styler"]
        Sync["builder/html_content.go<br/>Standalone Embedded String"]
    end

    Catalog --> NodeModal
    DocFile --> Embed --> Server
    DocFile -. Dev Hot-Reload .-> Server
    CanvasPartial --> DocModal
    NodeModal --> DocModal
    DocModal --> Server
    Server --> Renderer
    Renderer --> DocModal
    DocModal -. "⚡ Use Example" .-> NodeModal

docs.title: 2. Step-by-Step Implementation Guide
docs.text: Follow these 7 steps to add a documentation modal or tooltip to any node (e.g., <http>, <sql>, <template>, <assert>, <file>, <json_path>, <xml_path>).

docs.title: Step 1: Define Field Tooltips in builder/catalog.go
docs.text:
In builder/catalog.go, every node is represented by a ComponentMeta struct, and every attribute is a ComponentField.

  1. Open builder/catalog.go.
  2. Locate your component (e.g. http, sql, template, assert).
  3. Set the Description attribute on each field. This string is automatically rendered as helper text under the input field and used in hover tooltips:
{
    Type:        "http_client",
    Tag:         "http_client",
    Name:        "HTTP / REST Client",
    Category:    "Integration & Web",
    Description: "Executes HTTP GET/POST/PUT/DELETE requests with headers and payload handling.",
    Section:     "flow",
    HasContent:  true,
    ContentHelp: "Request body content (for POST/PUT). Supports JSON and variable interpolation.",
    Fields: []ComponentField{
        {Name: "id", Label: "Step ID", Type: "text", Mandatory: true, Description: "Unique step ID for logging and orchestration"},
        {Name: "url", Label: "Endpoint URL", Type: "text", Mandatory: true, Description: "Target endpoint URL (supports {{Variables}} & query params)"},
        {Name: "method", Label: "HTTP Method", Type: "select", Mandatory: true, Default: "GET", Options: []string{"GET", "POST", "PUT", "DELETE", "PATCH", "HEAD", "OPTIONS"}, Description: "HTTP request verb"},
        {Name: "headers", Label: "Request Headers", Type: "text", Mandatory: false, Description: `Custom headers: {"Authorization":"Bearer {{Token}}"} or K1:V1,K2:V2`},
        {Name: "content_type", Label: "Content-Type", Type: "text", Mandatory: false, Description: "Shortcut for Content-Type header (e.g. application/json, text/xml)"},
        {Name: "into", Label: "Response Variable", Type: "text", Mandatory: false, Description: "Variable name receiving the response body (alias output_var)"},
        {Name: "status_into", Label: "Status Code Variable", Type: "text", Mandatory: false, Description: "Variable name receiving HTTP status code (e.g. 200, 404)"},
        {Name: "timeout", Label: "Timeout Duration", Type: "text", Mandatory: false, Description: "Total request timeout duration (e.g. 10s, 30s, 2m)"},
        {Name: "proxy", Label: "HTTP Proxy URL", Type: "text", Mandatory: false, Description: "Proxy URL (e.g. http://proxy.internal:8080)"},
        {Name: "tls_insecure_skip_verify", Label: "Skip TLS Verify", Type: "select", Mandatory: false, Default: "false", Options: []string{"false", "true"}, Description: "Disable SSL/TLS certificate validation checks"},
        {Name: "follow_redirects", Label: "Follow Redirects", Type: "select", Mandatory: false, Default: "true", Options: []string{"true", "false"}, Description: "Follow HTTP 3xx redirect responses automatically"},
        {Name: "description", Label: "Description", Type: "text", Mandatory: false, Description: "Step explanation displayed in logs and flowcharts"},
    },
    DefaultXML: `<http_client id="FetchRemoteData" url="https://api.example.com/data" method="GET" into="ApiResponse" />`,
}

docs.title: Step 2: Prepare the Markdown Documentation Resource
docs.text:
1. Place or edit your canonical markdown file under docs/ (for example, docs/http_client.md or docs/templates.md).
  2. Make a copy under builder/tmpl/ for standalone compilation: 
    Copy-Item docs/http_client.md builder/tmpl/docs_http_client.md
  3. Update the //go:embed directive in builder/templates.go to include the new file:
// In builder/templates.go:
//go:embed tmpl/*.html tmpl/partials/*.html tmpl/docs_connection_strings.md tmpl/docs_http_client.md
var templateFS embed.FS

docs.title: Step 3: Add the Backend HTTP Endpoint in builder/server.go
docs.text:
In builder/server.go, implement an API handler that returns the documentation JSON. Always use the dual-source strategy (check disk first for live development changes, fall back to embedded filesystem for standalone binaries):

// handleHttpClientDoc serves the HTTP Client documentation markdown.
func (s *Server) handleHttpClientDoc(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    if r.Method != http.MethodGet {
        http.Error(w, "Method Not Allowed", http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
        return
    }

    docFilename := "http_client.md"
    diskCandidates := []string{
        filepath.Join("docs", docFilename),
        filepath.Join("..", "docs", docFilename),
        filepath.Join("builder", "tmpl", "docs_http_client.md"),
    }

    var content []byte
    var usedPath string

    for _, p := range diskCandidates {
        if b, err := os.ReadFile(p); err == nil && len(b) > 0 {
            content = b
            usedPath = p
            break
        }
    }

    // Fall back to embedded filesystem for standalone binary
    if len(content) == 0 {
        if b, err := templateFS.ReadFile("tmpl/docs_http_client.md"); err == nil && len(b) > 0 {
            content = b
            usedPath = "embedded:tmpl/docs_http_client.md"
        }
    }

    if len(content) == 0 {
        http.Error(w, "HTTP Client documentation not found", http.StatusNotFound)
        return
    }

    w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
    json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(map[string]string{
        "filename": docFilename,
        "path":     usedPath,
        "content":  string(content),
    })
}

Register the endpoint in registerRoutes under the authentication middleware:

// In builder/server.go under authenticated router:
s.mux.Handle("/api/docs/http-client", s.requireAuth(http.HandlerFunc(s.handleHttpClientDoc)))

docs.title: Step 4: Wire Trigger Links & Dynamic Header Guide in builder/tmpl/index.html
docs.text: When a user adds or edits a node, renderModalFields and modal openers dynamically construct the form inputs and configure header buttons.

docs.title: 4.1 Modal Header Guide Button (#node-modal-guide-btn)
docs.text:
In #node-modal header, add a dynamic guide button that adapts based on the active node type:

<button type="button" id="node-modal-guide-btn" class="hidden text-xs px-2.5 py-1 bg-slate-800 hover:bg-slate-700 text-cyan-400 hover:text-cyan-300 border border-slate-700/80 rounded transition cursor-pointer flex items-center space-x-1 font-medium">
    <span>📖 Guide</span>
</button>

Wire updateNodeModalGuideButton(nodeType) into openAddNodeModal(type, ...) and openEditNode(id, type, ...):

function updateNodeModalGuideButton(nodeType) {
    const guideBtn = document.getElementById('node-modal-guide-btn');
    if (!guideBtn) return;
    if (nodeType === 'http_client') {
        guideBtn.innerHTML = '<span>📖 HTTP Guide</span>';
        guideBtn.setAttribute('onclick', 'openHttpDocsModal()');
        guideBtn.setAttribute('title', 'Open HTTP Client Guide (docs/http_client.md)');
        guideBtn.classList.remove('hidden');
    } else if (nodeType === 'database') {
        guideBtn.innerHTML = '<span>📖 DB Guide</span>';
        guideBtn.setAttribute('onclick', 'openDbDocsModal()');
        guideBtn.setAttribute('title', 'Open Database Connection Strings Guide');
        guideBtn.classList.remove('hidden');
    } else {
        guideBtn.classList.add('hidden');
    }
}

docs.title: 4.2 Inline Field-Level Triggers in renderModalFields()
docs.text:
To add contextual helper links directly to specific form fields (such as url and headers for http_client):

// Field-specific helper link next to the label
let labelExtra = '';
if (f.name === 'connection_string') {
    labelExtra = '<button type="button" onclick="openDbDocsModal(getModalCurrentDriver())" class="text-[11px] text-cyan-400 hover:text-cyan-300 font-medium underline underline-offset-2 cursor-pointer flex items-center space-x-1" title="View documentation and examples"><span>📖 Connection String Guide</span></button>';
} else if (f.name === 'url' && (meta.type === 'http_client' || meta.tag === 'http_client')) {
    labelExtra = '<button type="button" onclick="openHttpDocsModal()" class="text-[11px] text-cyan-400 hover:text-cyan-300 font-medium underline underline-offset-2 cursor-pointer flex items-center space-x-1" title="View HTTP Client documentation, headers, and request examples from docs/http_client.md"><span>📖 HTTP Client Guide</span></button>';
} else if (f.name === 'headers' && (meta.type === 'http_client' || meta.tag === 'http_client')) {
    labelExtra = '<button type="button" onclick="openHttpDocsModal(\'headers\')" class="text-[11px] text-cyan-400 hover:text-cyan-300 font-medium underline underline-offset-2 cursor-pointer flex items-center space-x-1" title="Jump to Headers documentation"><span>📖 Headers Ref</span></button>';
}

// Assemble the label header
div.innerHTML = '<div class="flex justify-between items-center">' +
    '<label class="text-xs font-medium text-slate-300">' + f.label + (f.mandatory ? ' <span class="text-red-400">*</span>' : '') + '</label>' +
    '<div class="flex items-center space-x-2">' + labelExtra + '<span class="text-[10px] text-slate-500">' + (f.description || '') + '</span></div>' +
'</div>' + inputHtml;

And optionally add inline helper footers below inputs:

} else if (f.name === 'url' && (meta.type === 'http_client' || meta.tag === 'http_client')) {
    inputHtml = '<div class="space-y-1">' +
        '<input type="text" id="attr_' + f.name + '" name="attr_' + f.name + '" value="' + (val || '').replace(/"/g, '"') + '" placeholder="https://api.example.com/v1/resource" class="w-full bg-slate-950 border border-slate-700 rounded p-1.5 text-xs text-cyan-300 font-mono focus:outline-none focus:border-blue-500">' +
        '<div class="flex justify-between items-center text-[10px] text-slate-500">' +
            '<span>Supports {{Variables}} and query parameters</span>' +
            '<a href="javascript:void(0)" onclick="openHttpDocsModal()" class="text-cyan-400 hover:text-cyan-300 hover:underline cursor-pointer">HTTP Reference & Headers ↗</a>' +
        '</div>' +
    '</div>';
}

docs.title: Step 5: Add Guide Buttons to Canvas & Node Cards
docs.text:
1. Canvas Section Headers (builder/tmpl/partials/canvas_nodes.html): 

    <div class="flex items-center space-x-1.5">
    <button type="button" onclick="openDbDocsModal()" class="px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-medium bg-slate-800 hover:bg-slate-700 text-cyan-400 hover:text-cyan-300 border border-slate-700 rounded transition flex items-center space-x-1 cursor-pointer" title="View documentation and connection string examples for all supported databases">
        <span>📖 Connection Guide</span>
    </button>
    <button type="button" onclick="openAddNodeModal('database', 'Database Connection', 'databases')" class="px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-medium bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-500 text-white rounded transition flex items-center space-x-1 cursor-pointer">
        <span>＋ Add Database</span>
    </button>
</div>

  2. Canvas Node Cards (builder/tmpl/partials/node_card.html): In leaf node headers, expose a direct documentation shortcut button: 

    {{if eq .NodeType "http_client"}}
<button type="button" onclick="openHttpDocsModal()" class="p-1 hover:bg-slate-700 rounded text-cyan-400 hover:text-cyan-300 transition text-[11px]" title="Open HTTP Client Guide (docs/http_client.md)">📖</button>
{{else if eq .NodeType "database"}}
<button type="button" onclick="openDbDocsModal()" class="p-1 hover:bg-slate-700 rounded text-cyan-400 hover:text-cyan-300 transition text-[11px]" title="Open Connection String Guide">📖</button>
{{end}}

docs.title: Step 6: Create the Popup Modal & Client-Side Logic
Modal HTML Container Pattern
docs.text:
Add the modal structure right before <!-- EVENT DETAIL MODAL --> in builder/tmpl/index.html:

<!-- HTTP CLIENT DOCS MODAL -->
<div id="http-docs-modal" class="hidden fixed inset-0 bg-black/80 backdrop-blur-sm flex items-center justify-center p-4 z-[75]" onclick="if(event.target===this)closeHttpDocsModal()">
    <div class="bg-slate-900 border border-slate-800 rounded-xl max-w-5xl w-full p-6 shadow-2xl flex flex-col space-y-4 max-h-[92vh]">
        <!-- Header -->
        <div class="flex items-center justify-between border-b border-slate-800 pb-3">
            <div class="flex items-center space-x-3">
                <span class="text-2xl">🌐</span>
                <div>
                    <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-white flex items-center space-x-2">
                        <span>HTTP Client & API Guide</span>
                        <span class="text-[10px] font-mono px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-slate-800 text-slate-400 border border-slate-700">docs/http_client.md</span>
                    </h3>
                    <p class="text-xs text-slate-400">REST methods, authentication headers, query parameters, and payload examples</p>
                </div>
            </div>
            <div class="flex items-center space-x-2">
                <button type="button" onclick="copyHttpDocsRaw()" id="btn-copy-raw-http-docs" class="text-xs px-2.5 py-1 bg-slate-800 hover:bg-slate-700 text-slate-300 rounded border border-slate-700 transition cursor-pointer">📋 Copy Markdown</button>
                <button onclick="closeHttpDocsModal()" class="text-slate-400 hover:text-white text-xl leading-none px-2 py-1 cursor-pointer">×</button>
            </div>
        </div>

        <!-- Filter & Quick Jumps -->
        <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-2 bg-slate-950/70 p-2.5 rounded-lg border border-slate-800">
            <div class="flex items-center space-x-2 flex-1 min-w-[200px]">
                <span class="text-xs text-slate-500">🔍</span>
                <input type="text" id="http-docs-filter" oninput="filterHttpDocs(this.value)" placeholder="Search endpoints, headers, auth..." class="w-full bg-transparent text-xs text-white placeholder-slate-500 focus:outline-none">
            </div>
            <div class="flex items-center space-x-1 text-[11px] overflow-x-auto">
                <button type="button" onclick="jumpToHttpSection('attributes')" class="px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-slate-800 hover:bg-blue-600 text-slate-300 hover:text-white transition cursor-pointer">Attributes</button>
                <button type="button" onclick="jumpToHttpSection('client')" class="px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-slate-800 hover:bg-emerald-600 text-slate-300 hover:text-white transition cursor-pointer">Client Settings</button>
                <button type="button" onclick="jumpToHttpSection('tls')" class="px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-slate-800 hover:bg-amber-600 text-slate-300 hover:text-white transition cursor-pointer">TLS & Proxy</button>
                <button type="button" onclick="jumpToHttpSection('payload')" class="px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-slate-800 hover:bg-purple-600 text-slate-300 hover:text-white transition cursor-pointer">Payloads & Vars</button>
                <button type="button" onclick="jumpToHttpSection('loops')" class="px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-slate-800 hover:bg-cyan-600 text-slate-300 hover:text-white transition cursor-pointer">Loops & Parallel</button>
                <button type="button" onclick="jumpToHttpSection('examples')" class="px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-slate-800 hover:bg-rose-600 text-slate-300 hover:text-white transition cursor-pointer">Examples</button>
            </div>
        </div>

        <!-- Scrollable Body -->
        <div id="http-docs-content" class="flex-1 overflow-y-auto custom-scrollbar bg-slate-950 p-4 rounded-lg border border-slate-800 text-xs text-slate-300 leading-relaxed space-y-4">
            <div id="http-docs-loading" class="flex items-center justify-center p-12 text-slate-400 space-x-2">
                <span class="animate-spin text-base">⏳</span>
                <span>Loading documentation...</span>
            </div>
            <div id="http-docs-body" class="hidden space-y-4"></div>
        </div>

        <!-- Footer -->
        <div class="flex items-center justify-between pt-2 border-t border-slate-800">
            <span class="text-[11px] text-slate-500">Click any snippet or button to insert or copy</span>
            <button type="button" onclick="closeHttpDocsModal()" class="px-4 py-1.5 text-xs font-semibold bg-slate-800 hover:bg-slate-700 text-slate-300 rounded-md transition cursor-pointer">Close</button>
        </div>
    </div>
</div>

docs.title: JavaScript Controller Logic
docs.text:
let httpDocsLoaded = false;
let httpDocsRawContent = '';

function openHttpDocsModal(preferredSection) {
    const modal = document.getElementById('http-docs-modal');
    if (!modal) return;
    modal.classList.remove('hidden');

    if (!httpDocsLoaded) {
        document.getElementById('http-docs-loading').classList.remove('hidden');
        document.getElementById('http-docs-body').classList.add('hidden');
        fetch('/api/docs/http-client')
            .then(res => {
                if (!res.ok) throw new Error('HTTP ' + res.status);
                return res.json();
            })
            .then(data => {
                httpDocsRawContent = data.content || '';
                const html = renderMarkdownToHtml(httpDocsRawContent);
                const body = document.getElementById('http-docs-body');
                body.innerHTML = html;
                document.getElementById('http-docs-loading').classList.add('hidden');
                body.classList.remove('hidden');
                httpDocsLoaded = true;
                if (preferredSection) setTimeout(() => jumpToHttpSection(preferredSection), 150);
            })
            .catch(err => {
                document.getElementById('http-docs-loading').innerHTML =
                    '<div class="text-rose-400 p-4 border border-rose-900/50 rounded bg-rose-950/20">Failed to load documentation: ' + escapeHtml(err.message) + '</div>';
            });
    } else {
        if (preferredSection) setTimeout(() => jumpToHttpSection(preferredSection), 50);
    }
}

function closeHttpDocsModal() {
    const modal = document.getElementById('http-docs-modal');
    if (modal) modal.classList.add('hidden');
}

function jumpToHttpSection(sec) {
    if (!sec) return;
    sec = sec.toLowerCase();
    const map = {
        'attributes': 'sec-2-complete-attribute-specification',
        'core': 'sec-2-1-core-request-variable-attributes',
        'headers': 'sec-2-1-core-request-variable-attributes',
        'client': 'sec-2-2-go-http-client-settings',
        'timeout': 'sec-2-2-go-http-client-settings',
        'tls': 'sec-2-3-go-http-transport-tls-tuning',
        'proxy': 'sec-2-3-go-http-transport-tls-tuning',
        'payload': 'sec-3-payload-resolution-variable-interpolation',
        'payloads': 'sec-3-payload-resolution-variable-interpolation',
        'vars': 'sec-3-payload-resolution-variable-interpolation',
        'loops': 'sec-4-control-flow-loop-integration',
        'parallel': 'sec-4-3-concurrent-requests-parallel',
        'examples': 'sec-5-comprehensive-pipeline-examples'
    };
    const targetId = map[sec] || ('sec-' + sec);
    const targetEl = document.getElementById(targetId);
    if (targetEl) {
        targetEl.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' });
        targetEl.classList.add('bg-blue-900/40', 'p-1', 'rounded', 'transition-colors');
        setTimeout(() => {
            targetEl.classList.remove('bg-blue-900/40', 'p-1', 'rounded', 'transition-colors');
        }, 2000);
    }
}

docs.title: The Escape Key Priority Rule
docs.text:
In builder/tmpl/index.html, ensure that pressing Escape closes the documentation modal without closing the parent node modal underneath:

document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
        const httpModal = document.getElementById('http-docs-modal');
        if (httpModal && !httpModal.classList.contains('hidden')) {
            closeHttpDocsModal();
            return;
        }
        const dbModal = document.getElementById('db-docs-modal');
        if (dbModal && !dbModal.classList.contains('hidden')) {
            closeDbDocsModal();
            return;
        }
        closeFileBrowser();
        closeNodeModal();
        closeComponentPicker();
        closeDatabaseModal();
    }
});

docs.title: Step 7: Synchronizing builder/html_content.go
docs.text: [!CAUTION] Zero Inconsistency Rule: builder/html_content.go contains const IndexHTML = + "<index.html>". It must remain identical to builder/tmpl/index.html so that the standalone binary works without disk files.

docs.title: Two Critical Pitfalls to Avoid:
docs.text:
1. No Raw Backticks Inside tmpl/index.html: In Go, raw string literals (`...`) cannot contain a backtick, even when escaped.
  2. ❌ Do not write: text.replace(/`([^`]+)`/g, ...)
  3. ❌ Do not write: if (line.startsWith('```'))

  4. ✅ Write instead: 

    const fence = String.fromCharCode(96, 96, 96);
const inlineCodeRegex = new RegExp('\\x60([^\\x60]+)\\x60', 'g');

  5. No Unescaped Go Template Actions {{...}}: Go's html/template.Parse parses any {{...}} sequence as a Go template variable or action.

  6. ❌ Do not write: '<span>Supports {{Variables}}</span>' (Go will error with function "Variables" not defined)
  7. ✅ Write instead: '<span>Supports {{Variables}}</span>'

docs.title: Safe Synchronization Command:
docs.text:
Use this PowerShell one-liner to synchronize builder/html_content.go:

powershell -Command "& { `$h = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllText('builder/tmpl/index.html'); `$bt = [char]96; `$content = 'package builder' + [Environment]::NewLine + [Environment]::NewLine + 'const IndexHTML = ' + `$bt + `$h + `$bt + [Environment]::NewLine; [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText('builder/html_content.go', `$content, [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8); Write-Host 'html_content.go successfully synchronized.' }"

docs.title: 3. The Form Autofill Pattern (⚡ Use Example)
docs.text:
One of the most useful features of Flow Builder modal guides is the ability to directly populate form inputs from code examples.

When markdown code blocks are parsed by renderMarkdownToHtml, any snippet containing a URL, connection string, or <http_client ...> XML node includes a ⚡ Use Example action button:

function useSnippetInInput(codeId) {
    const el = document.getElementById(codeId);
    if (!el) return;
    const text = (el.innerText || el.textContent || '').trim();

    // 1. If Database Modal is open
    const dbModal = document.getElementById('database-modal');
    if (dbModal && !dbModal.classList.contains('hidden')) {
        const connInput = document.getElementById('db-conn-str');
        if (connInput) {
            connInput.value = text;
            closeDbDocsModal();
            return;
        }
    }

    // 2. If Node Modal is open in Script Editor
    const nodeModal = document.getElementById('node-modal');
    if (nodeModal && !nodeModal.classList.contains('hidden')) {
        // Direct URL insertion
        if (text.startsWith('http://') || text.startsWith('https://')) {
            const urlInput = document.querySelector('#modal-fields-container input[name="attr_url"]');
            if (urlInput) {
                urlInput.value = text;
                closeHttpDocsModal();
                return;
            }
        }
        // Full <http_client ...> XML snippet extraction
        if (text.startsWith('<http_client') || text.includes('<http_client')) {
            const urlMatch = text.match(/url="([^"]+)"/);
            const methodMatch = text.match(/method="([^"]+)"/);
            if (urlMatch) {
                const u = document.querySelector('#modal-fields-container input[name="attr_url"]');
                if (u) u.value = urlMatch[1];
            }
            if (methodMatch) {
                const m = document.querySelector('#modal-fields-container select[name="attr_method"]');
                if (m) m.value = methodMatch[1];
            }
            closeHttpDocsModal();
            return;
        }
    }

    // 3. Fallback: Copy to system clipboard
    navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
}

docs.title: 4. Writing Automated Verification Tests
docs.text:
Add automated tests in builder/builder_test.go to guarantee that: 1. Unauthorized requests to the API are rejected (401 Unauthorized). 2. Authorized requests return the JSON content with expected keywords. 3. Both builder/tmpl/index.html and builder/html_content.go contain the required modal DOM elements and triggers.

func TestHttpClientDocAPI(t *testing.T) {
    tmpDir := t.TempDir()
    storage, err := NewStorage(filepath.Join(tmpDir, "test_http_docs.db"))
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatalf("failed to create storage: %v", err)
    }
    defer storage.Close()

    srv, err := NewServer(storage, 0)
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatalf("failed to create server: %v", err)
    }
    srv.authToken = "test-token"

    // 1. Unauthorized request returns 401
    unauthReq := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/api/docs/http-client", nil)
    unauthRec := httptest.NewRecorder()
    srv.Handler().ServeHTTP(unauthRec, unauthReq)
    if unauthRec.Code != http.StatusUnauthorized {
        t.Errorf("expected 401, got %d", unauthRec.Code)
    }

    // 2. Authorized request returns 200 with JSON payload
    authReq := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/api/docs/http-client?token=test-token", nil)
    authRec := httptest.NewRecorder()
    srv.Handler().ServeHTTP(authRec, authReq)
    if authRec.Code != http.StatusOK {
        t.Errorf("expected 200, got %d", authRec.Code)
    }

    var resp struct {
        Filename string `json:"filename"`
        Content  string `json:"content"`
    }
    json.Unmarshal(authRec.Body.Bytes(), &resp)
    if resp.Filename != "http_client.md" || len(resp.Content) == 0 {
        t.Errorf("invalid response payload: %+v", resp)
    }
}

func TestHttpClientDocUI(t *testing.T) {
    indexBytes, err := os.ReadFile("tmpl/index.html")
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatalf("failed to read index.html: %v", err)
    }
    tmplStr := string(indexBytes)

    required := []string{
        `id="http-docs-modal"`,
        `openHttpDocsModal`,
        `closeHttpDocsModal`,
        `updateNodeModalGuideButton`,
        `node-modal-guide-btn`,
        `📖 HTTP Client Guide`,
        `/api/docs/http-client`,
    }
    for _, snippet := range required {
        if !strings.Contains(tmplStr, snippet) {
            t.Errorf("expected tmpl/index.html to contain %q", snippet)
        }
        if !strings.Contains(IndexHTML, snippet) {
            t.Errorf("expected IndexHTML in html_content.go to contain %q", snippet)
        }
    }
}

docs.title: 5. Summary Checklist for Adding New Node Modals
docs.text:
When adding a tooltip or documentation modal to any other node, check off each step:

  • [ ] Catalog Metadata updated in builder/catalog.go (Description on fields for hover tooltips).
  • [ ] Markdown File created under docs/ and copied to builder/tmpl/docs_<name>.md.
  • [ ] Embed Directive updated in builder/templates.go.
  • [ ] HTTP Handler implemented and registered in builder/server.go under /api/docs/<topic>.
  • [ ] Trigger Buttons wired in renderModalFields and/or canvas_nodes.html.
  • [ ] Modal HTML & JS defined in builder/tmpl/index.html.
  • [ ] Escape Key Listener updated so Escape dismisses the documentation modal first.
  • [ ] No Raw Backticks (\x60) and No Unescaped {{...}} ({{...}}) in tmpl/index.html.
  • [ ] Synchronized builder/html_content.go with builder/tmpl/index.html.
  • [ ] Unit Tests added in builder/builder_test.go and passing: 
    go test -v -run "TestHttpClientDoc" ./builder/...
go test ./builder/...
go build -o flow.exe .

docs.title: Executing Flow Pipelines
docs.text:
Flow provides two public execution methods on Executor:

func (e *Executor) Execute(ctx context.Context, nodes []PipelineNode) ([]ScriptResult, error)
func (e *Executor) ExecuteRun(ctx context.Context, nodes []PipelineNode) (RunResult, error)

Both methods execute the same nodes through the same executor implementation. They honor the same context.Context, execute the same sequential, parallel, conditional, loop, transaction, and leaf-node behavior, and return a non-nil Go error when the pipeline fails or is canceled.

The difference is the returned result model.

docs.title: Choose an API
docs.text: Need Use Existing caller that reads script output or return codes Execute Flat results for a simple sequential pipeline Execute Run ID, overall run status, or start/finish timestamps ExecuteRun Structured failure diagnosis for nested, parallel, or looped nodes ExecuteRun Row-count reporting for SQL and bulk ETL ExecuteRun JSON events, tracing, metrics, or an audit trail ExecuteRun with an EventSink

docs.title: Execute: Flat Results
docs.text:
Execute returns a []ScriptResult. Each result describes a script or leaf operation in a flat list:

type ScriptResult struct {
    ScriptID      string
    ReturnCode    any
    ResultsString string
    Duration      string
}

Use it when application code needs the output from a step, such as a SQL query result saved to ResultsString, and does not need a complete execution graph.

executor := flow.NewExecutor(registry)

results, err := executor.Execute(context.Background(), config.FlowNodes)
if err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("pipeline failed: %w", err)
}

for _, result := range results {
    fmt.Printf(
        "step=%s code=%v duration=%s\n%s\n",
        result.ScriptID,
        result.ReturnCode,
        result.Duration,
        result.ResultsString,
    )
}

Execute is fully compatible with callers written before run-level observability was introduced. It still collects the same flat ScriptResult values and returns the same generic execution error on failure.

docs.title: Handling a Failure with Execute
docs.text:
When a pipeline fails, Execute returns the results accumulated before execution stopped plus a non-nil error:

results, err := executor.Execute(ctx, config.FlowNodes)
if err != nil {
    for _, result := range results {
        if result.ReturnCode != 0 {
            log.Printf("step %s failed: %v", result.ScriptID, result.ReturnCode)
        }
    }
    return err
}

This works well for a linear workflow, but it does not provide a run ID, parent/child links, typed error categories, or a stable way to distinguish repeated executions of the same node inside a loop.

docs.title: ExecuteRun: Structured Run Result
docs.text:
ExecuteRun returns one RunResult, including details for the entire execution and a NodeResult for every node that actually starts:

type RunResult struct {
    RunID        string
    StartedAt    time.Time
    FinishedAt   time.Time
    Status       flow.RunStatus
    ErrorClass   flow.ErrorClass
    ErrorMessage string
    Nodes        []flow.NodeResult
}

Use it for production execution hosts, job runners, monitoring services, and operational tools. The method returns a populated RunResult even when execution fails or the context is canceled.

executor := flow.NewExecutor(registry)

run, err := executor.ExecuteRun(context.Background(), config.FlowNodes)
log.Printf(
    "run=%s status=%s nodes=%d duration=%s",
    run.RunID,
    run.Status,
    len(run.Nodes),
    run.FinishedAt.Sub(run.StartedAt),
)

if err != nil {
    log.Printf(
        "run=%s class=%s error=%s",
        run.RunID,
        run.ErrorClass,
        run.ErrorMessage,
    )
    return err
}

docs.title: Inspect Failed Nodes
docs.text:
Each NodeResult has a unique ExecutionID, its configured XML NodeID when present, a readable NodePath, optional ParentExecutionID, status, attempts, error classification, and row counts.

run, err := executor.ExecuteRun(ctx, config.FlowNodes)
if err != nil {
    for _, node := range run.Nodes {
        if node.Status != flow.RunStatusFailed && node.Status != flow.RunStatusCanceled {
            continue
        }

        log.Printf(
            "run=%s execution=%s node=%s path=%s class=%s error=%s",
            run.RunID,
            node.ExecutionID,
            node.NodeID,
            node.NodePath,
            node.ErrorClass,
            node.ErrorMessage,
        )
    }
    return err
}

For a nested XML structure, NodePath gives a stable structural location and ParentExecutionID points to the enclosing group, branch, loop, or assertion handler. Use ExecutionID, not NodeID, as the identity in external systems: a loop can execute one XML node multiple times.

docs.title: Read ETL Counts
docs.text:
Where the operation can measure them, NodeResult.RowCounts reports:

  • Affected for SQL DML when the driver provides rows affected.
  • Read and Written for bulk SQL ETL.
run, err := executor.ExecuteRun(ctx, config.FlowNodes)
if err != nil {
    return err
}

for _, node := range run.Nodes {
    if node.NodeKind != "sql_bulk" {
        continue
    }
    log.Printf(
        "bulk node %s streamed read=%d written=%d",
        node.NodeID,
        node.RowCounts.Read,
        node.RowCounts.Written,
    )
}

An omitted count is not a confirmed zero; it means that operation does not currently expose that measurement.

docs.title: The Go Error Is Still Required
docs.text:
Do not replace the returned Go error with RunResult.Status. Use both:

run, err := executor.ExecuteRun(ctx, config.FlowNodes)
if err != nil {
    switch run.Status {
    case flow.RunStatusCanceled:
        return fmt.Errorf("run %s canceled: %w", run.RunID, err)
    case flow.RunStatusFailed:
        return fmt.Errorf("run %s failed (%s): %w", run.RunID, run.ErrorClass, err)
    default:
        return err
    }
}

The error controls the caller's success path. RunResult supplies the structured context needed for logs, retries, alerting, or incident investigation.

docs.title: Add Events Without Changing Execution Semantics
docs.text:
Both APIs emit events when an event sink is configured, because both delegate to the same execution core. The sink does not change which method should be chosen; choose the API based on the return value your caller needs.

executor := flow.NewExecutor(registry)
executor.SetEventSink(&flow.JSONLineSink{Writer: os.Stdout})

// Legacy caller: events are emitted, but the returned value is still []ScriptResult.
results, err := executor.Execute(ctx, config.FlowNodes)

// Observability-aware caller: the same events are emitted and the returned value is RunResult.
run, err := executor.ExecuteRun(ctx, config.FlowNodes)

Do not call both methods for the same work. Each call starts a new pipeline run with a new run ID and executes the nodes again. Use ExecuteRun as the single call when a caller needs both execution and run-level observability.

See development_observability_usage.md for JSON Lines, multiple sinks, and custom sink examples.

docs.title: Observability Usage Guide
docs.text: Flow can return a structured record for each pipeline run and emit lifecycle events while work is executing. Use ExecuteRun when your application needs run status, node relationships, failures, or row counts. Continue using Execute when the existing []ScriptResult result is sufficient.

docs.title: Run a Pipeline and Inspect Its Result
docs.text:
ExecuteRun returns a RunResult whether the run succeeds, fails, or is canceled. The Go error remains the signal for control flow; inspect the result for the run ID, classification, and individual node outcomes.

ctx := context.Background()
executor := flow.NewExecutor(registry)

run, err := executor.ExecuteRun(ctx, config.FlowNodes)
if err != nil {
    log.Printf("run %s finished with %s: %s", run.RunID, run.ErrorClass, run.ErrorMessage)
}

log.Printf(
    "run=%s status=%s started=%s finished=%s nodes=%d",
    run.RunID,
    run.Status,
    run.StartedAt.Format(time.RFC3339),
    run.FinishedAt.Format(time.RFC3339),
    len(run.Nodes),
)

for _, node := range run.Nodes {
    log.Printf(
        "node=%s id=%s status=%s path=%s parent=%s error_class=%s error=%s",
        node.ExecutionID,
        node.NodeID,
        node.Status,
        node.NodePath,
        node.ParentExecutionID,
        node.ErrorClass,
        node.ErrorMessage,
    )
}

The run status is one of:

  • flow.RunStatusSucceeded: every executed node completed successfully.
  • flow.RunStatusFailed: a node failed and the executor stopped the pipeline.
  • flow.RunStatusCanceled: the context was canceled or reached its deadline.

Each NodeResult currently has exactly one AttemptResult. The attempts collection is present so retry support can add future attempts without changing the result format.

docs.title: Configure SetEventSink
docs.text:
Call SetEventSink before Execute or ExecuteRun to register one destination for structured lifecycle events:

executor := flow.NewExecutor(registry)
executor.SetEventSink(sink)

run, err := executor.ExecuteRun(ctx, config.FlowNodes)

The sink receives run.started before node work begins and run.finished after the executor has finalized the RunResult. Each executed node also emits node.started, attempt.started, attempt.finished, and node.finished events. Sinks do not require any XML configuration.

SetEventSink replaces every previously registered sink. Pass nil to disable event emission for later runs:

executor.SetEventSink(&flow.JSONLineSink{Writer: os.Stdout})
_, _ = executor.ExecuteRun(ctx, config.FlowNodes)

executor.SetEventSink(nil)
_, _ = executor.ExecuteRun(ctx, config.FlowNodes) // Does not emit events.

For more than one destination, use SetEventSinks rather than calling SetEventSink repeatedly:

executor.SetEventSinks(
    &flow.JSONLineSink{Writer: os.Stdout},
    auditSink,
)

docs.title: Print Failed Nodes Only
docs.text:
This sink sends a compact message to the standard logger only when an executed node fails or is canceled:

type FailureLogSink struct{}

func (FailureLogSink) Emit(_ context.Context, event flow.ExecutionEvent) error {
    if event.Type != flow.EventNodeFinished || event.Status == flow.RunStatusSucceeded {
        return nil
    }

    log.Printf(
        "run=%s node=%s id=%s status=%s class=%s error=%s",
        event.RunID,
        event.ExecutionID,
        event.NodeID,
        event.Status,
        event.ErrorClass,
        event.ErrorMessage,
    )
    return nil
}

executor.SetEventSink(FailureLogSink{})

docs.title: Capture Events in a Test
docs.text:
Custom sinks may be invoked by concurrent pipeline branches. Protect mutable in-memory state with a mutex when collecting events:

type MemorySink struct {
    mu     sync.Mutex
    events []flow.ExecutionEvent
}

func (s *MemorySink) Emit(_ context.Context, event flow.ExecutionEvent) error {
    s.mu.Lock()
    defer s.mu.Unlock()
    s.events = append(s.events, event)
    return nil
}

func (s *MemorySink) Events() []flow.ExecutionEvent {
    s.mu.Lock()
    defer s.mu.Unlock()
    return append([]flow.ExecutionEvent(nil), s.events...)
}

sink := &MemorySink{}
executor.SetEventSink(sink)

_, err := executor.ExecuteRun(context.Background(), config.FlowNodes)
if err != nil {
    t.Fatal(err)
}

events := sink.Events()
if events[0].Type != flow.EventRunStarted {
    t.Fatalf("first event = %s, want %s", events[0].Type, flow.EventRunStarted)
}

An error returned from Emit is intentionally ignored by the executor. This prevents a logging, tracing, or metrics outage from changing pipeline execution. A sink that requires reliable delivery should buffer or persist work internally and report its own health separately.

docs.title: Write JSON Lines Events
docs.text:
JSONLineSink writes one ExecutionEvent as a JSON object followed by a newline. This format works with common log collectors and makes it easy to filter by run_id, node_kind, status, or error_class.

logFile, err := os.OpenFile("flow-events.jsonl", os.O_APPEND|os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY, 0o644)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
defer logFile.Close()

executor := flow.NewExecutor(registry)
executor.SetEventSink(&flow.JSONLineSink{Writer: logFile})

run, err := executor.ExecuteRun(ctx, config.FlowNodes)
if err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("flow run %s failed: %w", run.RunID, err)
}

To write events to standard output, use os.Stdout as the writer:

executor.SetEventSink(&flow.JSONLineSink{Writer: os.Stdout})

docs.title: Control Event Output Format
docs.text:
SetEventSink selects the component that receives events. With JSONLineSink, the output format is fixed: one JSON-encoded ExecutionEvent per line. Writer controls the destination, such as a file, standard output, or a network-backed writer; it does not alter the JSON field selection or indentation.

To change the output format, implement flow.EventSink and register it with SetEventSink.

docs.title: Compact Text Output
docs.text:
Use a custom sink to produce human-readable lines rather than JSON:

type TextSink struct {
    Writer io.Writer
}

func (s TextSink) Emit(_ context.Context, event flow.ExecutionEvent) error {
    _, err := fmt.Fprintf(
        s.Writer,
        "%s run=%s type=%s node=%s status=%s error=%s\n",
        event.OccurredAt.Format(time.RFC3339),
        event.RunID,
        event.Type,
        event.NodeID,
        event.Status,
        event.ErrorMessage,
    )
    return err
}

executor.SetEventSink(TextSink{Writer: os.Stdout})

docs.title: Indented JSON Output
docs.text:
For formatted JSON, marshal each event with json.MarshalIndent. The mutex prevents parallel branches from interleaving writes:

type PrettyJSONSink struct {
    Writer io.Writer
    mu     sync.Mutex
}

func (s *PrettyJSONSink) Emit(_ context.Context, event flow.ExecutionEvent) error {
    s.mu.Lock()
    defer s.mu.Unlock()

    data, err := json.MarshalIndent(event, "", "  ")
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    _, err = fmt.Fprintln(s.Writer, string(data))
    return err
}

executor.SetEventSink(&PrettyJSONSink{Writer: os.Stdout})

docs.title: Reduced Audit JSON
docs.text:
Map ExecutionEvent to an application-specific structure when downstream systems should receive only selected fields. This is also the appropriate place to add application metadata, as long as it does not contain sensitive values.

type AuditEvent struct {
    Time   time.Time      `json:"time"`
    RunID  string         `json:"run_id"`
    Event  flow.EventType `json:"event"`
    NodeID string         `json:"node_id,omitempty"`
    Status flow.RunStatus `json:"status,omitempty"`
    Error  string         `json:"error,omitempty"`
}

type AuditSink struct {
    Writer io.Writer
    mu     sync.Mutex
}

func (s *AuditSink) Emit(_ context.Context, event flow.ExecutionEvent) error {
    audit := AuditEvent{
        Time:   event.OccurredAt,
        RunID:  event.RunID,
        Event:  event.Type,
        NodeID: event.NodeID,
        Status: event.Status,
        Error:  event.ErrorMessage,
    }

    s.mu.Lock()
    defer s.mu.Unlock()
    return json.NewEncoder(s.Writer).Encode(audit)
}

executor.SetEventSink(&AuditSink{Writer: os.Stdout})

Use SetEventSinks to retain the built-in JSON Lines output while emitting a second representation:

executor.SetEventSinks(
    &flow.JSONLineSink{Writer: jsonLogFile},
    TextSink{Writer: os.Stdout},
)

A typical event resembles this:

{
  "sequence": 6,
  "type": "node.finished",
  "occurred_at": "2026-09-03T12:00:01Z",
  "run_id": "4b7e3b2a5d4f...",
  "execution_id": "c0a8c3f6452e...",
  "parent_execution_id": "7683f0a2a9bd...",
  "node_id": "load_customers",
  "node_kind": "sql_bulk",
  "node_path": "group[0]/sql_bulk[0]",
  "attempt": 1,
  "status": "succeeded",
  "row_counts": {"read": 50000, "written": 50000}
}

Events are emitted in this lifecycle order for a run and each node:

  1. run.started
  2. node.started
  3. attempt.started
  4. attempt.finished
  5. node.finished
  6. run.finished

The sequence field increases for each event within a run. Parallel branches may complete in different wall-clock order, but the sequence provides a single ordering for a consumer.

docs.title: Use Multiple Sinks
docs.text:
Register more than one destination with SetEventSinks:

executor.SetEventSinks(
    &flow.JSONLineSink{Writer: os.Stdout},
    auditSink,
)

Calling SetEventSink or SetEventSinks replaces the previous sink configuration. Sinks are called for every event in registration order. A sink error is ignored so an unavailable telemetry destination cannot change pipeline execution; applications that need delivery guarantees should make the sink durable and monitor the sink independently.

docs.title: Implement a Custom Sink
docs.text:
Implement EventSink to forward events to a logging, tracing, or metrics system. An event sink can be called concurrently by parallel pipeline branches, so protect mutable state with a mutex, channel, or a concurrency-safe client.

type MetricsSink struct {
    mu      sync.Mutex
    finished map[flow.RunStatus]int64
}

func (s *MetricsSink) Emit(_ context.Context, event flow.ExecutionEvent) error {
    if event.Type != flow.EventNodeFinished {
        return nil
    }

    s.mu.Lock()
    defer s.mu.Unlock()
    s.finished[event.Status]++
    return nil
}

Use the same pattern to create an OpenTelemetry bridge: start a span on node.started, key it by ExecutionID, use ParentExecutionID to find its parent span, attach non-sensitive fields such as NodeKind, Status, and ErrorClass, then end it on node.finished. The base flow package deliberately has no OpenTelemetry or metrics backend dependency.

docs.title: Navigate Nested Results
docs.text:
RunResult.Nodes is a flat collection because it remains easy to serialize and query. Reconstruct the execution tree by matching ParentExecutionID to ExecutionID.

NodePath is a readable structural address. For example, group[0]/parallel[1]/script[0] describes a script beneath a parallel block inside a group. NodeID is the XML id when configured, while ExecutionID uniquely identifies a specific execution. Use ExecutionID rather than NodeID for loops and parallel work, where the same configured node can execute more than once.

docs.title: Interpret Row Counts and Errors
docs.text:
RowCounts contains only measurements known to the executed node:

  • SQL DML exposes Affected when the driver returns rows affected.
  • Bulk SQL ETL (<sql_bulk>) exposes Read and Written from the number of streamed rows.
  • Key-Value operations (<kv>) expose Affected for writes and deletions (put, set, delete, del), and Read for lookups and prefix scans (get, scan, list).
  • Key-Value bulk transfers (<kv_bulk>) expose Read and Written from the number of streamed records transferred from SQL to the KV store.
  • Excel reads and writes expose Read and Written row metrics.
  • Other nodes currently leave row counts empty.

An omitted count means the executor did not measure that value. Do not treat it as a confirmed zero.

ErrorClass is designed for filtering and alert routing. Current values include canceled, validation, database, http, filesystem, script, template, data_format, and unknown. Preserve the Go error returned by ExecuteRun for detailed handling; the classified fields are a summary rather than a replacement.

Events do not include SQL text, request/response bodies, headers, or pipeline variables. Common credential fragments in recorded error messages, such as password=... and token=..., are redacted. Applications should still avoid placing sensitive values in custom event fields or logs.

docs.title: Keep Existing Callers Unchanged
docs.text:
The original API remains available and keeps its existing behavior:

results, err := executor.Execute(ctx, config.FlowNodes)

Adopt ExecuteRun where structured observability is needed. No XML changes are required for either API.

docs.title: Flow Builder Theme Customization Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how the Flow Builder theming system works and provides step-by-step instructions for adding new themes.

docs.title: 1. Theme Engine Architecture
docs.text:
Flow Builder's theme engine operates via client-side DOM manipulation and CSS styling:

  1. Root Attribute: The theme is set on the root <html> element using the data-theme attribute (e.g. <html data-theme="soft-white">).
  2. Persistence: The chosen theme is automatically persisted in browser localStorage under the key flow_builder_theme. When the page loads, loadSavedTheme() retrieves and applies the stored theme immediately.
  3. Template Synchronization: Flow Builder uses two synchronized files for its UI markup:
  4. builder/html_content.go: Contains the compiled Go constant string IndexHTML.
  5. builder/tmpl/index.html: Contains the raw template counterpart. (Any theme added to one must also be added to the other to ensure consistency across build configurations and tests).

docs.title: 2. Built-In Themes
docs.text:
Flow Builder includes a broad range of themes to accommodate different environments and preferences:

Theme Key Name Type Notes slate Slate (Default) Dark Default deep slate palette (#020617 / #0f172a) midnight Midnight Blue Dark Deep navy with soft blue highlights nord Nord Frost Dark Arctic ice-blue Nordic palette emerald Emerald Matrix Dark High-tech emerald and mint palette amber Warm Amber Dark Low-fatigue golden amber tones cyberpunk Cyberpunk Neon Dark High-contrast neon cyan and magenta accents vscode-dark-plus VS Code Dark+ Dark Classic VS Code dark UI theme vscode-light-plus VS Code Light+ Light Classic VS Code light UI theme vscode-monokai VS Code Monokai Dark Monokai code palette with warm accents vscode-dracula VS Code Dracula Dark Gothic purple and vibrant pastel accents visual-studio-dark Visual Studio Dark Dark Visual Studio IDE charcoal palette visual-studio-light Visual Studio Light Light Classic Visual Studio light gray/blue palette visual-studio-blue Visual Studio Blue Custom Iconic Visual Studio blue IDE theme soft-white Soft White (Blue & Black) Light Gentle soft white background with deep black typography and vibrant blue accents light Clean Light Light Inverted high-contrast light theme

docs.title: 3. Theme Implementation Approaches
docs.text: There are two approaches to theming in Flow Builder:

docs.title: Approach A: CSS Filter / Variable Theming (Quick)
docs.text:
Useful for subtle tone shifts or dark variants where the default dark structure remains intact: 

html[data-theme="nord"] {
    filter: hue-rotate(190deg) brightness(0.95) saturate(1.1);
}

docs.title: Approach B: Explicit Tailwind Utility Overrides (Recommended for True Themes)
docs.text: Required for light themes (such as Soft White) or distinct custom color schemes (such as Visual Studio Blue). This explicitly overrides Tailwind classes used across the studio: - .bg-slate-950: Canvas background, deep containers, inputs, terminal blocks. - .bg-slate-900: Sidebars, header, modals, section containers. - .node-card: Leaf steps and container cards on the canvas. - .bg-slate-800, .bg-slate-700: Buttons, subtle tags, inactive tab pills. - .border-slate-800, .border-slate-700: Structural borders and divider lines. - .text-slate-100, .text-slate-200, .text-white: Primary text, titles, headings. - .text-slate-400, .text-slate-500: Secondary text, metadata, descriptions. - .text-cyan-400, .text-blue-400: Accents, step tags, highlights, links. - .bg-blue-600: Primary action buttons and active tabs.

docs.title: Step 1: Add Theme Root Declaration
docs.text:
In <style> in both builder/html_content.go and builder/tmpl/index.html: 

html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] {
    --bg-body: #f8fafc;
    filter: none;
}

docs.title: Step 2: Add CSS Overrides
docs.text:
Target the core layout classes for your theme: 

/* Custom Theme: Soft White with Blue & Black */
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"],
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] body {
    background-color: #f8fafc !important;
    color: #0f172a !important;
}
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] .bg-slate-950 {
    background-color: #f8fafc !important;
}
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] .bg-slate-900,
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] header,
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] aside {
    background-color: #ffffff !important;
}
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] .node-card,
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] .component-card {
    background-color: #ffffff !important;
}
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] .component-card:hover,
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] .node-card:hover {
    background-color: #f8fafc !important;
    border-color: #2563eb !important;
}
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] .border-slate-800,
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] .border-slate-700 {
    border-color: #cbd5e1 !important;
}
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] .text-slate-100,
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] .text-slate-200,
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] .text-white {
    color: #0f172a !important;
}
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] .text-slate-400,
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] .text-slate-500 {
    color: #334155 !important;
}
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] .text-cyan-400,
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] .text-blue-400 {
    color: #1d4ed8 !important;
}
html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"] .bg-blue-600 {
    background-color: #1d4ed8 !important;
    color: #ffffff !important;
}

docs.title: Step 3: Add the Option to the Theme Selector
docs.text:
Add your <option> inside <select id="theme-selector"> in both files: 

<option value="my-custom-theme" class="bg-slate-900 text-slate-200">My Custom Theme</option>

docs.title: Step 4: Add Automated Unit Tests
docs.text:
Add assertions in builder/builder_test.go to ensure that templates and the live HTTP handler contain the new theme: 

func TestMyCustomTheme(t *testing.T) {
    requiredSnippets := []string{
        `html[data-theme="my-custom-theme"]`,
        `<option value="my-custom-theme"`,
        `My Custom Theme`,
    }
    // verify tmpl/index.html, IndexHTML, and http GET "/"
}

docs.title: Step 5: Verify
docs.text:
Run the test suite: 

go test ./builder -v

docs.title: 5. Reference: The Soft White Theme
docs.text:
The Soft White (Blue & Black) theme (soft-white) serves as a prime reference implementation:

  • Canvas Background: #f8fafc (Slate 50 soft white).
  • Cards & Surfaces: #ffffff (Clean white) with #cbd5e1 crisp borders.
  • Primary Typography: Deep black (#0f172a) and dark slate (#334155).
  • Primary Accents & Actions: Royal blue (#1d4ed8 / #2563eb).
  • Inputs & Terminal: Pure white backgrounds with dark black text and blue focus rings.
